papers.abstract_full: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the most common birth defect, with the genetic defects remaining unknown in many patients. NR2F2 is a transcription factor that regulates cardiac endocardial development in a dosage-sensitive manner; however, the association between non-coding NR2F2 variants and CHD risk remains unclear. In this study, we performed a case-control analysis of the NR2F2 promoter, and identified four rare variants in isolated CHD patients with a frequency over 3% but undetected in controls. Histone modification analysis showed that two of the candidate variants, g.96330105C > T and g.96330128C > T, overlapped with active promoter-associated histone marks. Functionally, these two variants significantly reduced NR2F2 promoter transcriptional activity and protein expression. In addition, the variant g.96330128C > T abrogated ETS1 binding, thereby impairing ETS1-mediated positive transcriptional regulation of NR2F2. These findings highlight that loss-of-function (LOF) variants in the NR2F2 promoter, particularly g.96330128C > T, confer CHD susceptibility by reducing NR2F2 expression.

Yet for many, particularly those with complex lesions, childhood intervention does not equate to a cure. papers.abstract_full: Survival into adulthood is now the norm for individuals born with congenital heart disease, with over 90% of children reaching adult life. Yet for many, particularly those with complex lesions, childhood intervention does not equate to a cure. Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) face ongoing risks of haemodynamic complications, end-organ dysfunction, and premature morbidity. In this review, we present recent advances in ACHD care across five domains: lifelong care models, diagnostic techniques, management strategies, genetic and precision medicine, and machine learning. We highlight the pivotal role of specialized, multidisciplinary care in improving outcomes, and the need for structured transition programmes to ensure continuity from paediatric to adult services. Emerging priorities include reproductive counselling, exercise prescription, and psychosocial support. Advances in cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging, electrophysiological mapping, and four-dimensional flow imaging now offer unprecedented anatomical and haemodynamic insights. Recent trials have demonstrated encouraging results for novel heart failure therapies and pulmonary vasodilators in lesion-specific subgroups, while transcatheter technologies continue to expand therapeutic options for patients with complex anatomy. Genetic testing and machine learning are beginning to reshape risk stratification and workflow efficiency, though challenges remain in their implementation. As this population ages and acquires new comorbidities, care models must evolve to move beyond just survival, but towards improving quality of life, preserving organ function, and anticipating future needs. This review aims to support clinicians and researchers in meeting these challenges and advancing the next era of ACHD care.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmia (MVA) and end-stage heart failure (ESHF) in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) may vary by genotype. Comparative analyses remain limited. The aim of this study was to compare clinical outcomes and risk predictors across genotypes. METHODS AND RESULTS: Carriers of pathogenic variants in DCM-associated genes were identified from a dedicated database. Clinically affected variant-carriers from the five most prevalent genotypes were compared with genotype-negative patients. A composite primary endpoint consisted of MVA or ESHF. Secondary endpoints were MVA and ESHF individually. Incidence rates and baseline variables associated with outcomes were evaluated.Among 484 patients, 57 (11.8%) met the primary endpoint after 5 years. Genotype-negative patients had the lowest primary endpoint incidence rates [1.4 (0.7-2.1) per 100 person-years], whereas LMNA had the highest [6.2 (3.0-9.5)]. With a genotype-negative reference, incidence rate ratios were 1.3 for TTN, 1.7 for FLNC, 2.0 for DSP, 2.7 for RBM20 and 4.4 for LMNA. Rates were higher in LMNA and RBM20 than genotype-negative patients (P < .001 and P = .003, respectively) and higher in LMNA than TTN (P = .001). Results were similar for MVA. LMNA had higher ESHF rates than genotype-negative, TTN and DSP.Left ventricular diastolic diameter, LMNA variants and late gadolinium enhancement were independently associated with the primary endpoint. Baseline predictors varied by genotype. CONCLUSION: Genotype stratification in DCM reveals a risk hierarchy with risk lowest in genotype-negative and TTN patients, two-fold higher in DSP and FLNC, and three- and four-fold higher in RBM20 and LMNA, respectively. Accounting for genotype improves risk prediction.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: Delivery >39 weeks' gestation is recommended for fetuses with congenital heart disease (FCHD). However, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), maternal diabetes and fetal growth restriction (FGR) are more common in these pregnancies and often necessitate early delivery. We evaluated indications for delivery at <39 weeks and examined maternal covariates, cardiac diagnoses and placental pathology. STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective observational study included maternal-fetal dyads with prenatally diagnosed, structurally isolated, genetically unremarkable FCHD delivered at a single center. Gestational age and delivery indication were obtained from medical record. Placental pathology was assessed using Amsterdam criteria. Regression models evaluated associations with gestational age and neonatal mortality. RESULTS: 46.3% (99/214) delivered <39 weeks; 65.6% (65/99) were due to maternal or fetal compromise, and 34.3% (33/99) to obstetric indications. HDP (20.1%) was strongly associated with <39-week delivery (32.3% vs 9.6%, p<0.001) and the greatest reduction in gestational age (-2.31 weeks, p<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified preeclampsia, type 2 diabetes, lower birthweight Z-score, and race as independent predictors of earlier delivery (p<0.05). Neonatal mortality was higher with maternal/fetal indications (15.7%) versus obstetric (5.4%) or elective FCHD delivery (5.6%) (p=0.02). CONCLUSION: Nearly half of FCHD infants delivered before 39 weeks, largely due to maternal and placental disease, underscoring the importance of placental health in this population.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: To explore the clinical information and genetic characteristics of a child with Genitopatellar syndrome (GPS) and summarize relevant findings through a literature review. METHODS: A child with GPS diagnosed at the Department of Neonatology of Taizhou Hospital in Zhejiang Province in February 2024 was selected as study subject. Clinical data were collected, and trio Whole-exome sequencing (trio-WES) was carried out. Based on guidelines from the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG), the pathogenicity of candidate variant was assessed. Amino acid conservation was analyzed using MEGA, and three-dimensional structures of the wild-type and mutant proteins were predicted and compared using AlphaFold3 and PyMOL. A retrospective analysis was also conducted by searching the PubMed, Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) databases for case reports or studies of genetically confirmed GPS. This study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of the hospital (Ethics No.: L2024-10-06-01). RESULTS: The patient, a one-day-old male, had presented with genital abnormalities, clubfoot, polycystic kidneys, atrial septal defect, and agenesis of corpus callosum. Increased nuchal translucency and cervical lymphatic hygroma were detected during the first trimester of pregnancy. Trio-WES results revealed that he has harbored a de novo heterozygous c.3696del (p.Glu1233LysfsTer10) frameshift variant in exon 18 of the KAT6B gene (NM_012330.4). The variant was previously unreported, and its frequency in the general East Asian population has not been documented. Based on the ACMG guidelines, the variant was classified as likely pathogenic (evidence criteria including PS, PM, and PP). Protein homologous sequence alignment analysis suggested the variant site to be highly conserved across multiple species. Homology modeling and structural comparison further revealed varying degrees of change in the hydrogen bonding of amino acids adjacent to the variant site and in the two- and three-dimensional structures of the protein. Literature review has identified 19 patients, with the study cohort comprising 16 survivors (10 males, 6 females) and 3 non-survivors (1 male, 2 females). All patients exhibited varying degrees of genital anomalies, facial dysmorphism, corpus callosum dysgenesis, and flexion contractures of the hips and knees (19/19, 100.0%). Developmental delay/intellectual disability was observed in 17 patients (17/19, 89.5%), hydronephrosis/multiple renal cysts in 16 patients (16/19, 84.2%), patellar hypoplasia in 15 patients (15/19, 78.9%), congenital heart disease in 13 patients (13/19, 68.4%), and prenatal abnormalities were detected in 8 patients (8/19, 42.1%). Current management of the disease is primarily supportive and symptomatic, with the most effective measures including oxygen therapy, gastrostomy tube feeding support, and joint corrective surgeries. CONCLUSION: The c.3696del (p.Glu1233LysfsTer10) variant of the KAT6B gene probably underlay the pathogenesis of GPS in this child. Above finding has expanded the genotypic and phenotypic spectra of this syndrome. GPS may present with increased nuchal translucency accompanied by cystic hygroma during the first trimester. Additionally, the literature review in this study has systematically summarized the prenatal and postnatal phenotypic features, poor prognosis, and current clinical interventions for GPS, which may provide more robust evidence-based support for clinical diagnosis, treatment strategy selection, and prognostic evaluation.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Chromosome 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) is a common multisystem genomic disorder with marked phenotypic variability and diagnostic delay. Data on diagnostic pathways and specialist involvement in Eastern Europe remain limited. We aimed to characterize diagnostic pathways and clinical triggers, assess specialist involvement and follow-up, and identify factors associated with diagnosis before or after 1 year of age in a Ukrainian cohort. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter observational study of patients with 22q11.2DS registered in the Ukrainian National Registry of Primary Immunodeficiencies. Clinical manifestations, diagnostic triggers, specialists involved in diagnosis and follow-up, immunological findings, and age at diagnosis were analyzed. RESULTS: The cohort included 126 patients, with a median age of 12 years (range, 0.1-39 years) and median age at diagnosis of 1.0 year (range, 0.1-18 years). Among 120 patients with available diagnostic timing, 63 (52.5%) were diagnosed within the first year, including the two antenatal cases. Congenital heart disease (CHD) was the most frequent major manifestation (74/89, 83.1%), followed by craniofacial dysmorphism (62/74, 83.8%), thymic hypoplasia (54/65, 83.1%), developmental delay (46/62, 74.2%), and recurrent infections (44/65, 67.7%). Among 83 patients with documented diagnostic triggers, CHD was the most frequent (61/83, 73.5%). Developmental delay was more frequent among patients diagnosed after 1 year than within the first year (22.9% vs. 4.4%, p = 0.0135). Immunodeficiency was a diagnostic trigger in 10/83 patients (12.0%), despite T-cell lymphopenia in 31/59 (52.5%). Immunologists and geneticists were most frequently involved in diagnosis. Cardiothoracic surgeons and cardiologists were more frequently involved among patients diagnosed within the first year than after 1 year (27.9% vs. 9.1%, p = 0.0411). Among 13 patients diagnosed after implementation of TREC/KREC newborn screening, two were identified following an abnormal screening result. CONCLUSIONS: In this Ukrainian cohort, 22q11.2DS diagnosis was predominantly phenotype-driven, with CHD representing the principal diagnostic trigger. Developmental delay was associated with diagnosis after 1 year, whereas immunological abnormalities relatively infrequently initiated diagnostic evaluation. Broader recognition of non-cardiac presentations, standardized referral criteria, coordinated multidisciplinary care, and continued development of newborn and prenatal screening may improve timely diagnosis of 22q11.2DS in Ukraine.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: Adults with childhood-onset conditions are increasingly admitted to children's hospitals, yet many pediatric systems lack the infrastructure and expertise to manage adult-related medical needs. One approach to bridge this gap is the use of an adult medicine consult service. We aim to describe the demographics, clinical complexity, and consultation patterns of patients admitted to a freestanding children's hospital and evaluated by an adult medicine consult service, which is a current gap in the literature. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective descriptive cohort study was performed of admitted patients with a Hospital Medicine Adult Care (HMAC) service consult from July 2014 through June 2023. RESULTS: Annual adult admissions increased over the study period, from 7.4% to 10.2% of all admissions. HMAC consulted on 1666 admissions for 1008 unique patients (median age, 27 years [range, 14-71 years]). The most frequent reasons for consult were venous thromboembolism prophylaxis (33.7%), age older than 25 years (21.2%), transition of care (7.6%), and hypertension (7.6%). HMAC physicians addressed a mean of 5.5 diagnoses per encounter. Patients averaged 3.6 admissions (range, 1-22) and 4.9 comorbidities (range, 0-21) each. The most common comorbidities were technology dependence (47%), solid tumor malignancy (22.5%), genetic conditions (20.2%), epilepsy (19.7%), congenital heart disease (17.4%), and cerebral palsy (15.7%). CONCLUSIONS: Adult consult services in children's hospitals support a medically complex population with diverse childhood-onset and adult conditions and function as longitudinal clinical partners. These findings support the role of adult medicine expertise in children's hospitals to help recognize and manage adult-specific care needs and transitions.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), a major contributor to heart failure (HF), is characterized by ventricular dilation, impaired systolic and diastolic function, arrhythmias, and adverse cardiac remodeling. While genetic causes of DCM have been extensively investigated, non-genetic and acquired forms of DCM-like HF remain less well understood, particularly regarding regulation by non-coding RNAs. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are stable, covalently closed RNAs that regulate cellular processes through interactions with microRNAs, RNA-binding proteins, and translational machinery; however, their role in non-genetic DCM-like HF is largely unexplored. METHODS: We developed K9HeartCircDB ( https://www.k9heartcircdb.com/ ), a publicly accessible database of circRNAs identified in canine left ventricular (LV) tissues. The dataset includes samples from tachypacing-induced HF, a model of non-genetic DCM-like disease, and healthy controls. CircRNAs were annotated and integrated into a user-friendly platform that enables queries based on exon composition, predicted microRNA binding sites, protein-coding potential, siRNA targets, and primer design for validation. RESULTS: K9HeartCircDB provides a comprehensive catalog of circRNAs expressed in canine LV tissues under both HF and control conditions. The platform offers multiple analytical features, including circRNA annotation, predicted regulatory interactions, and experimental design support. Comparative exploration of circRNA profiles between tachypacing-induced HF and normal tissues enables identification of candidate molecules associated with non-genetic DCM-like pathology. CONCLUSIONS: K9HeartCircDB represents an integrated and accessible resource for studying circRNA biology in canine HF. By facilitating exploration of circRNA expression and function in a translationally relevant large-animal model, this database supports mechanistic investigations and advances research into non-genetic DCM-like disease.

papers.abstract_full: ABSTRACT  Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and ischemic heart disease (IHD) are leading causes of heart failure, yet isoform-level changes in the failing heart remain poorly defined because reference annotations are derived largely from healthy tissues and short-read sequencing cannot reliably reconstruct full-length transcripts. We sequenced six human left ventricles (non-failing, DCM, and IHD; n = 2 each) with PacBio HiFi long reads and curated 48,232 isoforms across 11,760 genes, including 15,535 novel NIC and NNC isoforms. Independent evidence supported most novel structures: 81.7% of isoforms with novel splice junctions had short-read support for all novel junctions, and a cardiac CAGE atlas supported the 5′ ends of 93% of NIC and 86% of NNC isoforms. Novel isoform diversification was concentrated in sarcomere genes and persisted after accounting for gene complexity, expression, sequencing depth, and transcript length. We then augmented GENCODE v43 with 18,637 non-FSM long-read isoforms and re-quantified two independent short-read cohorts (MAGNet and GSE116250). For most genes carrying a transcript that changed more than 2-fold in DCM, the gene itself changed less than 2-fold, so these changes are not apparent at the gene level. Of 626 transcripts differentially expressed in both cohorts, 98% changed in the same direction, including all 100 long-read isoforms among them. papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Cardiospondylocarpofacial syndrome is a rare genetic disorder associated with multisystem anomalies and fetal growth restriction. Prenatal diagnosis is uncommon, with only 1 case reported to date. This case report aims to add to the prenatal as well as postnatal phenotypic features of cardiospondylocarpofacialsyndrome and highlight characteristics that may facilitate earlier recognition and diagnosis. CASE PRESENTATION: This is a case of a 29-year-old woman and her 6 pregnancies with 2 live births. Prenatal diagnostic testing in 1 of her pregnancies identified a pathogenic variant in the mitogen-activated protein kinase 7 gene. This finding subsequently enabled the identification of the same pathogenic variant in the mother. We present the clinical manifestations of the multiple comorbidities of the patient as well as the ultrasound findings of the fetuses with mitogen-activated protein kinase 7 mutation and their neonatal outcomes. Prenatal evaluation of the fetuses revealed fetal growth restriction, craniosynostosis, hypospadias sine hypospadia, and congenital heart defects. The mother suffered from arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy with left ventricular damage, chronic kidney disease because of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis after tuberculosis of the kidneys and digestive tract, scoliosis, short stature (153 cm), facial dysmorphia, and otosclerosis with hearing loss. CONCLUSION: This case expands the known prenatal phenotypic spectrum of cardiospondylocarpofacialsyndrome syndrome and underscores the importance of integrating advanced molecular diagnostics with detailed fetal imaging in evaluating ultrasound-detected anomalies.

papers.abstract_full: Air pollution and extreme heat frequently co-occur, yet their combined effects on cardiac development following gestational exposure remain poorly understood. We investigated the effects and potential mechanisms of gestational co-exposure to PM2.5 and heat. Pregnant mice were exposed to filtered air, PM2.5 (10 μg/m3), heat (39 ℃), or both for 2 h/day from embryonic day 6.5 (E6.5) to E18.5, and offspring hearts were evaluated on postnatal day 1 (P1). Gestational co-exposure increased ventricular wall thickness and impaired systolic function, accompanied by inflammatory cell infiltration, oxidative damage, and mitochondrial ultrastructural changes. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that co-exposure altered pathways related to energy metabolism, including inositol phosphate metabolism and pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis. Further analysis of the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) revealed that myo-inositol levels and Ucp2 expression were reduced after co-exposure. These changes are noteworthy because myo-inositol has been linked to congenital heart defect risk, while UCP2 contributes to neonatal cardiomyocyte metabolism. Experimental validation further showed that co-exposure decreased ATP content, downregulated cardiac development-related genes, and increased the protein expression of DRP1 and FIS1. Collectively, these findings suggest that mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to impaired cardiac development following gestational co-exposure, with reductions in myo-inositol levels and UCP2 expression potentially involved in this process. These findings provide preliminary mechanistic insights into the developmental cardiotoxicity of combined environmental exposures.

papers.abstract_full: The etiology of severe left-sided obstructive lesions (LSOL) of the heart, a common form of congenital heart disease (CHD), often remains unknown even after comprehensive genetic testing. Preclinical models implicate placental perturbations in abnormal cardiogenesis; however, little is known about connections between human placenta and fetal cardiac diseases. We profiled term placentas from severe LSOL pregnancies (n = 20) with and without placental pathologies and healthy controls (n = 10) to test whether severe fetal LSOL is associated with distinct transcriptomic and cellular states. Bulk RNA-sequencing of archival formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissues identified 1,030 differentially expressed protein-coding genes (580 [up], 450 [down]). Upregulated programs involved heart-valve development, endothelial signaling, and extracellular-matrix processes; while endocrine, trophoblast and gamma-aminobutyric acid signaling processes were downregulated. Severe LSOL pregnancies with histologically normal placentas showed enrichment of lymphatic-vascular development and cyclic-nucleotide signaling. Digital deconvolution analysis inferred reduced trophoblast fractions with reciprocal increase in endothelial and immune cell types. These findings support a unique placental gene expression in abnormal cardiac development, even in the absence of overt placental histopathology. These RNA expression signatures may serve as candidate biomarkers and lay the groundwork for mechanistic studies of the heart-placenta axis and future risk stratification in pregnancies with fetuses diagnosed with severe LSOL.

papers.abstract_full: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) remains one of the most severe gastrointestinal emergencies of prematurity. Although survival of extremely preterm infants has improved, NEC continues to cause substantial mortality, intestinal failure, neurodevelopmental impairment, and prolonged neonatal intensive care. Its pathogenesis has traditionally been described as a convergence of prematurity, enteral feeding, intestinal ischemia, and abnormal bacterial colonization. This model remains useful, but it does not fully explain why only a subset of high-risk infants develop NEC or why single interventions show inconsistent benefit. This narrative review examines classic preterm NEC as a disorder of neonatal mucosal immune ecology, while distinguishing it from spontaneous intestinal perforation and predominantly hemodynamic injury in congenital heart disease. Epithelial immaturity, dysbiosis, altered microbial metabolism, exaggerated pattern-recognition signaling, immune-cell activation, endothelial dysfunction, thromboinflammation, and regulated cell death amplify one another. Particular attention is given to cell-specific signaling, the interaction of vascular and epithelial injury, and the distinction between protective autophagy and destructive stress responses. These mechanisms inform translational opportunities involving mother's own milk, donor human milk, strain-specific probiotics, postbiotics, defined microbial metabolites, extracellular vesicles, organoids, and multi-omics biomarkers. A mucosal immune-ecology model supports precision prevention based on developmental timing, microbial function, immune state, and injury mechanism.

papers.abstract_full: Genetic variation among C57BL/6 mouse strains may influence cardiovascular phenotypes and contribute to inter-study variability in biomedical research. We investigated the distribution of the Mylk3 c.-5T>A variant, previously shown to cause loss of cardiac myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK3) and late-onset dilated cardiomyopathy, across C57BL/6 lineages. The variant was homozygously present in C57BL/6N and C57BL/6By strains but absent from C57BL/6J-derived mouse strains. This distribution indicates that the variant was established before divergence of the C57BL/6By branch, although its precise origin cannot be determined from contemporary samples. Despite preserved Mylk3 transcript abundance, C57BL/6N hearts lacked full-length MLCK3 protein. These findings exemplify how genetic differences between seemingly identical wild-type backgrounds can introduce significant confounding factors, highlighting the importance of accurate substrain identification and reporting for experimental design, interpretation, and reproducibility. Highlighting the broader relevance of these findings, a survey of 1238 recent open-access articles from cardiovascular journals found that 35% reported the use of C57BL/6 mice without specifying the N or J substrain. Altogether, our findings identify the Mylk3 variant as a lineage-defining feature of C57BL/6N mice and related substrains, with potential implications for cardiovascular studies using this background.

papers.abstract_full: RATIONALE: Noonan syndrome (NS) is an autosomal dominant RASopathy caused by pathogenic variants in genes that regulate the rat sarcoma (RAS)/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway. Hearing impairment is increasingly recognized as part of the NS phenotype and may include sensorineural hearing loss of varying severity. Severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss may occasionally be an early presenting feature, particularly when other manifestations are subtle. PATIENT CONCERNS: A male infant aged 2 months and 24 days was evaluated after repeatedly failing newborn hearing screening. DIAGNOSES: Diagnostic auditory brainstem response (ABR) testing was reported to indicate bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss; however, the original ear-specific audiological data were unavailable for independent review. The infant had poor postnatal growth, with low weight and length for age, whereas head circumference remained within the World Health Organization (WHO) reference range. No characteristic facial features were identified at the initial assessment, and echocardiography revealed no structural cardiac abnormality. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous c.182A > G (p.Asp61Gly) variant in the protein tyrosine phosphatase non-receptor type 11 gene (PTPN11). Parental Sanger sequencing did not detect the variant in either parent, supporting a de novo origin. These findings were consistent with a diagnosis of Noonan syndrome. INTERVENTIONS: The infant was referred to pediatric audiology for hearing-aid assessment and early auditory-verbal rehabilitation. According to parental report, hearing aids were subsequently fitted and auditory-verbal rehabilitation was initiated. Cochlear implant evaluation was under consideration because of the reported profound sensorineural hearing loss. The legal guardians also received genetic counseling regarding the diagnosis and inheritance of Noonan syndrome. OUTCOMES: At approximately 7 months of age, the family reported ongoing hearing-aid use and auditory-verbal rehabilitation, with subjective improvement in auditory responsiveness. Cochlear implant evaluation remained under consideration. No formal post-referral records or objective audiological outcome measures were available. LESSONS: This case illustrates that Noonan syndrome can be diagnosed in early infancy when reported profound sensorineural hearing loss is accompanied by poor growth, even when typical facial and cardiac findings are not evident at the initial evaluation.

papers.abstract_full: Marfan syndrome (MFS) is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder mainly affecting the cardiovascular, ocular, and skeletal systems. Fibrillin-1 (FBN1) is the primary causative gene for MFS. Molecular testing can not only facilitate early detection and differential diagnosis but also provide a basis for familial cascade testing, prenatal diagnosis, and long-term risk stratification. In 2024, the ClinGen FBN1 Variant Curation Expert Panel published an ACMG/AMP gene-specific refinement consensus for the classification of FBN1-related MFS variants, emphasizing the uniform reference transcript, standardized phenotypic data collection, family segregation evidence, and quantitative application of phenotype-specific evidence. Guided by this consensus, this review has summarized FBN1 testing technologies, variant interpretation, quality control, family screening strategies in international guidelines, and implementation pathways in domestic laboratories. It also compared the difference in MFS family screening strategies among three guidelines from the United States, Europe, and Japan. Furthermore, management recommendations are proposed from the laboratory medicine perspective for special scenarios such as newborns/children, prenatal diagnosis, variants of uncertain significance (VUS), and variant-negative relatives, with an aim to provide a reference for clinical laboratories to achieve accurate diagnosis and family management of MFS.

papers.abstract_full: Left-sided obstructive lesions (LSOLs), represented by coarctation of the aorta (CoA), cause persistent vascular pathology and pressure overload that can lead to pathological cardiac remodeling. However, the epigenetic changes associated with local vascular abnormalities and ventricular remodeling remain incompletely understood. We performed H3K27ac chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) in paired aortic tissues from patients with CoA to characterize region-associated super-enhancer (SE) landscapes and transcriptional alterations. Integrated multi-omics analysis, together with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) from LSOLs patients, identified neuropeptide W (NPW) as a SE-associated candidate. c-JUN CUT&RUN-qPCR showed AP-1 enrichment at successfully amplified NPW-associated SE regions (Peak1). In primary smooth muscle cells (SMCs), broad BET inhibition or NPW silencing was associated with reduced contractile-marker expression, whereas exogenous NPW attenuated angiotensin II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy in vitro. Plasma NPW levels were lower in patients with CoA and were associated with echocardiographic indices of remodeling. These findings identify NPW as a SE-associated candidate pathway in CoA and provide supportive evidence for broader relevance to LSOLs-associated cardiac remodeling.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: The mammalian heart is formed from distinct cardiac progenitor fields: the first heart field (FHF), second heart field (SHF), and juxta-cardiac field (JCF). How these fields are established remains one of the oldest questions in cardiac biology and is central to understanding congenital heart disease, which differentially affects derivatives of the individual fields. Previous work has demonstrated that the fields emerge and differentiate at distinct times; however, the mechanisms underlying their establishment have remained elusive. Here, we implicate Hedgehog signaling-dependent heterochronic control of cardiac differentiation in the emergence of different heart fields. METHODS: We assessed Hedgehog signaling activity by assembling a cardio-mesodermal single-cell atlas. We analyzed Hedgehog ligand gene expression by confocal imaging in gastrulating mouse embryos. We investigated the necessity of Hedgehog signaling using 2 distinct genetic Hedgehog loss-of-function mouse models, analyzed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing analysis. RESULTS: Our results show that Hedgehog signaling mediates field-specific heterochronic control of differentiation timing that orchestrates the establishment of the SHF and JCF as distinct from the FHF. We identify a common cardiac progenitor transcriptomic state from which all 3 fields emerge. We show that the SHF and JCF are established coincident with Hedgehog signaling reception, whereas the FHF evades Hedgehog pathway activity and rapidly differentiates. We find that Hedgehog ligand expression sandwiches the cardiac mesoderm emerging from the primitive streak, spatially coordinating SHF and JCF establishment. Partial depletion of Hedgehog signaling causes premature activation of the cardiac differentiation program in the SHF and JCF. Complete ablation of Hedgehog signaling results in failed SHF and JCF establishment. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings reveal a Hedgehog signaling-dependent, non-cell-autonomous heterochronic mechanism required for SHF and JCF formation. This heterochronic mechanism provides a new paradigm for understanding the ordered temporal emergence of the cardiac progenitor fields that support the development of the 4-chambered heart, as well as a general model for the emergence of progenitor fields that drive organogenesis across the mammalian body plan.

papers.abstract_full: Myocardial infarction (MI) is a metabolic disorder that poses a notable threat to human health, with post-MI heart failure (HF) markedly affecting patient prognosis. The overactivation of inflammation and fibrosis serves an important role in the progression of post-MI HF; however, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. The present study aimed to investigate the associations among metabolic reprogramming, inflammation and fibrosis after MI. By integrating single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics data from MI and dilated cardiomyopathy, a common metabolic feature, glycolysis, was identified. This feature was shared by cardiomyocytes and monocytes in myocardial infarction and was specifically localized to the peri-infarct region. Pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 was identified as a core gene linking metabolic reprogramming to fibrosis. A mouse model of MI was established by permanent ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery. PDK4 knockout was applied to evaluate its role in post-infarction fibrotic remodeling. Furthermore, the results of the present study revealed a cross-cellular metabolic reprogramming process mediating chronic inflammatory cell interactions. In conclusion, the findings of the present study suggested that targeting metabolic reprogramming may offer a promising strategy for preventing inflammation and fibrosis to mitigate post-MI HF.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Genomic studies in hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) are limited by sample sizes and targeted approaches. METHODS: The Genomic Studies in Blood and Marrow Transplantation (GS-BMT) project is a collaboration between the National Cancer Institute (NCI) and the CIBMTR® designed to investigate recipient and donor determinants of HCT outcomes. We are generating genome-wide SNP-array genotyping for all samples, and sequencing and methylation profiling for selected subsets. We report study design and cohort characteristics and present two proof-of-concept analyses: comparison of conventional and machine learning prediction of overall survival after HCT in 9,262 patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and assessment of inherited susceptibility to clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) among 19,750 HCT donors using polygenic scores (PGS). RESULTS: GS-BMT includes 30,718 donor-recipient pairs who received allogeneic HCT in the United States between 2000 and 2019. In AML, clinical variables alone provided modest prediction for post-transplant survival, with similar performance for Cox proportional hazards, random survival forest, and deep neural network survival models (C-index=0.63, 0.62, and 0.62, respectively). In donors, CHIP-PGS did not differ by age (p=0.76) but was modestly lower in unrelated vs . related donors (-0.06 standard deviation [SD]; p=0.002). In an illustrative analysis assuming risk of event increases by 50% or 80% per PGS-SD, the top 5.2% and 12.3% of the donors, respectively, would have at least twice the risk of a donor with the average PGS. CONCLUSIONS: GS-BMT establishes a large genomic platform aiming to improve individualized risk prediction, donor selection, and precision medicine in HCT.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVES: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) arises from complex interactions between genetic and environmental factors, creating a need for approaches that integrate inherited susceptibility and cumulative environmental exposure. Previous models have focused on clinical or genetic data and provided limited mechanistic insight. This study developed a machine-learning model that integrated a polygenic risk score (PRS) and DNA methylation to classify prevalent T2DM and assessed their individual and combined contributions to classification performance. METHODS: Models were developed and validated using data from the Ansan/Ansung cohort (n = 1,318) and the independent Health Examinee cohort (n = 358). PRS was calculated using external genome-wide association study summary statistics, and DNA methylation features were represented by β-values at T2DM-related cytosine-phosphate-guanine sites. Three feature sets were compared: Base, Base + PRS, and Base + PRS + DNA methylation. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Decision curve analysis assessed clinical utility, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were used to interpret the models. RESULTS: Adding PRS and then DNA methylation features progressively increased AUROC across algorithms. The linear support vector machine with the fully integrated feature set achieved the highest discrimination (AUROC = 0.896, AUPRC = 0.801). PRS improved accuracy, and DNA methylation data produced further gains, particularly in recall and F1-score. Decision curve analysis showed that the integrated model provided greater net benefit across clinically relevant threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis identified PRS as the most influential individual feature and DNA methylation features as the largest contributors at the group level. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating PRS and DNA methylation improves the performance of machine-learning models for T2DM classification. Genetic and epigenetic factors thus provide complementary information for characterizing prevalent T2DM.

papers.abstract_full: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) hold promise for stratifying inherited disease risk, yet their clinical adoption remains constrained by poor transferability across populations and cohorts. To bridge this gap, we propose a pragmatic framework that recalibrates externally derived PRSs to local datasets through machine learning-based optimization. This post-PRS calibration approach integrates multiple published PRSs for a given disease and reweighs them based on predictive performance in the target cohort, generating composite locally optimized PRS that is fine-tuned to local disease risk. We test local optimization on three diseases currently under active clinical trials for PRS utility (coronary artery disease [CAD], breast cancer [BC], and prostate cancer [PC]). Local optimization achieves substantial C-statistic improvements across diseases in MGB Biobank, with C-statistics improving by an average of 19.8% for CAD, 9.4% for PC, and 8.3% for BC. The locally optimized CAD PRS identifies 27.7% of CAD cases compared with 17.8% by the top-performing published CAD PRS, and improvements in case enrichment are more pronounced for breast cancer (20.8% vs. 7.1%) and prostate cancer (16.4% vs. 8.8%). This low-complexity post hoc calibration approach enables scalable implementation of PRS across diverse health systems without new GWAS discovery or complex upstream algorithmic innovations. By treating PRS as adaptable rather than static, the locally optimized PRS framework provides a practical blueprint for clinical adoption of PRS in diverse local settings and helps mitigate disparities stemming from one-size-fits-all applications of externally derived PRS.

papers.abstract_full: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been instrumental in uncovering the genetic basis of complex traits, yet classical single-variant testing remains limited in power and biological interpretability. Over the past decade, GWAS methodology has expanded from purely statistical association frameworks toward integrative models that incorporate functional annotations, multi-trait information, and data-driven prioritization strategies. Early developments leveraged regulatory genomics and cross-phenotype statistics to improve locus discovery, while machine learning approaches enabled systematic ranking of sub-threshold variants. More recently, deep learning architectures, including Transformer-based frameworks, have been introduced to integrate GWAS summary signals with linkage disequilibrium patterns and diverse genomic annotations. In parallel, multi-omics integration and transfer learning across related traits have emerged as practical solutions for limited sample sizes and population heterogeneity. This chapter reviews the evolving methodological landscape of AI-enabled GWAS, highlights key advances in variant discovery and functional interpretation, and discusses remaining challenges such as ancestry bias, interpretability, and the need for biological validation. Together, these approaches provide a foundation for more context-aware and scalable genetic studies of complex disease.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) perform strongly on medical specialty board multiple-choice questions (MCQs) but underperform in complex medical reasoning. This gap indicates a need to improve LLM medical reasoning and evaluation paradigms. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and evaluate MedEvalArena, a dynamically regenerable benchmark for assessing medical reasoning in LLMs. METHODS: In a symmetric round-robin format, 6 frontier LLMs from the OpenAI, Grok, Gemini, Claude, Kimi, and DeepSeek families generated challenging board-style medical MCQs, adjudicated question validity on an ensemble LLM-as-judge panel, and answered the validated examination. Candidate items were generated until each model contributed 50 validated questions according to Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC)/American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS) physician specialty distributions, yielding a 300-question examination. Judges adjudicated candidate questions' logical validity and medical accuracy. We compared question-generation validity rates, assessed leave-one-out judge agreement, and tested for self-judging preference. Questions were audited for overlap with public MedQA (medical question-answering) benchmarks. We tested question-answering (QA) accuracy across LLMs using a binomial-logit generalized linear mixed model likelihood-ratio test. A generator-stratified 90-question subset was completed by 5 board-certified physicians for paired human-LLM analysis. We evaluated inference cost-accuracy tradeoffs. Multiple comparisons were adjusted by the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure. RESULTS: Judge-panel validity rates were significantly higher for questions generated by OpenAI (94.8%, Wilson 95% CI 85.9%-98.2%), Gemini (92.3%, 95% CI 83.2%-96.7%), and Claude (83.3%, 95% CI 72.6%-90.4%) models than those generated by Kimi (63.8%, 95% CI 54.3%-72.4%), Grok (56%, 95% CI 45.8%-65.8%), and DeepSeek (46.0%, 95% CI 37.4%-54.7%). Kimi also demonstrated significantly higher validity than DeepSeek (2-sample tests of proportions; BH-adjusted P=.01). The public-source similarity audit found no exact or near-duplicate matches. Leave-one-out judge agreement was moderate. Generator-specific same-family judging coefficients were nonnegative (0 to 11.0 percentage points); however, none remained significant after BH adjustment. There was no significant difference between the 6 frontier LLM QA accuracies, which ranged from 85.7% (257/300) to 91.7% (275/300), on the 300-question examination (generalized linear mixed model likelihood-ratio test P=.07). The study had 80% power to detect LLM accuracy differences of 9.2 percentage points; nonsignificance did not establish equivalence. On the 90-question subset, physician accuracy was 85.6% (95% CI 79.4%-91.7%; stratified normal with finite-population correction), compared with aggregate LLM performance of 94.4% (85/90; Wilson 95% CI 87.6%-97.6%). This difference was not significant (McNemar test, P=.08); however, the study was powered to detect a human vs LLM accuracy difference of 14% to 15%. Answering-only costs varied by nearly 2 orders of magnitude, with multiple models on the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier. CONCLUSIONS: MedEvalArena enables scalable, regenerable, peer-judged benchmarking of LLM medical reasoning. Question-generation validity differentiated model families more clearly than answering accuracy, suggesting that valid MCQ generation may complement QA benchmarks for assessing LLM medical reasoning.

papers.abstract_full: AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)]-lowering therapies are being investigated to reduce atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. However, their implications on women's reproductive health are unknown, and pre-clinical models offer limited insight towards understanding such effects. We evaluated potential causal effects of genetically proxied Lp(a) lowering on reproductive and offspring health outcomes. METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed common and rare variants in the LPA region using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), genetic risk scores (GRSs), and gene-based tests. Additionally, performing individual-level analyses using UK Biobank and All of Us cohorts, with genome sequencing linked to biomarkers and electronic health records, we investigated outcomes spanning maternal health during pregnancy, labour and delivery complications, pregnancy outcomes, and congenital malformations in 236 228 UK Biobank and 122 038 All of Us women and recorded female infertility in 102 549 All of Us women. In summary-level analyses, no significant adverse associations of genetically predicted low Lp(a) with reproductive and offspring health outcomes were detected. Nominal associations were present across MR, GRS, and gene-based analyses, but no adverse reproductive findings survived the multiple-testing corrections. Confidence intervals for all fertility and reproductive-count estimates included the null. Controls showed expected associations for higher Lp(a) with LDL cholesterol (P = 2 × 10-19) and triglycerides (P = 4 × 10-9). CONCLUSION: In summary, we found no robust or multiplicity-adjusted evidence of adverse reproductive or offspring health effects related to genetically proxied Lp(a) lowering. These findings provide genetic evidence relevant to assessing the reproductive and offspring health implications of targeting Lp(a).

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Taxanes are standard chemotherapeutic agents for breast cancer, yet their clinical utility is often limited by severe multi-organ adverse drug reactions (ADRs), which show marked inter-individual variability. METHODS: To investigate the genetic basis of this variability, we performed whole-exome sequencing (WES) in 203 breast cancer patients receiving taxane-based chemotherapy and assessed five ADR phenotypes-neutropenia, leukopenia, rash, peripheral neurotoxicity, and gastrointestinal toxicity. Common variants were tested via single-variant association tests, and rare variants via gene-based burden tests (SKAT-O). RESULTS: In common-variant analysis, PTGES rs2302821 showed a significant association with neutropenia (joint genotype test P = 5.57 × 10-6; adjusted P = 2.19 × 10-6), with the AC genotype conferring a protective effect (adjusted OR = 0.17, 95% CI: 0.08-0.35). For rash, rare-variant gene-based analysis nominated GSDMA as a candidate (P = 2.88 × 10-7). GSDMA exhibited skin-specific expression, and missense variants were exclusively observed in affected cases; however, these results remain exploratory given the limited number of rash cases (n = 12). A common-variant signal in IL36B was nominally significant in unadjusted analysis but attenuated after covariate adjustment, warranting further validation. DISCUSSION: Our findings identify PTGES rs2302821 as a potential genetic marker for taxane-induced neutropenia and nominate GSDMA as a preliminary candidate for rash susceptibility, providing a genomic perspective on inter-individual variability in taxane-related ADRs.

papers.abstract_full: Genetic causes are identified in up to 15% of Parkinson's disease (PD) patients; the remaining idiopathic PD (iPD) patients are attributed to polygenic risk, environmental and lifestyle factors, and interactions thereof. We applied five advanced polygenic score (PGS) tools to data from 1762 iPD patients and 4227 healthy controls of European ancestry. 5-fold cross-validation revealed a significant boost in the discriminative power of modern Bayesian methods over simpler approaches, leading to the development of a novel iPD-PGS. This score demonstrated significantly improved performance compared to existing scores, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.680 (95% confidence interval (-CI):[0.665, 0.695]). External validation confirmed its robustness. Early-onset iPD patients exhibited higher PGS values than late-onset iPD patients and healthy controls, indicating increased polygenetic burden. Applying our novel iPD-PGS to carriers of heterozygous PRKN variants and GBA1 coding risk variants suggested that penetrance in these groups is partly explained by the same polygenic alterations as observed mitigating iPD. GBA1 showed a trend toward higher discriminative potential than PRKN (GBA1: AUC = 0.639, 95%-CI:[0.590, 0.687]; PRKN: AUC = 0.594, 95%-CI:[0.501, 0.687]), though confidence intervals overlapped. Our study highlights the potential of advanced PGSs in PD research, particularly in identifying high-risk individuals and modifying risk in rare-variant carriers.

papers.abstract_full: Moyamoya angiopathy (MMA) is a rare steno-occlusive condition resulting in transient ischemic attacks and strokes in children and adults. Previous studies, mainly in adult patients, suggested RNF213 as the most prevalent susceptibility gene due to an Asian founder variant. Nevertheless, the genetic landscape in early-onset European MMA patients requires further elucidation. Exome-sequencing was performed in 104 pediatric MMA patients, including three with Down syndrome, and 520 healthy controls. Rare-variant enrichment testing was performed using the R-package SKAT on the whole cohort as well as in a 100% European subset, revealing a total of 28 enriched genes. Both tests showed the most common known MMA genes (RNF213 and NF1) among the top three enriched genes, underlining the validity of our approach. Seven of the concordantly enriched genes are novel MMA candidates (ATAD2, COL18A1, NAV1, ALOX12B, KRTAP4-7, KCNJ12, and KBTBD13). De novo variants were found in NF1, RNF213, COL18A1, ECI1, and YIPF1. In summary, our study confirms RNF213 and NF1 as major susceptibility genes and suggests seven novel early-onset MMA susceptibility genes. Of special interest is the novel candidate gene COL18A1, which is involved in angiogenesis and endothelial cell proliferation, due to its potential additional role as a modifier of MMA in trisomy 21.

papers.abstract: Background:  Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a clinically and genetically heterogenous neurodegenerative disorder in which both monogenic and complex genetic mechanism contribute to disease susceptibility. papers.abstract_full: Background:  Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a clinically and genetically heterogenous neurodegenerative disorder in which both monogenic and complex genetic mechanism contribute to disease susceptibility. Increasing evidence also indicates that non motor manifestations, including sleep disturbances, significantly influence disease burden. This study aimed to characterize the genetic spectrum of ALS in a predominantly North Indian cohort while evaluating the prevalence of sleep related abnormalities. Methods: Seventy-three clinically diagnosed ALS patients were recruited from a tertiary care centre in North India. Disease severity was assessed using the ALSFRS-R. Sleep quality, daytime sleepiness, and REM sleep behaviour disorder symptoms were evaluated using the PSQI, ESS and RBDQ questionnaires, respectively. Genetic analysis included targeted sequencing of SOD1, TARDBP, and ANG, followed by repeat expansion analysis of C9orf72, ATXN1, ATXN2, ATXN3, and ATXN7. Whole exome sequencing was performed in selected cases to further investigate the genetic basis of ALS. Results: The cohort demonstrated a male predominance and an earlier age of onset compared to many Western populations. Poor sleep quality and excessive daytime sleepiness were frequently observed although no significant association was found between sleep parameters and disease severity. Genetic screening identified a pathogenic/likely pathogenic TARDBP variant classified by ClinVar while no known or novel pathogenic variants were detected in SOD1 or ANG. Repeat expansion studies revealed one patient harbouring pathogenic C9orf72 repeat expansions. For the ATXN1, one patient harboured pathogenic repeat expansions and two patients carried intermediate length repeats. Additionally, one patient harboured intermediate repeat expansions in ATXN2. Whole exome sequencing revealed novel and rare variants in ALS associated genes including ANXA11, SIGMAR1, SETX, ERBB4 and NEK1, highlighting substantial genetic heterogeneity. Conclusions: Our findings highlight the complex genetic heterogeneity of ALS, with pathogenic repeat expansions and rare variants identified across multiple disease associated genes. These results demonstrate the importance of comprehensive genetic testing to improve the detection of clinically relevant variants in ALS. In addition, the high prevalence of sleep related disturbances observed in the cohort emphasizes the need to incorporate non motor assessment into routine clinical evaluation of patients with ALS.

Genetic screening identified a pathogenic/likely pathogenic TARDBP variant classified by ClinVar while no known or novel pathogenic variants were detected in SOD1 or ANG.

papers.abstract: Rare alleles arise from mutations on an existing haplotype background, yet current gene-based rare variant association tests treat low-frequency coding variants as effects independent of the common regulatory variants that surround them. The penetrance of rare coding variants can be modulated by the cis-regulatory landscape, and failing to account for this context limits the statistical power of existing methods for complex traits. papers.abstract_full: Rare alleles arise from mutations on an existing haplotype background, yet current gene-based rare variant association tests treat low-frequency coding variants as effects independent of the common regulatory variants that surround them. The penetrance of rare coding variants can be modulated by the cis-regulatory landscape, and failing to account for this context limits the statistical power of existing methods for complex traits. We present PrediXSKAT, a kernel-based rare variant association framework that incorporates the surrounding cis-regulatory landscape by estimating its impact on gene expression via PrediXcan. PrediXSKAT embeds predicted gene expression directly into the Sequence Kernel Association Test kernel through element-wise similarity weighting, concentrating rare variant signal among individuals who share concordant genetic and regulatory backgrounds. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that PrediXSKAT increases power over standard kernel-based testing under biologically realistic conditions where a proportion of tested variants carry small, mixed-direction effects. Type I error rates are controlled in the absence of association. Power gains persist across a range of sample sizes and causal variant architectures. Applied to whole-genome sequencing data from the Alzheimer’s Disease Sequencing Project, PrediXSKAT recapitulates established disease loci and amplifies signals at previously unreported candidate genes without indiscriminately inflating genome-wide results. PrediXSKAT provides a generalizable and extensible framework for the joint analysis of common regulatory and rare coding variants. The approach can be applied to any kernel-based set test and extended to jointly consider multiple genes within the same biological pathway, offering a principled strategy for improving rare variant discovery in large-scale sequencing studies of complex disease.

papers.abstract_full: PURPOSE: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) are an emerging type of risk prediction for common conditions in the clinical setting. However, most clinical implementations of PRS have been of limited scope. In its fourth phase, the Electronic Medical Records and Genomics Network has validated and returned PRS, monogenic findings, family history, and clinical risk factors for 11 common conditions across 10 sites to nearly 24,000 individuals. This provides an opportunity to identify cases that highlight illustrative and challenging aspects of the return of results experiences among patients, providers, and institutions receiving clinical genome-informed risk assessments. METHODS: A survey was distributed across the eMERGE sites, engaging researchers conducting results disclosures to share experiences relating to communicating PRS results, return challenges, patient and provider perceptions of the return, and more. A primary reviewer used content analysis to establish categories validated by secondary review. RESULTS: A total of 64 cases from 9 sites were submitted, with 24 cases meeting criteria. Additional review coded these cases into 4 categories: PRS-driven findings and outcomes, return of results challenges, primary care provider (PCP) interactions and perceptions, and monogenic and mosaic results. CONCLUSION: These cases highlight considerations when clinically implementing genome-informed risk assessments, and specifically PRS, into the health care system at large. Future studies implementing PRS in clinical workflows should aim to provide patient- and provider-facing educational materials or staff trained professionals such as genetic counselors, identify care coordination for patients receiving multiple genomic results, and investigate the risk impact of multiple genetic risk contributors.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Germline variants predicting treatment toxicity guide care for a few drug-gene pairs, yet most reported associations never reach the clinic. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) isolates the problem: somatic genotyping is standard and toxicity limits dose intensity across chemotherapy, radiotherapy and immunotherapy, yet no germline marker guides therapy. METHODS: Per a registered protocol (PROSPERO CRD420261364865), we searched four databases for 2020-2026 publications, synthesizing 35 studies from 15 countries. Thirty-four variant-toxicity associations were grouped by mechanism (transport/metabolism, DNA repair, immune regulation, target pathway). The 11 priority loci (12 variants) were benchmarked against the Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium (CPIC) hierarchy. RESULTS: Twenty-nine of 34 associations were nominally significant. Of 10 studies correcting for multiplicity, seven had a finding that passed its own threshold (the lead association in five). Of 12 studies with validation analyses, three mounted an independent attempt (two with stated reservations), all nominally positive (single SNP, FDR-adjusted p=0.179; polygenic score; 27 patients); none replicated an association passing a multiplicity threshold. Across 23 significant lead associations, effect magnitude decreased with sample size (Spearman ρ=-0.48, 95% CI -0.81 to -0.07), consistent with selection-driven inflation. XRCC1 rs25487 effects differed by treatment and endpoint. No priority locus reached CPIC level A or B for its NSCLC drug pair. CONCLUSIONS: Many germline toxicity biomarkers are reported in NSCLC, but evidence remains exploratory: validation is uncommon, effect-size inflation is plausible, and within the review window no candidate met implementation standards. The bottleneck is evidence maturation, not discovery. We propose a four-phase framework toward genotype-guided care.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Prior studies of cardiovascular health (CVH) and genetic susceptibility have not accounted for heterogeneity in underlying cardiometabolic-renal states. Whether ideal CVH protects against cardiovascular disease (CVD) across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome continuum, and whether this benefit is modified by CKM stage or genetic susceptibility, remains unknown. METHODS: This prospective study included 242,951 UK Biobank participants (aged 37-73) in CKM Stages 0-3, free of CVD at baseline (2006-2010), followed through 2022. CVH was quantified using Life's Essential 8 (LE8) (poor, <50; intermediate, 50-79; ideal, ≥80). A cardiovascular-specific polygenic risk score (PRS) was categorized into tertiles. The primary outcome was incident composite CVD. Multivariable Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs); cumulative incidence functions accounting for competing mortality were compared by Gray's test. RESULTS: Among 242,951 participants (mean age, 55.7 years; 53.1% women), 39,355 incident CVD events occurred over a median follow-up of 15.2 years. Ideal CVH was associated with 53% lower CVD risk versus poor CVH (HR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.45-0.49), with the largest reductions for heart failure (HF) (HR, 0.33) and coronary heart disease (CHD) (HR, 0.35). Higher CVH was associated with lower CVD risk across genetic risk strata. No CKM × CVH interaction was detected (P = .335), indicating preserved protection across the disease continuum; a significant CKM × PRS interaction (P = .003) indicated amplified polygenic risk impact in advanced stages. Both CVH- and PRS-based stratification significantly separated cumulative CVD incidence across all CKM stages (all Gray's test P < .001). Results were robust to inverse probability weighting (IPW), competing risk models, and landmark analyses. CONCLUSION: Favorable CVH was associated with substantially lower CVD risk across the full CKM continuum without attenuation in advanced disease, whereas polygenic risk consequences were amplified in later CKM stages. These findings support integrating CVH assessment as a complementary axis within CKM risk stratification.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Multiple myeloma is a genetically complex malignancy influenced by environmental and inherited factors. Genome-wide association studies have identified multiple single nucleotide polymorphisms associated with multiple myeloma risk, yet data from South Asian populations remain scarce. This study evaluated the association of multiple myeloma risk single nucleotide polymorphisms in a European population and examined cumulative genetic risk using polygenic risk scores in a Pakistani cohort. METHODS: A total of 337 individuals were genotyped for 24 genome-wide association study-identified single nucleotide polymorphisms using a TaqMan Assay. Polygenic risk scores were calculated using both unweighted and weighted models. Participants were stratified into polygenic risk scores quintiles, and odds ratios were computed to assess risk trends. RESULTS: Significant associations were identified for rs6746082 (DTNB), which conferred a protective effect (p < 0.001), and rs7187359 (SRCAP), associated with increased risk under both models (log additive: p = 0.024 and dominant: p = 0.009). The unweighted polygenic risk scores indicated elevated multiple myeloma risk in the 4th quintile (p = 0.017), while the weighted polygenic risk scores showed more consistent stratification, with individuals in the highest quintile having a 2.20-fold increased risk (p = 0.034). CONCLUSION: This study reinforces the polygenic basis of multiple myeloma susceptibility and demonstrates that certain genome-wide association study-identified single nucleotide polymorphisms are relevant in the Pakistani population. While weighted polygenic risk scores showed modest risk stratification, their clinical utility remains exploratory.

papers.abstract_full: Anthocyanidins have antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties, but prospective evidence linking dietary intake to autoimmune hypothyroidism remains limited. We examined this association in 118 724 UK Biobank adults with at least two valid 24 h dietary recalls. Follow-up began at the last recall; 2350 events occurred over a median of 13.28 years. In sex-stratified multivariable Cox models, participants in the highest intake category had a lower hazard than those consuming ≤1 mg d-1 (HR 0.75; 95% CI 0.65-0.87; P for trend <0.001). Five of six individual anthocyanidins met the false discovery rate (FDR) criterion; pelargonidin did not. Berries and cherries, red/rosé wine, and juices and smoothies contributed 39.1%, 38.5%, and 15.9% of total intake, respectively. Additional ethanol-spline adjustment attenuated the highest-category association (HR 0.83; 95% CI 0.71-0.96; P for trend = 0.005). For nonalcoholic-source intake, the highest-category HR was 0.95 (95% CI 0.83-1.08; P for trend = 0.216). Among 247 nuclear magnetic resonance biomarkers measured after dietary assessment, five fatty-acid measures and two small-LDL lipid-composition measures met the FDR criterion after adjustment for recruitment biomarker values and ethanol dose. Among 73 807 genetically eligible participants, neither thyroid polygenic score showed evidence of interaction with intake. Higher anthocyanidin intake was associated with a lower hazard of autoimmune hypothyroidism and subsequent lipid-related biomarker differences. Residual confounding and uncertainty about nonalcoholic sources limit causal interpretation.

Cox regression models were used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for overall CVD, coronary heart disease (CHD), stroke, atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure (HF), cardiovascular mortality, and all-cause mortality. Genetic predisposition was assessed by the PRS. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 13.6 years, 61,129 incident CVD events, 5,585 CVD deaths, and 30,513 all-cause deaths were recorded. Exploratory HR-based RERI estimates were positive for CVD and CHD. Continuous PRSs were associated with CVD and CHD, but not HF. CONCLUSION: MetS was associated with higher hazards of incident cardiovascular outcomes and mortality. Associations with incident CVD were stronger in women, whereas evidence of modification by BMI was limited. Genetic interaction findings were exploratory and require independent validation.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosed before age 50 years has increased, prompting lowering of screening initiation to age 45. However, age-based screening strategies treat younger adults as a homogeneous population and do not account for heterogeneity in inherited susceptibility. To evaluate whether an integrated inherited risk measure (GenProbCRC) stratifies the risk of early-onset CRC (EOCRC; <50 years). METHODS: Prospective cohort study conducted in 2 independent biobanks: the UK Biobank and the Genomic Health Initiative, a US health system-based biobank. Participants younger than 50 years at recruitment and free of CRC at baseline were followed for incident CRC until age 50. Four prespecified inherited risk groups defined by GenProbCRC, an integrated genetic risk measure incorporating a polygenic risk score, family history, and pathogenic variants in Lynch syndrome genes. Incident EOCRC. Associations between GenProbCRC and EOCRC were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models with age as the underlying time scale. Cumulative incidence by age 50 was estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods. RESULTS: Among 102,797 UK Biobank participants, 109 developed EOCRC. Compared with the low-risk group, hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) were 1.36 (0.68-2.71) for the intermediate-risk group, 5.95 (3.77-9.38) for the high-risk group, and 28.41 (13.88-58.17) for the very-high-risk group. Cumulative incidence by age 50 increased progressively across risk groups: 0.08% (low), 0.11% (intermediate), 0.46% (high), and 2.06% (very high), log-rank P < .001. Although representing approximately 21% of the population, individuals in the high- and very-high-risk groups accounted for 61% of EOCRC cases. Associations were directionally consistent in Genomic Health Initiative, although estimates were imprecise due to the smaller sample size (7206 participants; 14 EOCRC cases). CONCLUSION: The Risk of EOCRC varies substantially across inherited risk strata. These findings highlight marked heterogeneity among adults younger than 50 years and support evaluation of genomics-informed risk-based screening approaches beyond age-, family history-, and monogenic-based strategies.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Older adults with high inherited Alzheimer's disease (AD) susceptibility can still be cognitively normal (CN). An overall risk estimate alone does not show the cognitive and genetic contributions within a forecast. OBJECTIVE: To quantify clinical and genetic contributions to cognitive prognosis. METHODS: PRISM-AD combined nonlinear clinical functions and a polygenic risk score (PRS) term in 4,435 European-ancestry participants. Participant-level internal validation evaluated first recorded mild cognitive impairment (MCI) after CN in 908 participants and AD dementia after MCI in 714, within three or five years. Separately fitted comparators used identical inputs. Post hoc clinical-course comparisons used regression with robust standard errors and Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction. RESULTS: PRISM-AD using current assessments achieved average precision of 0.2996 and 0.4094 for three- and five-year CN-to-MCI, with estimates close to logistic regression. No PRISM-AD PRS increment met BH q < 0.05. Three-year first-MCI forecasts characterized risk contributions in 893 initially CN participants. A retrospective comparison over available follow-up included 95 participants with later AD and 701 with CN at their last diagnostic assessment. Modeled genetic factors were higher in later AD in nine of ten shared cognitive-risk deciles. After adjustment for modeled cognitive risk and fold, the genetic-factor ratio was 1.135 (nominal 95% CI, 1.073 to 1.201, BH q < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Higher genetic contributions were associated with later AD at comparable modeled cognitive risk. These exploratory profiles require independent validation before use in cognitive follow-up or prevention research.

papers.abstract_full: Increased fasting insulin reflects insulin resistance and is as a precursor to type 2 diabetes and a risk factor for kidney, heart and liver diseases and mortality. Cluster-specific fasting insulin polygenic scores (PS) characterize insulin resistance mechanisms based on insulin-related genetic associations with metabolic traits, and they have not been evaluated for liver outcomes. We calculated seven previously developed FI cluster-specific PS, including non-diabetogenic (Preserved Insulin Secretion, Elevated Insulin Secretion, Proinsulin) and diabetogenic clusters (Adiposity-driven Hyperinsulinemia, Visceral Adiposity, Lipodystrophy, Liver/Lipid) in 12,631 participants of the Hispanic Community Healthy Study/Study of Latinos (HCHS/SOL), and tested their association with type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney and liver outcomes. We also tested the association of FI clusters with indices of insulin homeostasis in additional 1,316 Hispanic individuals. Among HCHS/SOL participants (mean age 46 years, 59% women, 20% with diabetes), we validated associations of FI cluster-specific PS and the 19 traits used to generate clusters. The Lipodystrophy cluster was associated with type 2 diabetes (p-value =3.5 x 10 -5 ). In addition, the Adiposity-driven Hyperinsulinemia cluster was associated with the hepatic steatosis index (p-value = 2.2 ×10 -17 ) and the fatty liver index (p-value = 1.7 ×10 -14 ), while the Liver/Lipid cluster with liver fibrosis (p-value = 1.5 ×10 -4 ) and lower kidney function (p-value = 5.2 x 10 -5 ). The non-diabetogenic Elevated Insulin Secretion cluster-specific PS was associated with the disposition index (p = 0.0015). These results support insulin resistance mechanisms implicated in type 2 diabetes, liver and kidney outcomes.

papers.title: How inherited variation shapes human disease trajectories.
papers.abstract: Although inherited variation is fixed at birth, its effects on health change with age and differ between common and rare variants. Here, we introduce Mendelnoulli, a longitudinal model that combines the age-dependent effects of polygenic and monogenic variation on health records, separating how much disease each individual accumulates overall from diseases to which they are prone. Mendelnoulli further allows polygenic and monogenic components to exert different influences on latent disease traje…
papers.abstract_full: Although inherited variation is fixed at birth, its effects on health change with age and differ between common and rare variants. Here, we introduce Mendelnoulli, a longitudinal model that combines the age-dependent effects of polygenic and monogenic variation on health records, separating how much disease each individual accumulates overall from diseases to which they are prone. Mendelnoulli further allows polygenic and monogenic components to exert different influences on latent disease trajectories. We apply the model to 348 diseases, 36 polygenic scores, and 34 monogenic conditions across three biobanks and provide an atlas of the age-dependent effects of inherited variation on common human diseases. We show that polygenic effects change significantly with age, with Mendelnoulli improving held-out one-year discrimination for all 28 diseases tested compared with a model whose polygenic effects are constant over age (median AUC 0.95 vs 0.92). For individuals with no prior diagnoses, Mendelnoulli identified 8.6 more of every 100 new cases than that model, when each flagged the 5% at highest risk. For genes with an established disease, Mendelnoulli selected that disease for 27 of 30 genes and ranked it first for 17 (7 expected by chance), and recovered known differences in timing, such as earlier breast cancer effects for BRCA1 than BRCA2 (peak 48 vs 66 years). Mendelnoulli provides a unified model of common and rare genetic influences on disease trajectories across the life course.
