papers.title: One blood methylation profile stratifies ten-year risk across 21 common diseases
papers.abstract: Blood DNA methylation offers a dynamic readout of inherited and acquired influences on health, creating an opportunity for risk prediction beyond polygenic scores, which are fixed at conception and have yet to demonstrate broad clinical utility. As such, we aimed to develop methylation risk scores for 21 common diseases in 12,785 adults from Generation Scotland and the Mass General Brigham Biobank, combining technically reproducible probes, null-calibrated feature selection and ten-year survival…
papers.abstract_full: Blood DNA methylation offers a dynamic readout of inherited and acquired influences on health, creating an opportunity for risk prediction beyond polygenic scores, which are fixed at conception and have yet to demonstrate broad clinical utility. As such, we aimed to develop methylation risk scores for 21 common diseases in 12,785 adults from Generation Scotland and the Mass General Brigham Biobank, combining technically reproducible probes, null-calibrated feature selection and ten-year survival models, with evaluation in a single holdout that was not used for feature selection, model fitting or tuning. The methylation risk scores for eight diseases reached a holdout C-index of at least 0.80: chronic kidney disease, peripheral vascular disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, heart failure and type 2 diabetes with at least 50 events each, and interstitial lung disease, dementia and fatty liver disease with fewer. For the five scores with at least 50 events, adjusted hazard ratios per standard deviation ranged from 2.6 to 4.1, with the highest risk tertile containing 73 to 90% of the ten-year events. Panel CpGs were enriched for cytokine signalling, innate immune sensing and sterol metabolism. Against reported values, the eight top-tier methylation risk scores exceed published polygenic and methylation scores alone, and exceed published polygenic and methylation scores that include clinical covariates for seven of the eight diseases (the exception is type 2 diabetes, where our AUC of 0.865 without clinical risk factors is close to a methylation-plus-risk-factor model at 0.872, and our C-index of 0.809 is lower than the C-index for a polygenic-plus-risk-factor at 0.85). These results indicate that a single blood methylation profile can rank ten-year risk for several common diseases at a level that compares favourably with published genetic and methylation scores.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Predicting whether a pull request (PR) will be merged, rejected, or left unre solved is a recurring problem in empirical software engineering, yet it remains unclear how much explicit fusion of code changes and reviewer comments adds over simpler designs, and conclusions drawn from a single training run can be misleading. We report a multi-seed comparison of encoder-based fusion strategies on a retrospective dataset of 33,955 PRs from 155 projects, three platforms, and 12 programming languages. A CodeBERT–RoBERTa hybrid with bidirectional cross-modal attention is compared with concatenation and late-fusion variants, four alternative code encoders (GraphCodeBERT, UniXcoder, CodeT5, CodeReviewer), unimodal baselines, and two re-implemented prior systems, using five random seeds per model. The cross-attention hybrid reaches 88.11% mean accuracy (sample SD 0.39 percentage points, pp) and outperforms its code-only counterpart in every seed (+1.85 pp; Holm-adjusted paired p = 0.008). How-ever, the seven best models lie within a 0.42 pp band, and cross-attention exceeds concatenation by only 0.34 pp on average across five encoders (positive for four of five, not significant for any single encoder); at one seed (42) the ordering of the two reversed. Review comments alone are about as informative as code alone, and combining them adds roughly 1.6–1.9 pp. Project identity is strongly associated with the outcome (Cram´er’s V = 0.60), so the random split used here probably overstates generalisation. All analyses are retrospective, use features that become available only after review, and exclude LLM-based baselines.

papers.abstract_full: C09.RCO, an LMI1-like homeobox gene, was identified as a candidate regulator of lobed-leaf formation in Siberian kale; promoter variation was associated with increased C09.RCO expression and the lobed-leaf phenotype. Leaf margin morphology represents a key aspect of phenotypic diversity in the Brassicaceae. Siberian kale (Brassica napus subsp. pabularia) is characterized by deeply lobed leaves and is cultivated as a nutritious leafy vegetable with potential advantages for high-density planting and hybrid production. However, the genetic basis of the lobed-leaf trait remains poorly understood. In this study, bulked segregant analysis sequencing (BSA-seq) identified a candidate locus associated with the lobed-leaf trait in an F2 population derived from a cross between the deeply lobed-leaf Siberian kale line, Beta, and the weakly serrated-leaf rapeseed line, Line35. Through KASP-based fine mapping, the candidate region was narrowed to a 163.1-kb interval on chromosome C09, which contained 23 predicted genes, including two tandemly duplicated LMI1-like homeobox genes, C09.RCO and C09.LMI1. Comparative sequence analysis identified three deletions (1,586, 60, and 3 bp) and two SNPs in the C09.RCO promoter in Beta relative to the corresponding sequence in Line35, whereas no sequence variation was detected in C09.LMI1. RT-qPCR analysis showed that C09.RCO expression in the shoot apices of the Beta variety was 14.3-28.5 times that in the Line35 variety across the three profiled stages of development. Ectopic expression of C09.RCO under the CaMV 35 S promoter in Arabidopsis thaliana produced serrated and lobed-leaf margins, supporting a role for C09.RCO in lobed-leaf formation. Together, these results identify C09.RCO as a candidate regulator of lobed-leaf formation in Siberian kale and indicate that promoter variation is associated with increased C09.RCO expression and the lobed-leaf phenotype, providing a basis for further investigation of the molecular mechanisms underlying leaf margin development in Brassicaceae crops.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: To compare the short-term outcomes of patients undergoing knee needle arthroscopy versus conventional arthroscopy for partial meniscectomy. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent primary arthroscopic partial meniscectomy using either needle or conventional arthroscopy for isolated meniscal tears between October 2021 and April 2025. Patient reported outcome measures included Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score - Jr (KOOS Jr), Euro Quality of Life (QOL), Global Physical Health Score (GPH), Global Mental Health Score (GMH), and the North American Spine Society (NASS) Patient Satisfaction Index measured at baseline (T0), 84 (T1), 168 (T2), and 336 (T3) days postoperatively. Complications within 30 days of surgery were recorded. A linear-mixed model (LMM), a logistic regression model, and a responder analysis were performed to assess statistical and minimal clinically important difference (MCID) significance. RESULTS: A total of 581 arthroscopies (160 needle and 421 conventional) were performed among 574 patients. Needle arthroscopy was associated with statistically significantly greater KOOS Jr improvements at T1 (Δ 8.33; p < 0.0001), T2 (Δ6.61; p = 0.0007), and T3 (Δ10.86; p < 0.0001). Similar early advantages were seen in QOL and GPH, with QOL higher in the needle group at T1 (p < 0.0001) and T3 (p = 0.008), and GPH higher at T1 (p < 0.0001), T2 (p = 0.034), and T3 (p = 0.002). These differences were clinically meaningful, with adjusted MCID odds ratios (adjORs) statistically significantly favoring needle arthroscopy for KOOS Jr at T1 (adjOR = 2.03; p = 0.0214) and T3 (adjOR = 4.22; p = 0.0002), and for QOL (adjOR = 2.36; p = 0.0022) and GPH (adjOR = 2.6; p = 0.0009) at T1. Two (1.3%) and 12 (2.9%) complications were reported in the needle and conventional groups, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Needle arthroscopy was associated with statistically and clinically improved short-term patient-reported outcomes compared with conventional arthroscopy for partial meniscectomy, with a low observed rate of short-term complications. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

papers.abstract_full: Drought is a major abiotic stress that limits wheat productivity and yield stability. Drought adaptation in wheat is a complex quantitative trait governed by multiple genes and quantitative trait loci (QTLs) and is strongly influenced by developmental stage, drought intensity and duration, and environmental conditions. In recent years, QTL mapping, genome-wide association studies (GWAS), and functional genomics have identified numerous loci and candidate genes associated with drought adaptation. However, substantial differences among studies in mapping populations, environmental conditions, and phenotyping methods have resulted in numerous dispersed, often minor-effect loci, many of which lack independent validation, thereby limiting their utility for gene cloning and molecular breeding. To address this gap, we systematically integrated 199 drought-related QTLs, 512 GWAS-associated loci, and 45 drought-responsive genes into a unified framework and anchored them to the wheat reference genome (IWGSC RefSeq v1.0). Based on positional co-localization and reproducibility across independent studies, we further delineate 32 drought-related QTL-rich clusters (QRCs). We further organized these loci within three interconnected drought-response strategies-drought escape, drought avoidance, and drought tolerance-and summarized the underlying genetic and molecular regulatory networks. Finally, we discuss future opportunities for identifying major-effect loci, candidate genes, and favorable alleles and for applying marker-assisted selection (MAS) to improve drought adaptation and yield stability in wheat. This review provides an integrated framework for understanding the genetic architecture of drought adaptation in wheat and for prioritizing robust loci, candidate genes, and breeding targets for drought-adaptation improvement.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Depersonalisation-derealisation (DPDR) is associated with trauma, but the relationship between conflict-related adverse experiences and DPDR remains unclear. The present study examined armed conflict-related trauma exposures, adverse childhood experiences, trauma-related comorbid psychopathology, and trauma appraisals as predictors of DPDR. METHODS: Analyses were conducted on data from 562 Colombian adults exposed to armed conflict across three waves, over 18 months. Three generalised linear mixed modelling frameworks were used: a two-step hurdle, including (i) a logistic model after recoding DPDR as binary, and (ii) a positive-part Gamma mixed model on non-zero DPDR scores; (iii) a Tweedie model. Predictors were entered sequentially as: Trauma exposure, adverse childhood experiences, DPDR-specific covariates, and trauma appraisals. RESULTS: Across all models, armed conflict-related trauma exposure variables and adverse childhood experiences were not independently associated with DPDR, while non-DPDR dissociative experiences showed significant and positive associations with DPDR. Trauma appraisals did not predict DPDR presence or severity. CONCLUSIONS: This was the first study to investigate DPDR in adults exposed to continuous and cumulative trauma related to armed conflict. Findings suggest that, in this population, DPDR was associated with broader dissociative experiences but not with cumulative trauma exposure or trauma appraisals, with important implications for theory and practice.

papers.abstract: Diabetes, a pervasive chronic disease that dysregulates glucose metabolism, presents an intricate web of systemic inflammatory complications. Yet this relationship remains controversial and poorly understood, lacking robust evidence from large-scale data. In this study, we used data from multiple large-scale Genome-wide Association S…
papers.abstract_full: Diabetes, a pervasive chronic disease that dysregulates glucose metabolism, presents an intricate web of systemic inflammatory complications. Clinical observations have suggested an association between diabetes and iridocyclitis (anterior uveitis, the most prevalent form of uveitis in European countries). Yet this relationship remains controversial and poorly understood, lacking robust evidence from large-scale data. In this study, we used data from multiple large-scale Genome-wide Association Studies to investigate the causal relationship between type 1 diabetes (T1D) (odds ratio per 2-fold increase in T1D incidence = 1.058, P MR = 1.36 × 10-42; P LDSC = 0.02) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) (P MR = 0.639; P LDSC = 0.47) with iridocyclitis. Through multi-omics data, we explored the shared genetic architecture of T1D and iridocyclitis at the levels of DNA, methylation, transcriptomics, proteomics and metagenomics. For T1D-iridocyclitis, we prioritized four pleiotropic genes (e.g., PRCC and FUT2) and a shared gut microbiota feature (Parabacteroides) that contribute to the pathogenesis of both conditions. For T2D-iridocyclitis, no such high-level pleiotropic evidence was observed. Finally, through univariable and multivariable Mendelian randomization, we investigated the relationship between diabetes-free glycemic phenotypes and iridocyclitis. We found that genetically predicted relatively higher fasting insulin and lower 2-h glucose levels were associated with a reduced risk of iridocyclitis. Overall, this study elucidates the causal link between diabetes and iridocyclitis, providing insight into their shared molecular mechanisms and potential avenues for preventive clinical strategies, and drawing attention to the often-overlooked clinical entity of "Type 1 diabetes-related iridocyclitis".

papers.abstract_full: Epistasis plays a crucial role in explaining missing heritability in complex traits, yet most detection methods fail to effectively capture local and global interaction patterns and long-range dependencies critical to complex trait architecture. We propose Epiformer that leverages genome language model Evo 2 to capture long-range dependencies from genetic background, and a dual-channel network to jointly model local and global epistasis and additive effects. Epiformer can identify key SNPs and their interactions from complex genomic data to empower phenotype prediction with interpretability, which reinforces epistasis detection. Epiformer performs robustly across species, revealing biologically meaningful patterns and offering new insights into genetic architecture.

papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: With the development of high-throughput sequencing technologies, microbiome data play an increasingly important role in pathological analysis and disease prediction. papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: With the development of high-throughput sequencing technologies, microbiome data play an increasingly important role in pathological analysis and disease prediction. However, microbiome data are typically characterized by high dimensionality, small sample sizes, and compositional constraints, which present challenges to conventional statistical methods, particularly in studies of specific diseases with limited sample sizes. METHODS: Motivated by these challenges, this paper develops an adaptive Bayesian transfer learning framework built upon the Bayesian Compositional Generalized Linear Mixed Model (BCGLMM). The proposed framework integrates a power-prior-based adaptive Bayesian transfer learning with BCGLMM, which enables information borrowing from a related source dataset while accounting for compositional constraints, phylogenetic relatedness among taxa, and dependence among samples in high-dimensional microbiome data. By adopting an adaptive transfer parameter, the framework can adjust the contribution of source information according to the compatibility between the source and target datasets, thereby improving robustness and reducing the risk of negative transfer. RESULTS: Systematic simulation studies show that the proposed Bayesian transfer learning methods generally achieve better predictive performance than target-only, pooled, and existing transfer-learning competitors, especially when the target sample size is limited and related source data are available. Compared with the fixed-transfer method, Adaptive BTL-CGLMM maintains more stable performance under increasing source-target discrepancy, different dimensions, varying sample sizes, and heterogeneous covariance structures. Real gut microbiome applications, including body mass index (BMI) prediction, type 2 diabetes (T2D) diagnosis, and colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosis, further demonstrate that the proposed methods improve prediction by borrowing useful auxiliary information from related source datasets. The microbial taxa identified by Adaptive BTL-CGLMM are also consistent with existing biological findings, supporting the interpretability of the proposed framework. CONCLUSION: This study provides an adaptive Bayesian transfer learning framework for high-dimensional microbiome data analysis with limited target sample sizes. By enabling knowledge transfer under compositional constraints, the proposed method improves predictive performance and robustness across varying data settings, thereby enhancing phenotype prediction and disease diagnosis in small-sample microbiome studies.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVES: To identify shared genetic susceptibility to ulcerative colitis (UC) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and the cell types and genes that may link these diseases. METHODS: We integrated genetic association data from populations of European ancestry with evidence on gene regulation and gene expression in tissues and individual cells. This approach assessed shared genetic susceptibility and prioritized relevant cell types and genes across complementary sources of evidence. We also examined patterns of coordinated gene expression in B cells to provide additional biological context for each disease. Additional analyses examined the consistency of prioritization across analytical settings. RESULTS: UC and RA showed a positive genome-wide genetic correlation (r_g = 0.1591, P = 5.77 × 10⁻4). Eighteen genomic regions showed significant correlations, including 11 positive and seven negative correlations. Tissue analyses implicated intestinal and immune tissues. B cells were the only cell type meeting the primary selection criteria. IRF5, MMEL1 and TYK2 emerged as shared candidate genes supported by genetic association and gene regulatory evidence in both diseases. All three remained eligible under a stricter threshold for shared genetic signals in the analysis that included all tissues. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating genetic, regulatory, and single-cell evidence identified B cells and three candidate genes as priorities for understanding the shared susceptibility to UC and RA. These findings provide a basis for investigating shared immune pathways and potential therapeutic targets for both diseases. Further functional studies can clarify their biological roles and therapeutic relevance. Key Points • UC and RA share genetic susceptibility with heterogeneous effect directions across genomic regions. • B cells met the primary prioritization criteria, although selection was sensitive to analytical choices. • IRF5, MMEL1, and TYK2 were prioritized by shared association and matched bilateral colocalization. • Separate UC and RA B cell networks provided transcriptional context without establishing shared causal mechanisms.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Psychiatric and neurodegenerative conditions have both shared and distinct symptomatology, but the brain mechanisms underlying diagnostic similarities and differences remain unclear. METHODS: Using genome-wide association data, we analyzed 12 psychiatric disorders and four neurodegenerative diseases, assessing polygenic overlap, shared loci, and genetic causal relationships linking their genetic latent factors with 3,935 brain imaging-derived phenotypes (IDP). RESULTS: Using genomic structural equation modeling, we identified an internalizing factor (F1), an addiction factor (F2), a factor related to schizophrenia and bipolar disorder (F3), a neurodevelopmental factor (F4), and a factor related to Alzheimer's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (F5). These showed shared transcriptomic enrichments for frontal and anterior cingulate cortical regions, while F1-specific depletion in substantia nigra and F3-specific enrichment in nucleus accumbens appeared to be specific. Fine-mapping identified 99 variants, including shared loci (e.g., VRK2: F1, F2, F3; TSHZ3: F1, F2; TCF4: F1, F3) and factor-specific loci (e.g., DRD2-F2; SCN2A-F3; FOXP2-F4; TNIP1-F5). The brain-wide analysis of fine-mapped loci identified 1,480 IDP associations (false discovery rate q<0.05). Among these, BANK1 rs1813006, related to F2, was associated to >400 brain IDPs (mostly related to cortical area, cortical grey-white contrast, cortical thickness, and regional and tissue volume). Similarly, MOBP rs1768190 related to F5 was associated with >200 brain IDPs, with about half of them related to cortical thickness. CONCLUSIONS: The present study provides new insights into cross-diagnostic mechanisms linking genetic variation and molecular changes to the brain structural and functional variation across psychiatric and neurodegenerative conditions.

papers.abstract_full: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has a complex genetic architecture, and the regulatory transcripts underlying common-variant associations with ASD risks remain incompletely resolved. We integrated ASD genome-wide association summary statistics with genetically predicted expression across 29 GTEx v8 tissues using Joint-Tissue Imputation (JTI) and FUSION, followed by summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), regional conditional/joint analysis, colocalization and comparison with external ASD molecular evidence. All-tissue false-discovery-rate correction identified 264 significant JTI gene-tissue associations representing 64 genes and 561 FUSION associations representing 128 genes, with an overlap of 40 genes between JTI and FUSION and 152 unique genes in the union set. Brain eQTL and mQTL SMR identified 22 and 21 significant probes, respectively, while analyses across 16 non-brain tissues identified 59 significant probe-tissue associations. TWAS signals converged at 17q21.31. Conditional/joint FUSION retained only the Brain Cerebellar Hemisphere MAPT-AS1 model among 353 significant associations in the primary regional analysis, with the same model retained in an extended-window sensitivity analysis. BrainMeta-ASD colocalization was completed for 23 probes; none met the prespecified criterion for strong colocalization, and MAPT showed the highest PP·H4 (0.5052). Among the 152 union genes, 82 were supported by at least one of the Huang, Matoba or Gandal studies and 15 by at least two; MAPT and XRN2 were the only genes supported by all three data sets. MAPT-AS1 was supported by Matoba et al. in H-MAGMA analysis and is classified as a Category 2 gene in SFARI Gene, while Walker et al. provided additional developmental-brain context through prenatal-brain TWAS. These findings prioritize 17q21.31 as an ASD-associated locus supported across multiple genetic and regulatory evidence layers.

papers.abstract_full: We hypothesized that a shortened gestation length (GL) in Japanese Black cattle operates as a discrete maternal qualitative trait. To examine this, we compared the statistical fit of a linear mixed model (LMM, continuous trait) and a generalized linear mixed model (GLMM, binary trait) for GL analysis using a sire-dam model approach. The practical threshold for defining a shortened GL in the GLMM was determined to be ≤ 280 days. While the LMM was dominated by high residual and sire variances, the GLMM estimated higher dam variance than sire variance, supporting our hypothesis. Analysis of fixed effects suggested that lower parity and summer heat stress act as potential environmental triggers for these shortened GL events. A genome-wide association study (GWAS) using SNP data from 52 multiparous cows categorized into "short-GL" (n = 23, at least one delivery ≤ 280 days) and "normal-GL" (n = 29) groups identified significant peaks on bovine chromosome 6 (BTA6), where the lead SNPs were located within janus kinase and microtubule interacting protein 1 (JAKMIP1).

papers.abstract_full: Autumn sowing of spring oat in Central Europe improves yield and agronomic performance with genomic analyses highlighting VRN1- and VRN3-linked loci as breeding targets for winter resilience. Milder winters in Central Europe enable autumn sowing of spring oats, but risks and benefits still largely remain unclear. To address this knowledge gap, a panel of 250 spring oat lines was seeded in autumn and spring across five European sites over two seasons using unreplicated augmented designs with ten replicated controls. Winterkill varied by site, occurring in four experiments (including complete loss in one site-year), primarily due to insufficient snow cover and frost durations of more than four days between - 5 and - 8 °C. Canopy damage (CAN, scored with Canopeo app) had a heritability estimate of 0.55. Across all experiments, autumn sowing increased grain yield by 5-79% compared to spring sowing, driven by advanced development, lower mildew infection and extended tillering, though associated with higher lodging. GWAS (GAPIT3; 14,614 SNPs) identified 17 robust MTAs for winter hardiness, clustering on chromosomes 2D (novel), 4A and 4D (overlapping with VRN1), 6D, and 7D (near VRN3). Genomic prediction accuracy for CAN was 0.66. Based on our observations, we suggest that breeding should prioritize region-specific trials, winter oat crosses, and genomic selection to mitigate mycotoxin/lodging risks while exploiting yield gains in autumn sown oat.

papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a life-threatening mental disorder with high mortality and morbidity due to its various health complications. While observational studies have highlighted the role of alcohol consumption in the risk of ischemic stroke (IS), the contribution of shared genetic factors remains unclear. papers.abstract_full: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a life-threatening mental disorder with high mortality and morbidity due to its various health complications. While observational studies have highlighted the role of alcohol consumption in the risk of ischemic stroke (IS), the contribution of shared genetic factors remains unclear. Our study used cross-trait Multi-trait Analysis of GWAS (MTAG) to investigate the shared genetic architecture underlying AUD and IS using genome-wide association studies (GWAS) summary statistics for alcohol use disorder (N = 500,348) and ischemic stroke (N = 1,296,908) from the FinnGen and GIGASTROKE databases. Local Analysis of Variant Association (LAVA) identified nine loci exhibiting significant positive and negative genetic correlation after Bonferroni correction. We further identified 19 independent genome-wide significant variants (P < 5 × 10- 8), among which one variant (rs12979469) mapped to SLC44A2 showed evidence of association with both traits. Gene-based analysis via MAGMA also supports SLC44A2 as a shared gene. Fine-mapping and colocalization further identified additional candidate genes, including CDK6 and RASIP1, which were supported by cross-trait analysis (CPASSOC P < 5 × 10- 8) but showed weaker evidence in single-trait GWAS. Summary data-based Mendelian Randomization (SMR) revealed significant associations between the expression of ABO and NBEAL1 and IS in tibial artery tissue (PSMR = 4.28 × 10⁻⁶, PHEIDI > 0.05), whereas no significant association was observed in brain tissues for AUD. Tissue enrichment analysis by GTEx further supports these findings, showing significant enrichment of AUD in brain tissues but nominal significance of IS in tibial artery tissues. Together, these findings suggest that the genetic overlap between AUD and IS is more consistent with variant-level pleiotropy rather than a shared gene expression or tissue-specific mechanism. Overall, our findings highlight SLC44A2, CDK6, and RASIP1 as candidate genes associated with both IS and AUD, and provide insights into the complex genetic relationship between AUD and IS.

papers.abstract_full: High kernel moisture content (KMC) at harvest impedes mechanized harvesting of maize and increases production costs. As a complex trait influenced by both genetic and environmental factors, kernel moisture dynamics can be quantified using three key metrics: KMC, kernel dehydration rate (KDR), and area under the dry-down curve (AUDDC). Here, we evaluated the dynamic changes of kernel moisture across five consecutive stages in a KD recombinant inbred line population across five environments. KMC was measured every 5 days from 34 to 58 days after pollination (DAP), and KDR and AUDDC were calculated based on these measurements. Quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping identified 100 non-redundant QTLs, mainly located at distal chromosomal regions. Of these, we prioritized environmentally stable QTLs and 9 high-confidence pleiotropic candidate regions controlling all 3 kernel dehydration traits, alongside trait-specific loci unique to KMC (11), KDR (28), and AUDDC (4). Meanwhile, combined with RNA-seq data and published literature, we further identified 982 genes differentially expressed between the parental lines at the late stage of kernel development within these 100 QTL intervals. The colocalization of our QTLs with meta-QTLs (11 for GDR and 34 for GWC) revealed 13 high-confidence conserved genomic regions, among which 2 prioritized candidate genes (Zm00001d002455 and Zm00001d005798) were identified. Our study integrated QTL mapping, genome-wide association studies, and transcriptomic analysis to identify high-confidence pleiotropic QTLs and key candidate genes regulating maize kernel moisture, revealing the genetic architecture of moisture dynamics and supporting the breeding of fast-dehydrating maize varieties.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Electrically evoked compound action potential thresholds (TECAP) are quick, accessible, and objective measurements used to evaluate the electrode-to-neuron interface in cochlear implant recipients. While TECAP levels are assumed to covary with electrode position, limited sensitivity of previous electrode localization methods has thus far complicated a detailed analysis of this relationship. This study utilized high-resolution cone-beam computed tomography (CT) and a validated algorithm in order to reevaluate the relationship between electrode position and threshold profiles. METHODS: Intra-operative TECAPs and CT scans from 16 adult recipients of Cochlear Nucleus Contour Advance arrays were retrospectively analyzed. Electrode-to-modiolar wall distances (EMDs), electrode-to-Rosenthal's canal distances (ERDs) and mid-modiolar axis distances were determined and correlated with the threshold profiles. RESULTS: Linear regression analysis on a per subject basis confirmed that TECAP significantly increased with EMD and ERD. Electrode-toRosenthal's canal distances yielded higher R2 values than EMD in 13 of 16 subjects and demonstrated near-perfect correlation in 3 individuals (R2 > 0.8, P < .001). Substantial inter-subject variability was also observed in regression slopes and intercepts, which may partly reflect subject-specific neural health. A linear mixed model accounting for this variability was fitted and explained 69.4% of the total variance (R2> 0.694, P < .001). CONCLUSION: The results from this study suggest that TECAP profiles are associated with mediolateral electrode position and are possibly affected by subject-specific differences in neural health. Incorporating electrode position from specialized CT analysis algorithms into neural health measures may help isolate the neural aspects and enable novel therapeutic applications.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: To explore the effects of combining intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) and transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) on corticospinal excitability and plasticity in healthy subjects. METHODS: This was a single-blind, sham-controlled, 2 × 2 within-subject crossover study with two factors: the timing of combined stimulation (Session) and the type of taVNS. taVNS and iTBS were given either sequentially (1 h of taVNS, then iTBS) or simultaneously, with real or sham taVNS in each session (four sessions in total). Motor cortex excitability and plasticity were assessed with TMS immediately before and after the combined stimulation. RESULTS: Twelve subjects (mean age 29.1 ± 4.6 years; 7/12 females) were enrolled. A linear mixed model on the Δslope (post- minus pre-stimulation slope) of the input-output (I/O) curve showed a significant main effect of taVNS condition (p = 0.021): real taVNS reduced the slope after iTBS, whereas sham did not. Consistently, at the two highest intensities (140% and 160% RMT) MEP responses were significantly lower under real than sham taVNS. CONCLUSIONS: In healthy subjects, combining taVNS with iTBS attenuated corticospinal excitability as shown by the decrease of the I/O slope. This pattern might reflect a homeostatic constraint on synaptic plasticity. SIGNIFICANCE: To our knowledge, this is the first study to examine the effects of combining taVNS and iTBS on human motor cortex excitability and plasticity. These findings may inform the design of combined neuromodulation protocols, an approach that warrants further investigation in specific populations, such as individuals with neurological disorders characterized by synaptic dysfunction.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Molecular quantitative trait locus analysis can nominate genes for vascular dementia (VaD), but association alone does not identify the transcript underlying a disease signal. We assessed candidates using independent outcome replication and regional analyses. METHODS: We used summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) with eQTLGen Phase I blood expression data and FinnGen R13 VaD. Of 19,250 annotated probes, 15,785 were eligible before outcome matching and 15,631 formed the tested family after outcome quality control. Experiment-wide discoveries underwent independent outcome replication in UK Biobank (GCST90473240), regional colocalization, heterogeneity in dependent instruments (HEIDI) testing, and BrainMeta version 2 cortex follow-up. RESULTS: Kinesin light chain 3 (KLC3) was the only experiment-wide significant signal (p = 9.79×10-8); LON peptidase N-terminal domain and ring finger 1 (LONRF1) met false discovery rate correction only. KLC3 did not meet the UK Biobank replication criterion (SMR effect estimate = 0.095, 95% CI: -0.214 to 0.404; p = 0.547). The KLC3 expression quantitative trait locus peak (rs9749618) differed from the FinnGen VaD peak (rs429358, apolipoprotein E [APOE] ε4). Under a model allowing one causal variant per trait, colocalization favored distinct regional signals (PP3≈1; negligible PP4 across tested priors). Blood HEIDI results differed between implementations; cortex analyses did not provide convergent transcript support. LONRF1 colocalization was sensitive to the prior. No candidate met all criteria in the study-specific evidence framework. DISCUSSION: Independent outcome replication and regional analyses refined interpretation of the expression screen. Under the current data and models, KLC3 was not supported as the transcript underlying the VaD signal. Non-replication does not establish absence of KLC3 biology, and the complex APOE region requires cautious attribution.

papers.abstract_full: Thousand-grain weight (TGW) is a primary determinant of grain yield in bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) and exhibits high broad-sense heritability, making it a critical target for genetic improvement. In this study, we evaluated TGW in a panel of 120 modern bread wheat cultivars across two consecutive growing seasons, and conducted whole-genome resequencing aligned to the gap-free Chinese Spring telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome. Quality filtering yielded 6,313,343 high-confidence, independent single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). Integrating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) across three mixed linear models with selective sweep scans based on population differentiation statistics (Fst), nucleotide diversity ratios (Pi), and cross-population composite likelihood ratio (XP-CLR) tests mapped a major candidate gene, TaPTC52, within a 646.3 to 646.8 Mb interval on chromosome 5A. This gene encodes protochlorophyllide-dependent translocon component 52. We also detected a putative minor candidate gene encoding a sesquiterpene synthase on chromosome arm 2AS. Haplotype analysis revealed that a regulatory SNP at Chr5A: 646,781,924 bp, located 24.4 kb upstream of the TaPTC52 transcription start site, underlies the divergence between the favorable Hap1 and the alternative Hap2. Accessions carrying Hap1 with the T allele produced significantly higher TGW than those carrying Hap2 with the C allele (P < 0.0001). In silico analyses revealed that the T-to-C transition in Hap2 disrupts a canonical W-box cis-regulatory element and abolishes predicted binding affinity for WRKY transcription factors. Crucially, quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) confirmed that accessions harboring Hap1 exhibited significantly elevated TaPTC52 transcript levels compared with Hap2 (P < 0.0001), which positively correlated with TGW. Pedigree tracking revealed that Hap1 reached a frequency approaching 90% in modern elite lines derived from founder parents Zhoumai 16 and Zhoumai 22 through strong positive selection, whereas Hap2 was predominantly retained in direct lineages of Bainong Aikang 58. Together, these findings provide novel insights into the genetic and transcriptional regulation of TaPTC52 in governing grain weight and provide diagnostic functional markers for marker-assisted selection (MAS) and targeted parental selection in wheat breeding programs.

papers.title: Swine inflammation and necrosis syndrome as a systemic vascular-inflammatory disorder: an integrative review.
papers.abstract: Swine Inflammation and Necrosis Syndrome (SINS) is an increasingly recognised condition in pigs characterised by inflammatory and necrotic alterations at multiple anatomical sites, including the tail, ears, teats, coronary bands, heels and claws. papers.abstract_full: Swine Inflammation and Necrosis Syndrome (SINS) is an increasingly recognised condition in pigs characterised by inflammatory and necrotic alterations at multiple anatomical sites, including the tail, ears, teats, coronary bands, heels and claws. Its simultaneous occurrence at anatomically distant body regions, its presence at birth and the histopathological evidence of vascular inflammation and thrombosis support the concept that SINS is not primarily a local or mechanically induced disorder, but reflects a systemic endogenous process. This review integrates clinical, pathological, transcriptomic, metabolomic, genetic and field evidence to propose SINS as a systemic vascular-inflammatory syndrome centred on the gut-liver-vascular axis. A proposed pathophysiological model links dysbiosis, impaired intestinal barrier function and translocation of microbe-associated molecular patterns to hepatic inflammatory activation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, coagulation disturbances and microcirculatory impairment. Transcriptomic findings support this model by revealing alterations in genes associated with acute-phase responses, inflammation, oxidative stress, vascular regulation and metabolism in the liver. Genetic studies further indicate moderate heritability, breed and sire effects, and a complex polygenic architecture involving immune, metabolic and vascular pathways. Recent European field studies support the reproducibility of SINS under commercial conditions and show that early-life SINS is associated with later tail integrity and tail lesions. The available evidence supports a phase-based model describing age-related changes in clinical expression and associated systemic alterations, while the precise temporal relationships between inflammatory, metabolic and vascular processes remain incompletely resolved. Practical implications include the need for integrated prevention strategies targeting genetics, feeding, water supply, thermoregulation, transition management and early detection. Overall, SINS may represent a previously under-recognised biological contributor to impaired tissue integrity and welfare problems in modern pig production.

papers.abstract_full: Mapping genetic effects on distal genes and regulatory programs is essential for understanding how genetic variation influences complex diseases; yet trans -QTL discovery remains limited by weak effect sizes, extensive multiple testing and poor reproducibility. Here, we introduce TransMap , a generalizable computational framework that combines multi-scale trans -QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve the discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Beyond individual trans -eGenes, TransMap constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes that account for background expression variation to improve the detection of weak, coordinated distal genetic effects. Across a broad range of simulation settings, TransMap achieved 9.2-36.7% higher trans -QTL discovery power than existing methods while maintaining well-controlled type I error rates. We applied TransMap to bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomic profiles from the aging human brain in the ADSP Functional Genomics Consortium (FunGen-AD), further integrating proteomic, glycoproteomic and metabolomic biomarker measurements (average N= 476 donors). Genome-wide fine-mapping of TransMap single-gene and program-level QTL yielded variant annotations with 2.75-2.88x heritability enrichment across 57 complex diseases and traits (average N= 307K), with complementary heritability information captured across regulatory scales. Multi-phenotype colocalization identified 49,532 trans -regulatory events supported by shared genetic signals with cis -eQTL or biomarker-QTL, including 1,825 candidate cis-trans-biomarker regulatory configurations. TransMap further revealed an asymmetric cross-cell-type regulatory architecture in which neuronal cis -regulatory signals preferentially associate with coordinated glial trans -regulatory responses, supported by co-culture experiments and spatial transcriptomics. Alzheimer's disease (AD) GWAS-prioritized colocalization identified trans -regulatory associations in 115 AD-associated loci, including a KNOP1 cis -eQTL associated in trans with a microglial regulatory program containing MS4A4E , with additional support from statistical mediation analysis. TransMap provides a multi-scale, cell-type-resolved atlas of trans -regulatory variation and a generalizable framework for elucidating the regulatory architecture of complex diseases.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Despite extensive knowledge of how degeneration-related structural changes affect the compressive properties of the meniscus, the associated tribological changes remain poorly understood. Moreover, both functionalities have largely been investigated independently, leaving a knowledge gap regarding possible interrelationships. The aim of this study was to elucidate how alterations in meniscus biomechanical and structural properties affect the tissues tribological properties. METHODS: Human menisci with varying degrees of degeneration were collected from patients undergoing total knee replacement surgery. The compressive meniscus properties were determined using established indentation and compression tests, while the tribological properties were analyzed under simulated gait conditions. Macroscopic as well as microscopic degeneration was assessed by means of Pauli scoring and quantitative histology of glycosaminoglycan, collagen and proteoglycan-4 content. Statistically, linear mixed model analysis and Spearman correlation were applied. RESULTS: Higher macroscopic degeneration severity was associated with both increased friction (ρ = 0.30-0.32, p < 0.05) and reduced compressive stiffness (ρ = 0.30, p < 0.05). Increased friction coefficients were significantly associated with lower initial elastic properties (ρ = 0.30-0.42, p < 0.05) and higher viscoelastic relaxation behavior (ρ = 0.30-0.35, p < 0.05). DISCUSSION: Degenerative changes in the meniscus manifest themselves in a coupled tribological-functional impairment. The interaction between altered friction and compressive properties could represent a mutually reinforcing, degeneration-promoting feedback loop. To prevent a potential function-driven vicious cycle, disease modifying therapies may target the meniscus' dual functionality in gonarthrosis progression.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung function are highly heritable, but for most genome-wide association study (GWAS) loci, the effector gene and the lung cell type in which it acts are unknown. Single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) offer a way to resolve the cell types in which regulatory variants act. RESULTS: We integrated a multi-ancestry GWAS of the ratio of forced expiratory volume in one second to forced vital capacity (FEV1/FVC; Shrine et al., n = 588,452) with single-cell lung eQTLs across 38 cell types (Natri et al., n = 114) by colocalization. We identified 20 candidate colocalizations (posterior probability of a shared causal variant > 0.7) for 13 genes in nine cell types, predominantly epithelial and immune. The two strongest signals localized DSP, an established COPD effector gene, and NRP2, a candidate effector gene, to alveolar type 2 epithelial cells; only these two colocalizations remained supported under a more conservative shared-effect prior. Both signals, together with FAM13A, were also detectable in bulk lung eQTLs, whereas most remaining loci colocalized only in the single-cell analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Single-cell eQTL colocalization resolves the alveolar epithelium as a cellular context for DSP and nominates NRP2 as a candidate lung function effector gene in the same compartment, highlighting the additional cellular resolution provided by single-cell data. The remaining candidate colocalizations warrant replication.

papers.abstract: Population DNA methylome analyses remain largely confined to reference-defined genomic space despite extensive human genetic diversity. A central challenge is therefore to define comparable methylation phenotypes across diverse genomes and map the genetic architecture of methylome variation. Here, using 460 haplotypes from the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium Release 2, we develop two complementary pangenome-based frameworks: one compares methylation within homologous regions while retaining…
papers.abstract_full: Population DNA methylome analyses remain largely confined to reference-defined genomic space despite extensive human genetic diversity. A central challenge is therefore to define comparable methylation phenotypes across diverse genomes and map the genetic architecture of methylome variation. Here, using 460 haplotypes from the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium Release 2, we develop two complementary pangenome-based frameworks: one compares methylation within homologous regions while retaining haplotype-specific structural configuration and CpG content; the other represents CpG island (CGI) variation at homologous loci as sequence-resolved alleles. We identified 47,039 CGI alleles, including 8,040 absent from CHM13; 62% were attributable to structural variants and 31% to small variants. Through local genealogies, we reconstructed CGI gain, loss and turnover, revealing how present-day methylation differences align with CGI evolutionary trajectories. We found that genome-wide, methylation variability was buffered against genetic diversity across more than 90% of the genome, with exceptions at extreme nucleotide diversity and locally around structural variants. Our methylation framework enabled population-scale allele-aware methylation quantitative trait locus (mQTL) mapping into non-reference and structurally complex sequence, where mQTL-associated intervals were enriched. mQTLs linked methylation to transcriptomic phenotypes, population differentiation and complex traits, supporting 8% of population differentially methylated regions and colocalizing with more than half of genome-wide association study loci. Together, our study redefines human methylome analysis and our findings reveal a genome-wide architecture of genetic-epigenetic coupling, reshaping how methylation variation is interpreted across human development and disease.

papers.abstract: Background:  Digestive infectious diseases and cardiovascular diseases may share common genetic, inflammatory and immune-related mechanisms. papers.abstract_full: Background:  Digestive infectious diseases and cardiovascular diseases may share common genetic, inflammatory and immune-related mechanisms. However, the shared genetic architecture between these disease groups, the specific pleiotropic loci involved and the potential contribution of intestinal infectious diseases (IID) to cardiovascular risk remain incompletely understood. Methods We analysed publicly available genome-wide association study summary statistics for 36 binary traits of European ancestry, including 16 digestive infectious disease traits and 20 cardiovascular traits. Univariate linkage disequilibrium score regression was used to estimate SNP-based heritability and prioritise traits. Global and local genetic sharing were evaluated using cross-trait LDSC and SUPERGNOVA. Multi-trait analysis of GWAS, cross-trait sensitivity analyses, FM-summary fine-mapping and Bayesian colocalisation were used to identify and refine pleiotropic loci. Candidate genes and biological functions were investigated using MAGMA, tissue- and cell-type-specific enrichment analyses, transcriptome-wide association analysis and protein-wide association analysis. Bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomisation and two-step mediation analyses using three independent gut microbiome GWAS resources were subsequently performed. Results Sixteen traits passed heritability quality control, yielding 39 trait pairs with significant global genetic correlations after Bonferroni correction. MTAG identified 41 candidate SNP records and 14 trait-pair-specific lead-SNP records representing eight unique SNPs; 39 candidate records and 12 lead records involved IID. Fine-mapping and colocalisation prioritised eight records representing four unique variants. Locus-based gene prioritisation retained 24 candidate genes across four pairs. Gene-set enrichment identified 43 significant trait-pair-GO term associations, and tissue enrichment identified seven significant associations. Transcriptome-wide analyses implicated 21 candidate genes, and proteome-wide analyses identified four associations involving three proteins. After false discovery rate (FDR) correction, forward MR supported associations of IID liability with cardiac arrhythmias, myocardial infarction, atrial fibrillation and flutter, and ischaemic heart disease; reverse MR supported only cardiac arrhythmias to IID. Five positive exploratory microbiota-IID-cardiovascular mediation patterns were described. Only the Oxalobacter-IID-cardiac arrhythmias indirect effect reached unadjusted P < 0.05. Conclusions Digestive infectious diseases, particularly IID, share substantial genetic architecture with cardiovascular diseases. Integrative genetic analyses identified recurrent pleiotropic loci, candidate genes and putative microbiome-mediated pathways linking IID with cardiovascular outcomes. These findings provide testable hypotheses for further functional validation and clinical investigation.

We applied two gene fine-mapping methods, TGVIS and M cTWAS, which jointly model gene expression, splicing and alternative polyadenylation (APA) with direct variant effects, to overall BC, estrogen receptor-negative (ER negative) BC and triple-negative BC (TNBC) in women of Eur…
papers.abstract_full: Most breast cancer (BC) risk loci identified by genome wide association studies lie in noncoding regions, and traditional transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) often prioritize multiple correlated genes per locus. We applied two gene fine-mapping methods, TGVIS and M cTWAS, which jointly model gene expression, splicing and alternative polyadenylation (APA) with direct variant effects, to overall BC, estrogen receptor-negative (ER negative) BC and triple-negative BC (TNBC) in women of European and African ancestry. Using 11 BC-relevant GTEx v10 tissues, we prioritized 31, 13 and 5 candidate causal genes, respectively, in European-ancestry populations. Compared with marginal TWAS, fine-mapping reduced the number of candidate genes per locus by 72 to 88%, and credible sets explained 97 to 100% of significant marginal associations. Seven candidates were not reported by previous GTEx v8-based TWAS, including RIN3, supported only by APA, and NPAT for TNBC. Analyses across 48 tissues and brain cell types revealed brain contributions, including ARHGEF5 in oligodendrocytes. In African-ancestry populations, EN1 was prioritized for ER negative BC and TNBC through variants common in African but rare in European ancestry. These results refine BC susceptibility genes, highlight regulatory mechanisms beyond breast tissue and gene expression, and reveal the challenge of mapping GWAS variants to causal genes with currently available data.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Whether the epigenome constitutes a “code” has been debated for decades, largely qualitatively. We define the codeness of an epigenetic layer as the geometric mean of heritability, causality and sequence-predictability, with heritability measured as the mutual information between mother- and daughter-cell states conditional on DNA sequence, which separates self-templating from sequence-driven re-derivation. Axes were parameterized from published perturbation and sequence-prediction data; DNA-methylation maintenance and de novo rates were measured by reprocessing Hammer-seq data; and promoter readability was tested against persistent silencing in the genome-wide CRISPRoff screen. Of seven mammalian layers, DNA methylation was the most code-like (C = 0.59; 90% assumption-uncertainty interval 0.51–0.65), ranking first in more than 99.9% of Monte-Carlo draws and under all nine aggregation schemes tested. Hammer-seq gave a maintenance rate of 0.933, a de novo rate of 0.007 and an end-of-cycle mother–daughter mutual information of 0.72, essentially unchanged by conditioning on local CpG density. Conditioning on sequence removed most of the apparent heritability of chromatin accessibility and activating histone marks but little of that of the centromeric histone variant CENP-A, separating copied from re-derived layers. The order of the intermediate layers, and the correlation between codeness and predictability, depended on how the axes were combined. Among 18,984 CRISPRoff targets, silencing persisted more often at CpG-island promoters (11.4% versus 2.8%); H3K9me3 did not predict persistence, whereas a cross-validated readability model reached an area under the curve of 0.71. Codeness makes the epigenetic-code question measurable and identifies which parameters must be measured next.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Net blotch (  Pyrenophora teres  ) and spot blotch (  Bipolaris sorokiniana  ) are damaging foliar diseases of barley, but the quantitative trait loci (QTL) reported for resistance are scattered across mapping populations that cannot be compared directly. We meta-analysed 405 unique QTL records from 40 studies and projected the 175 with complete flanking-marker, logarithm of the odds (LOD) and phenotypic variance explained (PVE) data onto a consensus map of 29,016 markers. The Goffinet–Gerber algorithm resolved 27 meta-QTLs (mQTLs), 21 of them shared by both diseases. Meta-analysis narrowed the mean confidence interval 5.14-fold, to 11.83 cM, and raised the average LOD (9.0). Six mQTLs (MQTL1H.1, 1H.2, 4H.1, 6H.1, 6H.2 and 7H.3) met stringent criteria for QTL number, LOD and PVE. All six overlapped marker–trait associations (MTAs) from 24 genome-wide association studies, and 23 of the 27 mQTLs overlapped at least one of 757 unique MTAs. Three major mQTLs (1H.1, 6H.2 and 7H.3) span less than 12 Mb and are the most immediately useful for marker-assisted selection; the others need fine mapping. Annotation of 137 genes in seven representative regions, together with expression data from spot blotch-inoculated barley, identified 175 differentially expressed genes, including receptor-like kinase, resistance-protein-like and defence-related genes, notably in MQTL1H.1, 2H.1 and 3H.1. Candidate-gene data are still missing for three of the six major mQTLs. These regions and genes offer a prioritised resource for breeding barley with combined resistance to both diseases.

papers.abstract_full: Gene-by-environment (GxE) interactions inform where genetics and environment converge to impact human health and disease. However, systematically mapping GxE interactions has been challenging due to the diversity of testable exposures and a lack of scalable approaches to measure the environments cells experience  in vivo . Here, we identified modules of correlated plasma metabolites and proteins and used them as quantitative proxies for environmental exposures experienced by circulating leukocytes. We demonstrated that these proxies are associated with environmentally-modifiable clinical traits such as diet and infection and support broad mapping of gene-by-environment (  G × E ) interactions affecting gene expression and CpG methylation in leukocytes. We identified significant interactions for 95.2% of tested genes and 5.9% of tested methylation sites. These  G × E interactions showed specificity to exposures and cell type. Colocalization analysis further provided links between interactions and complex trait and disease loci. Finally, we expanded  G × E interaction mapping to unexplored cell types using a zero-shot transfer model to predict  G×E interactions in held-out cell types, demonstrating how plasma metabolomics and proteomics can enhance the discovery of  G × E interactions across the body. Altogether, this work provides a systematic multi-omic framework to study how gene regulation is shaped by both the genome and the molecular environments cells experience  in vivo .

papers.abstract_full: Aging is a complex biological process leading to tissue dysfunction, and driven in part by progressive epigenetic drift, widespread transcriptional dysregulation and cellular senescence. Senescent cells (SnCs) accumulate across tissues in a heterogeneous and cell type-specific manner, yet their molecular signatures and spatial organization within native tissue have not been systematically mapped. Here we combined single-nucleus transcriptomic, epigenomic, three-dimensional (3D) genome and spatial profiling to systematically characterize aging of the mouse liver and associated cellular senescence. Aging was marked by hepatocyte loss, immune cell expansion, erosion of repressive H3K9me3 heterochromatin, alteration of 3D genome organization, and activation of stress-response pathways known to promote senescence. Age-associated SnCs were spatially colocalized within discrete inflammatory microenvironments termed SenSpots. Different SenSpots were dominated by distinct hepatocyte senescence states (senotypes), driven by unique transcription factors, and exhibited distinct lobular zonation. Single-cell DNA methylation profiling revealed a subset of immune cells in aged livers with loss of DNA methylation at constitutive heterochromatin and elevated senescence signatures. AAV-mediated, p21-promoter driven  Stat1 deletion in the aged liver selectively suppressed interferon-responsive senescence programs while pharmacological inhibition of MDM2 attenuated senescence-associated inflammatory signatures. Together, these findings reveal that hepatic senescence is not a uniform state but a set of diverse epigenetically reprogrammed, spatially organized, and pharmacologically modifiable inflammatory niches.

papers.abstract: Dissecting the genetic basis of complex traits and pyramiding favorable alleles are central to crop breeding. However, jointly evaluating pleiotropy and epistasis to identify allele combinations that meet multiple breeding objectives remains challenging. papers.abstract_full: Dissecting the genetic basis of complex traits and pyramiding favorable alleles are central to crop breeding. However, jointly evaluating pleiotropy and epistasis to identify allele combinations that meet multiple breeding objectives remains challenging. Here, we present BPEA (Bayesian Pleiotropy and Epistasis Analysis), a Bayesian framework integrating LD-guided QTL interval identification, joint genetic inference and allele-combination assessment. BPEA uses the joint posterior to estimate the posterior probability of simultaneous improvement (PPSI) between allele combinations and ranks them by mean PPSI. In simulations, BPEA improved interval identification and epistatic interaction attribution relative to comparator methods and maintained high precision in shared-signal detection. When epistasis was present, it reduced mean combination-selection regret by 68.4-86.3% relative to a model without interaction terms. Applications to three rapeseed populations identified shared genetic signals and candidate epistatic interactions associated with seed-quality traits. BPEA also prioritized allele combinations for simultaneous reductions in erucic acid and glucosinolate contents and identified complementary parents for cross design. BPEA thus provides a framework for genetic dissection and genomics-guided crop improvement.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Selection and mate allocation shape performance and diversity in future breeding populations. Although numerous criteria for evaluating and selecting crosses exist, few tools offer a unified, scalable framework for different breeding schemes, multi-trait objectives, and diversity management. We present CrossingTools, an open source R package for predicting cross performance and optimising crossing plans using marker genotypes and genetic effects. Crosses can be evaluated based on their expected progeny mean, optimal haploid value, or superior progeny value using segregation (co)variance models for inbred and heterozygous parents with additive and dominance effects. Multi-trait objectives can be defined using economic weight or desired gains indices, while crossing plans can be optimised to balance predicted performance and genomic diversity through optimal cross selection. Efficient C++ subroutines enable large-scale cross evaluation, allowing the screening of entire breeding populations. To demonstrate its application, we simulated a line breeding programme with correlated traits and found that, under genomic selection, superior progeny value and optimal haploid value improved upper-tail progeny performance more strongly than population mean gain and preserved more genetic variance than selection based on expected cross means. The criteria also affected genetic correlations differently as superior progeny value tended to shift correlations in directions favourable to the selection index, optimal haploid value largely maintained correlations, and selection on expected cross means often produced less favourable changes. Optimal cross selection reduced variance depletion at the cost of lower short-term gain. CrossingTools thus offers a framework for integrating progeny prediction, multi-trait selection, and genetic diversity management in plant breeding.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Background  Children with hypophosphataemic rickets (HR) remain short despite conventional treatment. It is still debated when height is lost, and pubertal timing and tempo have rarely been compared with population references. We compared both with Turkish references and described growth through puberty in children with HR of mixed aetiology. Methods  This exploratory retrospective single-centre study included 33 children with HR first seen in 1994–2025. Ages at pubertal onset (breast stage 2 or testicular volume ≥ 4 mL; interval-censored analysis of all patients) and at menarche were compared with Turkish references. Height standard deviation scores (SDS) across pubertal stages were analysed with a linear mixed model, excluding growth hormone-treated children. Results  Mean onset age was 9.68 years in girls and 9.75 years in boys; the differences from the reference were − 0.42 years (95% confidence interval [CI] − 1.25 to 0.38) and − 1.85 years (− 2.86 to − 0.86). Menarche (n = 10, mostly whole-year ages) was 0.95 years (0.40 to 1.49) later than the reference, mainly in girls first seen after onset. In five girls followed from before puberty, the difference in age at menarche was + 0.48 years (− 0.32 to 1.28), and their mean interval from breast stage 2 to menarche was at least 2.80 years (difference from the reference + 1.00 years, − 0.47 to 2.47). In 12 patients with ≥ 2 measurements from stage 2 onwards, height SDS fell by 0.82 (0.44 to 1.19) between stage 2 and near-final height (NFH), yet the five measured at both points gained 14.2–32.4 cm, within or above the reference range. NFH was − 2.88 ± 1.56 SDS (mean ± standard deviation; n = 12) and 1.70 SDS (0.58 to 2.82) below target height (n = 8). Conclusions  Pubertal onset was not delayed and may be early in boys; a slower tempo in girls needs confirmation. In this small cohort, height SDS fell through puberty despite height gains in centimetres within or above the reference range, and NFH remained well below target height.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background.  Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a common failure of fibrocollagenous pelvic support. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) report a sub-genome-wide suggestive association at PCOLCE2 (regional minimum p = 2.5×10⁻⁷), which encodes a secreted regulator of procollagen C-terminal processing, but they do not establish which cell type, which molecular species or which regulatory signal carries the risk.  Methods.  This was a pre-specified study of a five-gene collagen-assembly panel and of one GWAS-suggestive locus, not an unbiased genome-wide screen, and it used public summary-level and single-cell data only; no functional assay was performed. The analysis combined cis-Mendelian randomisation (MR) with fibroblast expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) instruments, colocalisation, the regional causal-inference method CAUSE, stratified fine-mapping across four molecular phenotypes, plasma protein QTL (pQTL) deconvolution, Steiger filtering, a fifteen-endpoint specificity panel, single-cell and pseudo-bulk transcriptomics, and exploratory regulatory annotation.  Results.  Conditional on the sub-genome-wide index signal set out under Background, genetic evidence supports a triangulated statistical causal inference for a fibroblast-lineage cis-regulatory effect at PCOLCE2 that raises POP risk (OR 1.282 per SD, 95% CI 1.112–1.477), with specificity of this cis-regulatory effect to pelvic-floor endpoints, colocalisation (PP4 = 0.954) and a causal rather than shared-confounding architecture (CAUSE ΔELPD = −7.99 ± 1.64). Within a single haplotype block the locus resolves into two functionally decoupled, statistically inferred cis-regulatory profiles (r² = 0.066); the blood-restricted profile controls circulating PCPE-2 but is unrelated to POP, and every variant that raises plasma PCPE-2 falls significantly below the POP effect predicted by a circulating-dosage model. The fibroblast signal also accounts for the locus's bone-density association, which we read as parallel pleiotropy rather than skeletal mediation. PCOLCE2 was expressed selectively in pelvic-floor fibroblasts, and exploratory, under-powered pseudo-bulk analysis (16 versus 5) placed an observed disease-associated expression increment within ECM-remodelling fibroblasts; there the collagen-assembly module was positively but non-significantly displaced (Hedges' g = +0.45, label-shuffling p = 0.38) and only the inhibitor module reached significance, so assembly-biased matrix decay remains a working mechanistic hypothesis.  Conclusions.  Conditional on independent POP GWAS replication — the index signal is sub-genome-wide significant and every inference here depends on it — the disease-relevant signal at this locus is a fibroblast-restricted cis-regulatory effect on PCOLCE2 rather than circulating protein dosage. More generally, the locus shows that apparent gene-level pleiotropy at matrix genes can resolve into functionally decoupled, tissue-restricted cis-regulatory profiles within a single haplotype block — a principle that changes how such GWAS signals should be read and followed up.

papers.abstract: Background:  Hematological traits are closely linked to immune and inflammatory processes implicated in thyroid dysfunction. Although observational studies have reported associations between blood-cell traits and thyroid disorders, whether these relationships reflect causal mechanisms remains unclear. papers.abstract_full: Background:  Hematological traits are closely linked to immune and inflammatory processes implicated in thyroid dysfunction. Although observational studies have reported associations between blood-cell traits and thyroid disorders, whether these relationships reflect causal mechanisms remains unclear. Methods: We performed a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to investigate the causal effects of 25 genetically predicted hematological traits on hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from the UK Biobank. Independent single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were selected as instrumental variables and harmonized before analysis. Causal estimates were primarily obtained using the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method and complemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, simple mode, MR-PRESSO, and MR-robust adjusted profile score (MR-RAPS) analyses. Sensitivity analyses assessed heterogeneity, horizontal pleiotropy, reverse causality, and directionality. Significant findings were replicated using independent FinnGen summary statistics. Multivariable MR and Bayesian colocalization analyses were subsequently performed to investigate significant associations further. Results: Among the 25 hematological traits evaluated, eosinophil-related traits showed the strongest associations with hypothyroidism. Genetically predicted eosinophil counts were associated with an increased risk of hypothyroidism (odds ratio [OR] = 1.25, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.11-1.42, P = 4.0E-04, FDR = 0.002), while combined eosinophil-basophil counts showed similar associations (OR = 1.24, 95% CI: 1.10-1.40, P = 5.0E-04, FDR = 0.002). These findings were consistently replicated in FinnGen and remained significant after adjustment for basophil traits, body mass index, and C-reactive protein in multivariable MR analyses. No significant associations were observed for hyperthyroidism. Bayesian colocalization identified strong evidence of a shared genetic signal at the rs653178 locus on chromosome 12 (PP.H4 = 0.994). Conclusions: This study provides genetic evidence supporting a causal role for eosinophil-related traits in hypothyroidism susceptibility. The consistency of the findings across complementary Mendelian randomization approaches, independent replication, multivariable analyses, and colocalization strengthens the evidence that eosinophil-related immune mechanisms contribute to hypothyroidism susceptibility.

papers.abstract_full: To date, predicting the genetic variance (VG) in biparental crosses has been unreliable. My objective was to determine if predicting VG via tabular analysis, which was developed assuming free recombination and having known VG in founder crosses, is effective even if these unrealistic assumptions are unmet. With line X being developed from the P1/P2 cross, the VG in X/Y was predicted as VX/Y = λ1VP1/Y + λ2VP2/Y, where λ1 was the parental contribution of P1 to X and λ2 was the parental contribution of P2 to X. Simulations involved four founder lines with biallelic marker loci and multiple alleles at quantitative trait loci. The VG in each founder cross was estimated from simulated phenotypic values of N lines under varying heritability (h2). Non-founder lines were developed successively from the founders. Among the 774 non-founder crosses, the mean correlation between the true VG and predicted VG ranged from 0.49 (N = 50 and h2 = 0.20) to 0.70 (N = 400 to 1000 and h2 ≥ 0.50). Overall, the results suggested that tabular analysis is currently the most effective method for predicting VG. papers.abstract_full: Background  The inhibition of NOD-, LRR- and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome is an emerging therapeutic strategy for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Although early clinical trials demonstrate reductions in inflammatory biomarkers, whether these translate into cardiovascular benefit remains uncertain. We investigated the potential efficacy and safety of NLRP3 inhibition using human genetics. Methods  We developed a  cis -genetic instrument for NLRP3 downregulation using C-reactive protein (CRP) associated variants (PResults  Using 14 variants in the  NLRP3 locus, we constructed a genetic instrument that corresponded to a 19% difference in circulating CRP between the extreme percentiles of its distribution. Colocalisation evidence suggested the effects on CRP to be driven by reduced  NLRP3 expression in naïve monocytes (PP.H4=98.7%). In accordance with the expected biological role of NLRP3, genetically proxied NLRP3 downregulation by the constructed instrument was associated with lower IL-18 (β=−0.11; 95%CI, −0.14 to −0.08) and IL-6 (β=−0.15; 95%CI, −0.17 to −0.12) and broadly similar pharmacodynamic effects to the NLRP3 inhibitor ruvonoflast across 8 biomarkers. Genetically proxied NLRP3 inhibition was associated with lower risk of recurrent pericarditis (OR per 19% decrease in CRP, 0.68, 95%CI, 0.58-0.80), but slightly elevated risk of coronary artery disease (OR, 1.06; 95%CI, 1.03–1.08) and peripheral arterial disease (OR, 1.10; 95%CI, 1.04–1.15) and no effect on ischaemic stroke (OR, 0.98; 95%CI, 0.94-1.02). The instrument was also associated with higher carotid-intima-media thickness and a worse cardiometabolic profile with increasing effects on blood pressure, waist-to-hip ratio, LDL cholesterol, and triglycerides. We found no associations with increased risk for prespecified infectious disease outcomes.  Conclusions  A genetic proxy for NLRP3 inflammasome downregulation reproduced key molecular effects of pharmacological NLRP3 inhibition but was not associated with reduced ASCVD risk. Clinical perspective  What is new?  - We developed a genetic proxy of NLRP3 inflammasome downregulation comprising 14 variants within the  NLRP3 locus.  - Mirroring the biology of NLRP3 signaling, genetically proxied NLRP3 downregulation was associated with lower IL-6 and IL-18 concentrations and showed broadly concordant biomarker effects with the oral NLRP3 inhibitor, ruvonoflast. - Despite mimicking pharmacologic NLRP3 inhibition at a biomarker level, genetically proxied NLRP3 downregulation was not associated with reduced lifetime cardiometabolic risk. What are the clinical implications?  - In view of emerging therapeutic efforts to target NLRP3 inflammasome, we could not find human genetic evidence supporting that NLRP3 downregulation could reduce risk of cardiovascular events.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background  Rice is one of the world's most important cereal crops and a major source of food and income for millions of people, especially Nigeria, which has almost reach her self-sufficient production capacity. However, genetic variability significantly influences yield component traits in rice for stability and adaptability. Therefore, this study assessed the genetic variability and trait associations influencing grain yield in upland rice genotypes evaluated under the Akungba Akoko agro-ecology.  Methods  Fourteen genotypes were tested under field conditions in a randomized complete block design at the experimental field of the department of Plant Science and Biotechnology, and data were collected on yield and related agronomic traits, analyzed using GLM models of SPSS version 27.  Result  The analysis of variance revealed highly significant differences among genotypes, confirming the presence of considerable genetic diversity. Plant height, number of tillers, effective tillers, flag leaf length, panicle length, panicle weight, number of grains per panicle, number of spikelets, thousand grain weight, grain length and width, days to panicle initiation, days to maturity, and grain yield per hill all vary significantly among the genotypes. These significant differences suggest considerable genetic variability within the tested genotypes, which is favorable for selection and breeding. Coefficient of variation (CV) provides a measure of experimental precision and variability relative to the mean. Most traits have CV values below 20%, with some lower than 10%, which suggests good experimental consistency. For example: Plant height CV 5.8% (high precision). Number of tillers CV 16.4%. Grain yield CV 25.8%, which is typical for yield traits due to their inherent variability. Estimates of genotypic and phenotypic coefficients of variation indicated that while some traits were strongly under genetic control, others were more sensitive to environmental influence. Grain yield showed positive and significant correlations with key yield components, particularly productive tillers, panicle weight, number of grains per panicle, and thousand-grain weight, highlighting their value as indirect selection criteria. Genetic parameter estimates further demonstrated high heritability (> 90%) for traits such as plant height, number of tillers, panicle weight, and maturity, coupled with high genetic advance values, suggesting strong additive gene action and effective selection potential. Conversely, traits like panicle length exhibited lower heritability, reflecting greater environmental influence. Conclusion The study shows good genetic variability and heritability for most important yield and agronomic traits in upland rice genotypes from this agro-ecology, indicating strong potential for selection and breeding improvements. Traits like panicle weight, grain yield, and tiller number are particularly promising targets for breeders.
