papers.abstract_full: Genetic variation influences brain physiology and disease across cell types and development. We integrated whole-genome sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, and single-nucleus multiome profiling from 231 human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex donors spanning six postconceptional weeks to 92 years. Across 24 brain-related traits, neurodevelopmental and psychiatric genetic risk was enriched in neuronal transcriptomic and chromatin profiles, whereas neurodegenerative risk was enriched in microglia. Thousands of expression, chromatin accessibility, and splicing quantitative trait loci revealed developmental and cell-type-specific regulatory effects. Colocalization linked multiple sclerosis risk to  AHI1 expression in prenatal neurons and problematic alcohol use to  GPX1 expression in postnatal glia. Leveraging dynamic cis-regulatory elements, we identified therapeutic candidates for haploinsufficient neurodevelopmental disorders, including a  SOX5 enhancer whose CRISPR activation increased transcript and protein abundance. Together, these findings establish a publicly accessible genomic resource for resolving the developmental and cellular contexts of genetic risk and identifying therapeutic targets in the human brain.

papers.abstract_full: Background  Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome reflects shared pathophysiology across metabolic, renal and cardiovascular systems, yet circulating proteins with causal effects spanning multiple CKM domains remain unclear. We aimed to identify and prioritize cross-domain candidate proteins using an integrative, dual-platform plasma proteogenomic framework. Methods  We combined genetic causal inference, statistical colocalization, single-cell expression mapping, and structure-based druggability assessment.  Cis -protein quantitative trait loci (  cis -pQTL) instruments were derived from two independent plasma proteomic platforms, UKB-PPP (2,030 proteins with valid cis instruments) and deCODE (1,640 proteins). Genetic causal inference (two-sample Mendelian randomization) was performed against seven CKM-related outcomes across the metabolic (type 2 diabetes [T2D], body mass index [BMI]), renal (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR], chronic kidney disease) and cardiovascular (coronary artery disease, heart failure, stroke) domains. Proteins showing false discovery rate (FDR)-significant associations in at least two CKM domains independently on both platforms were prioritized, and cross-platform directional concordance was evaluated as a robustness measure. Prioritized proteins were followed by colocalization, and characterization using single-cell expression, disease-association and druggability resources. Structural and ligand-efficiency analyses were performed for the leading candidate using its co-crystallized inhibitor complex.  Results  Proteome-wide analysis yielded 9,734 (UKB-PPP) and 8,837 (deCODE) protein-outcome estimates, with 77.9% two-platform directional concordance. Cross-domain prioritization identified six proteins (ARG1, GSTA1, INHBB, ITIH1, NCAN, SHBG), all acting across the metabolic-renal axis. Colocalization provided strong support for GSTA1 with eGFR (posterior probability of a shared causal variant 0.97) and ARG1 with BMI (0.93). Genetically higher GSTA1 was associated with lower eGFR and higher T2D risk, with kidney expression confined to proximal tubule cells. Genetically higher ARG1 was associated with lower BMI and lower T2D risk, consistent with hepatocyte-restricted expression. Both proteins were small-molecule tractable. For GSTA1, the inhibitor-bound structure (PDB 1GSF) showed a deep, enclosed H-site, and three chemotypes with previously reported low-micromolar potency against recombinant hGSTA1-1 (ethacrynic acid and the dietary flavonols fisetin and myricetin) all exceeded the lead-like ligand-efficiency threshold (0.30 kcal mol  -1 per heavy atom).  Conclusions  Using dual-platform proteogenomics, we identify genetically supported cross-metabolic-renal candidate proteins in CKM syndrome, with GSTA1 and ARG1 emerging as the most robust, pharmacologically tractable candidates. These findings nominate actionable targets and mechanistic entry points for CKM syndrome.

Genetically higher ARG1 was associated with lower BMI and lower T2D risk, consistent with hepatocyte-restricted expression.
These findings nominate actionable targets and mechanistic entry points for CKM syndrome.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Purpose. Sugarcane technologies are often evaluated in commercial strip trials with a few crop cuts and limited replication. We asked what Sentinel-2 imagery and georeferenced sampling add to such a trial, and how much independent evidence their dense sampling contains. Methods. A third-ratoon trial under natural nematode infestation (nine strips, three treatments in a repeated sequence) was reconstructed from archived materials: a one-year cloud-screened Sentinel-2 baseline of the normalised difference vegetation index (NDVI), 27 NDVI-stratified crop cuts and 90 nematode points sampled twice. Analyses combined NDVI to yield calibration, residual variograms, a random-strip mixed model, exact permutation and an independently built pre-treatment covariate. Results. A field-scale trend ran along the strip sequence, aliased with treatment position. With an intraclass correlation of 0.25, the 90 points carried the information of 27.7. For the main nematode contrast, p was 0.004 with points as independent, 0.162 in the mixed model and 0.046 to 0.095 by permutation; five defensible strip-level specifications gave 0.023 to 0.61. More points per strip could cut its standard error by at most 12%; 80% power needs about ten strips per treatment. Root Pratylenchus fell by 63 to 67% under both bionematicide treatments. Two pre-treatment covariates, correlated at 0.65, moved a crop-cut contrast from p = 0.176 to 0.048. Conclusion. The digital layer makes a strip trial auditable when the strip is the unit. It densifies sampling but adds no experimental units: with nine strips, the choice of model and covariate carries more of the p-value than the data do.

papers.abstract_full: Background:  Aerospace crews may need to perform physical tasks immediately after hy-pergravity (+Gz) exposure. Strategies to preserve submaximal cardiopulmonary perfor-mance in this window remain limited. Objective: To test whether peripheral skin cooling (PSC) applied during +Gz would attenuate residual effects on submaximal cardiopulmo-nary exercise performance. Methods: Eighteen healthy males completed a randomized crossover protocol on a short-arm human centrifuge. Participants underwent a standard-ized +Gz profile (up to +4 Gz) with bilateral thigh cooling or non-cooled control pads. Immediately after +Gz, cycle ergometry was performed to the first ventilatory threshold (VT1) and to volitional exhaustion. Primary outcomes were oxygen uptake (VO₂) and the body-surface-area-indexed VO₂–mean arterial pressure product at VT1. Results: The change from post-+Gz rest in the indexed VO₂–MAP product at VT1 was larger after PSC (+13.2 ± 24.7 L·mmHg·min⁻¹·m⁻², paired t-test p = 0.037). Absolute VO₂ at VT1 was also higher after PSC, but the .the distribution of differences was non-normal; consequently, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test was employed, which yielded no significant difference. No sig-nificant differences were observed at maximal exertion. Linear mixed models showed no significant Condition × Phase interaction for any primary outcome. The VT1 difference was larger when the control session preceded PSC. Conclusions: Bilateral thigh cooling during +Gz was associated with a larger rise in the indexed VO₂–MAP product from rest to VT1. The effect was modest, confined to submaximal intensity, sensitive to session or-der, and not confirmed by the mixed-model interaction or by absolute VO₂ on the preferred non-parametric test. Further studies are required before operational recommendations can be made.

papers.abstract_full: Background  Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung function are highly heritable, but for most genome-wide association study (GWAS) loci, the effector gene and the lung cell type in which it acts are unknown. Single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) offer a way to resolve the cell types in which regulatory variants act. Results  We integrated a multi-ancestry GWAS of the ratio of forced expiratory volume in one second to forced vital capacity (FEV1/FVC; Shrine et al., n = 588,452) with single-cell lung eQTLs across 38 cell types (Natri et al., n = 114) by colocalization. We identified 20 candidate colocalizations (posterior probability of a shared causal variant > 0.7) for 13 genes in nine cell types, predominantly epithelial and immune. The two strongest signals localized DSP, an established COPD effector gene, and NRP2, a candidate effector gene, to alveolar type 2 epithelial cells; only these two colocalizations remained supported under a more conservative shared-effect prior. Both signals, together with FAM13A, were also detectable in bulk lung eQTLs, whereas most remaining loci colocalized only in the single-cell analysis. Conclusions  Single-cell eQTL colocalization resolves the alveolar epithelium as a cellular context for DSP and nominates NRP2 as a candidate lung function effector gene in the same compartment, highlighting the additional cellular resolution provided by single-cell data. The remaining candidate colocalizations warrant replication.

papers.abstract_full: PURPOSE: Climate change poses a significant public health threat, and the health care sector could contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Operating rooms (ORs) are highly energy-intensive and produce substantial waste, including disposable products and anesthesia services. This study compares the environmental impact and cost-effectiveness of simple operative procedures like carpal tunnel release, ganglion excision, and trigger finger release performed in outpatient procedure rooms (PRs) versus ORs, hypothesizing that PRs are more sustainable and cost-effective. METHODS: This observational study was conducted at a level 2 trauma center in Saskatchewan, Canada. Institutional Research Ethics Board approval was obtained. A total of three OR and six PR surgeries performed by a single surgeon were observed. Data on procedural duration, resource utilization, waste generation, and associated direct costs were systematically collected. Carbon emissions in kilograms of CO2 equivalents (kgCO2e) were estimated using standardized emission factors based on the processing of surgical waste and linens, as well as energy consumption from room lights, surgical lights, and central processing. Statistical analysis was conducted using the statistical software SAS 9.4 (SAS Institute Inc). RESULTS: A single PR procedure produced 1.05 kgCO2e, whereas an OR procedure produced 4.36 kgCO2e. OR procedures generated 18 times more surgical waste and used twice as many linens. Financially, a PR procedure costs $376.78, whereas an OR procedure costs $1,004.28. CONCLUSIONS: Shifting simple operative procedures from ORs to PRs can significantly reduce environmental impact and costs. PR surgeries generated 76% less carbon emissions and 94.5% less surgical waste and were 62.5% less expensive. These findings suggest that outpatient PR settings offer a more sustainable and cost-effective alternative for many simple procedures, contributing to a greener and more economically efficient health care system. TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Economic/decision analysis IIb.

papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Dedicated exposure to plastic and reconstructive surgery (PRS) in undergraduate medical education is limited, with most Canadian medical students receiving no exposure throughout their training. papers.abstract_full: PURPOSE: Dedicated exposure to plastic and reconstructive surgery (PRS) in undergraduate medical education is limited, with most Canadian medical students receiving no exposure throughout their training. The lack of standardized PRS learning objectives leaves graduating medical students unaware of basic PRS principles, emergent presentations, and indications for referral. This study aims to develop a national consensus-based set of undergraduate PRS learning objectives. METHODS: A literature search was conducted to identify PRS learning objectives. The Canadian PRS Undergraduate Medical Education Curriculum Development Working Group, composed of PRS program directors (PDs), family medicine PDs, and surgical educators, was convened to assess the appropriateness of learning objectives for medical students. A 3-round Delphi consensus was completed (January-September 2025). Objectives achieving ≥75% consensus are included in the ratified list of objectives. Institutional research ethics board approval was obtained. RESULTS: Of 70 invited experts, 27 completed survey round 1, with a response rate above 70% in subsequent rounds. Panelists include 14 plastic surgeons across 7 provinces. A total of 56 objectives were included in the initial list of proposed objectives. After 3 rounds, 42 objectives were included in the final list, across the following subdomains: general principles of surgery and reconstruction, upper extremity, skin, burns, breast, craniofacial, and gender-affirming surgery. CONCLUSIONS: A standardized set of PRS learning objectives is available for all Canadian medical students to address current knowledge gaps in medical education. These consensus-based objectives should supplement current resources, such as the existing Medical Council of Canada Examination Objectives, and future plastic surgery-focused education initiatives. INTRODUCTION: L’exposition réservée à la chirurgie plastique et reconstructive (CPR) est limitée en formation médicale prédoctorale, puisque la plupart des étudiants en médecine canadiens n’y sont jamais exposés. En l’absence d’objectifs d’apprentissage normalisés en CPR, les finissants en médecine ne connaissent pas les principes de base de la CPR, les symptômes urgents ni les indications d’envoi en consultation. La présente étude vise à créer un ensemble consensuel national d’objectifs d’apprentissage de la CPR en médecine postdoctorale. MÉTHODOLOGIE: Les chercheurs ont effectué une analyse bibliographique pour répertorier les objectifs d’apprentissage en CPR. Le groupe de travail canadien sur l’élaboration d’un cursus de CPR en médecine prédoctorale, composé de directeurs de programme (DP) en CPR, de DP en médecine familiale et d’éducateurs en chirurgie s’est réuni pour évaluer la pertinence des objectifs d’apprentissage pour les étudiants en médecine. Ils ont participé à une méthode de consensus Delphi en trois tours (de janvier à septembre 2025). Les objectifs qui ont obtenu un consensus d’au moins 75 % ont fait partie de la liste d’objectifs ratifiée. Le comité d’éthique de la recherche de l’établissement a approuvé les résultats. RÉSULTATS: Des 70 experts invités, 27 ont rempli le premier tour du sondage, et le taux de réponse dépassait les 70 % aux tours subséquents. Les répondants étaient formés de 14 chirurgiens plasticiens de sept provinces. Au total, 56 objectifs figuraient dans la liste initiale d’objectifs proposés. Après trois tours, 42 objectifs avaient été retenus dans la liste finale, dans les sous-domaines suivants : principes généraux de la chirurgie et de la reconstruction, membres supérieurs, peau, brûlures, sein, crâne et face et chirurgie d’affirmation de genre. CONCLUSIONS: Un ensemble normalisé d’objectifs d’apprentissage en CPR est désormais à la disposition de tous les étudiants en médecine canadiens afin de combler les lacunes actuelles de la formation médicale. Ces objectifs consensuels devraient compléter les ressources actuelles, tels que les objectifs d’examen du Conseil médical du Canada, ainsi que les futures initiatives en chirurgie plastique.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Loneliness and social isolation are distinct risk factors for depression and other affective disorders but are often conflated. Whether adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) relate differently to the two, and whether this varies across adulthood, is unclear. METHODS: We analysed 24,219 adults from the nationwide 2024 Psychology and Behaviour Investigation of Chinese Residents. Seven ACE domains were assessed with items adapted from the WHO ACE-IQ. Social isolation (three-item structural index, score ≥ 2) and loneliness (two-item functional index, score 2) were defined using indices adapted from the UK Biobank. Adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) were estimated by modified Poisson regression with city-clustered standard errors; a stacked model compared the two outcomes. RESULTS: Social isolation (30.0%) and loneliness (11.0%) overlapped weakly (kappa 0.17). Each additional ACE was associated with higher prevalence of loneliness (PR 1.24, 95% CI 1.20-1.28) and, more weakly, isolation (PR 1.04, 1.01-1.08; ratio of PRs 1.19, 1.17-1.22). All seven domains were associated with loneliness; only emotional abuse, witnessed violence and, marginally, physical abuse were associated with isolation; sexual abuse, household substance use, household mental illness and parental incarceration were not. The association of ≥4 ACEs with loneliness strengthened with age (P for interaction <0.001; PR 2.71, 1.98-3.72, at ≥60 years). LIMITATIONS: The cross-sectional design and retrospectively self-reported ACEs preclude causal inference. CONCLUSIONS: ACEs were more strongly associated with loneliness than with social isolation, particularly in later life. Among adults with ACE histories, asking about loneliness may capture disconnection that structural indicators such as living arrangements or contact frequency miss.

papers.abstract_full: Photogranular sludge (PG) systems offer a promising route toward energy-efficient wastewater treatment and resource recovery, yet how granule size is associated with functional differentiation remains poorly understood. Here, mature PGs were separated into three size fractions (<0.5 mm, 0.5-1 mm, and 1-1.5 mm) to characterize size-associated differences in granular properties, microbial ecological organization, and system function. Larger granule-size fractions were characterized by greater physical compaction, with lower pore volume, porosity, and permeability, together with higher surface hydrophobicity and mechanical rigidity. Paradoxically, despite the development of a denser and less permeable structure, larger granules exhibited more integrated microbial networks, stronger phototrophic-heterotrophic associations, and a greater importance of stochastic processes in community assembly. Variation partitioning analysis showed that granule-associated properties jointly accounted for 59.0% of microbial community variation, quantitatively linking granular properties with ecological organization. These ecological shifts coincided with elevated metabolic potential, reflected by higher abundances of key functional genes (narG, nirS, and ppk1) and enzyme activities. Consequently, the 1-1.5 mm fraction exhibited the highest specific pollutant removal rates, with DOC, TN, and PO43--P removal rates increasing by 20.3%, 49.2%, and 32.4%, respectively, compared with the <0.5 mm fraction. Resource recovery also showed pronounced size dependence: small granules maximized alginate-like exopolysaccharide production, medium granules yielded hydrogels with a more compact macroscopic appearance, whereas large granules accumulated the most lipids (39.0% higher than the smallest fraction) and exhibited enhanced lipid biosynthesis potential. Overall, this study establishes a size-associated property-ecology-function framework for PG systems and suggests that managing granule-size distributions may provide a potential operational strategy for simultaneously optimizing wastewater treatment and resource recovery.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Polarization reveals critical diagnostic clues embedded in a range of diagnostic algorithms aimed at early skin cancer detection, but device-dependent visualization differences raise safety concerns. OBJECTIVES: The POLARIS study compared polarization-dependent structure visibility across seven commercial handheld dermatoscopes. METHODS: Twenty international dermatoscopists, informed of the target polarization-dependent structure(s) in each case and partially blinded to dermatoscope model, evaluated standardized cases imaged using seven devices (DL3, DL4, DL5, Handyscope, DELTA 20 T, DELTA 30, and DELTA 30 PRO). Feature visibility was scored on a 5-point Likert scale and analyzed with a cumulative link mixed model. RESULTS: Device type significantly impacted visibility (10,779 ratings by 20 raters of 61 lesions; p < 0.001). Against DELTA 30, every other device had higher odds of a better rating: the smallest odds ratio was 7.0 and the largest, for Handyscope, was 43.2. DELTA 30 received low-visibility ratings in 69.5% of assessments. Handyscope also was rated above every other device (odds ratios 2.3-43.2), and no device was estimated to outperform it for any structure. Those other devices formed a graded order. DELTA 30 PRO was rated markedly higher than DELTA 30 (odds ratio 10.1, Bonferroni-adjusted 95% CI 4.6-22.4). CONCLUSIONS: Hybrid dermatoscopes differ significantly in their visualization of polarization-dependent structures which remain vital diagnostic clues. The suboptimal recognition of these features by underperforming devices, highlights the need to understand how these disparities impact diagnostic accuracy. Consequently, dermatoscopists should be aware of the performance of the devices they use.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Model validation is important to quantify the generalization capability of a predictive model or learning algorithm. In practice, data splitting is required to quantify the relevant out-of-sample performance reliably. For practitioners it is often unclear which of the available data splitting schemes is most suitable for their specific problem. This is particularly true when not only (in-distribution) reproducibility but also (out-of-distribution) transferability to another population or context needs to be assessed. METHODS: We performed a selective review to assess the documentation of external validations of clinical risk prediction models in the literature. We derived a novel estimand framework based on existing frameworks for treatment and diagnostic studies. To conduct statistical inference, we adopted different established methods for our purpose (exploratory visualization, three-level meta-analysis, Bayesian mixed model​). Finally, we applied our framework in a hypothetical predictive modelling study based on real-world data. RESULTS: Our new framework allows a precise specification of the relevant performance estimand by defining constraints on inference and development context. To facilitate practical application, we provide an algorithm which allows estimand-aligned data splitting. We also propose a novel structured nested cross-validation scheme to enable an adequate empirical comparison of reproducibility and transferability. Our numerical experiments illustrate that the estimand can influence empirical validation results and should thus be carefully chosen. The meta-analysis approach offers a good compromise between simplicity and suitability for comparing the performance corresponding to different estimands. CONCLUSION: Our framework facilitates the specification of the estimand in the predictive modelling context and thus helps to describe the validation gap between validation study and intended use more precisely. It can improve the current practice in the clinical risk prediction literature where the estimand is often only vaguely defined and the usefulness of the performance estimate(s) is thus unclear.

To facilitate practical application, we provide an algorithm which allows estimand-aligned data splitting.
We also propose a novel structured nested cross-validation scheme to enable an adequate empirical comparison of reproducibility and transferability.

papers.abstract: Bacterial survival in fluctuating environments depends on the ability of individual cells to maintain physiological homeostasis under stress, yet how single cells recover from transient pH fluctuations remains poorly understood. papers.abstract_full: Bacterial survival in fluctuating environments depends on the ability of individual cells to maintain physiological homeostasis under stress, yet how single cells recover from transient pH fluctuations remains poorly understood. We tracked the cell-size dynamics and survival of Corynebacterium glutamicum cells exposed to short, strong acid (pH 4, 20 min) or alkaline (pH 11, 15 min) pulses. Acid stress considerably increases the size added during the stress cycle, whereas alkaline stress increases it only modestly. Nevertheless, surviving cells maintain their division strategy and restore size homeostasis in the next cycle. Coordination between relatives is short-lived: sister cells have similar cell-cycle durations after stress, but durations become uncorrelated once the last division shared by two cells precedes the stress by more than about 1.5 generations. Survival of acid stress favors larger cells and is largely stochastic, with no detectable lineage heritability. In contrast, survival of alkaline stress favors smaller cells and is transiently heritable: co-survival probability remains high among relatives separated by up to two generations. These findings provide insight into pH survival in C. glutamicum and present statistical methods to study cell-size regulation and survival under transient, severe environmental fluctuations.

In contrast, survival of alkaline stress favors smaller cells and is transiently heritable: co-survival probability remains high among relatives separated by up to two generations.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Purpose  To quantify upper-limb kinematics and estimated biomechanical load (a kinematics-derived load proxy, not measured muscle force) during simulated manual flexible ureteroscopy (fURS) using markerless 3D pose estimation, testing whether experience-related differences concentrate in lower-calyx access. Methods  Eighteen urologists (10 experts, 8 novices) performed a phantom task: renal pelvis to upper, middle and lower calyx, returning to the pelvis between calyces. 3D landmarks from smartphone video (MediaPipe Pose) were converted to joint angles, jerk and inverse-dynamics load estimates. Primary outcomes were right-wrist force, jerk and angle in the lower-calyx phase; others were exploratory, analysed with participant-level Welch tests, Hedges g, 95% CIs, Holm correction and a mixed model for group × phase interaction. Results  Procedure time was longer in novices (115.5 vs 61.5 s). In the lower-calyx phase, novices showed higher right-wrist force (1.87 vs 1.16 N; Holm p = 0.026), jerk (Holm p = 0.020) and angle (31.6° vs 24.9°; Holm p = 0.026), with no upper-calyx differences; force and jerk showed significant group × phase interactions (p = 0.004, 0.007) but angle did not (p = 0.35). Force, jerk and dispersion correlated strongly with movement speed (ρ = 0.93–0.99), and group differences were attenuated after speed adjustment. Conclusion  In this simulator study, experience-related differences in estimated wrist load emerged mainly during lower-calyx access, whereas wrist angle differed throughout, pinpointing an ergonomic target. Because estimates were kinematics-derived and not EMG-validated, findings are hypothesis-generating; correlating them with physiological muscle activity is an important next step for robot-assisted ureteroscopy design.

papers.abstract_full: PURPOSE: Occupational injury surveillance in low​ and middle-income countries remains fragmented, and nationally representative, mechanism-disaggregated risk profiles are rare in the Middle East and North Africa regi​on. This study provides the first multi-year, exposure-adjusted and composite-scored analysis of compensated workplace injuries in Tunisia. METHODS​: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 34,699 compensated workplace injury claims recorded by Tunisia's National Health Insurance Fund (CNAM) in 2019, supplemented by aggregate CNAM indicators for 2022-2023 for temporal trend assessment. An injury index (lost-time injuries per 1000 employees) with 95% confidence intervals and a Composite Risk Score (CRS) integrating rate, severity and mechanism diversity were computed for six sectors. Multivariable Poisson regression with robust standard errors estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) for six injury mechanisms. papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVES: Efforts to examine the influence of genetics in the efficacy of lithium using genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified several loci. Here, we report new cases and meta-analyses to combine previous efforts. METHODS: We report data from 1259 participants with bipolar disorder (BD) recruited at University College London who had been treated with lithium. The data come from three waves of genotyping on different arrays. The GWAS data from each array was analysed separately and then meta-analysed with two published lithium response GWAS datasets. Post-GWAS analyses were conducted to examine lithium response heritability and its genetic correlations with other traits. We also attempted to replicate past polygenic risk scores (PRS) results. RESULTS: SNP rs116927879 (A/G) was associated with lithium response at a genome-wide significance level (p = 4.509 × 10-08) with a consistent effect across all cohorts. rs116927879 is located on chromosome 7 and maps to the protein-coding gene ADCY1 and two pseudo-genes, GTF2IP13 and SEPT7P2. The sQTL results suggested that rs116927879 genotypes may influence the splicing of ADCY1 across different brain regions. We estimated the SNP heritability (h2) for good lithium response as 20.3% and 15.6% for subjective/objective response definitions, respectively. We did not observe any genetic correlation or PRS association between the lithium response and schizophrenia or major depression disorder. However, we found weak evidence to suggest that males are more likely to be good responders. CONCLUSIONS: Our GWAS identifies a genome-wide significant finding and provides updated heritability estimates for lithium efficacy.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Helicobacter pylori infection has been associated with iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) during pregnancy, but evidence from Uganda remains limited. This study compared IDA prevalence by H. pylori status, assessed the adjusted association between H. pylori positivity and IDA, and explored factors associated with IDA among infected pregnant women. METHODS: A facility-based analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 392 pregnant women attending antenatal care at Mubende Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda, from August to December 2025. Participants were systematically recruited into H. pylori-positive and -negative analytical groups (196 each). Active H. pylori infection was determined using stool antigen testing, and IDA was defined by concurrent anaemia and serum ferritin <15 µg/L. Prevalence ratios (PRs) were estimated for the H. pylori-IDA association, while logistic regression explored factors associated with IDA among H. pylori-positive women. RESULTS: IDA was more prevalent among H. pylori-positive than -negative women (14.8% [29/196] vs 6.6% [13/196]). H. pylori positivity was associated with a higher prevalence of IDA (cPR = 2.23, 95% CI: 1.20-4.16; p = 0.012), including after adjustment for residence, iron-rich food consumption and household income (aPR = 2.22, 95% CI: 1.16-4.24; p = 0.016). Median haemoglobin was lower among H. pylori-positive women (11 vs 12 g/dL; p < 0.001). Among H. pylori-positive women, lack of deworming (aOR=4.88, 95% CI: 1.73-13.79), tea or coffee consumption with meals (aOR=4.31, 95% CI: 1.22-15.20), and inadequate handwashing (aOR=3.18, 95% CI: 1.15-8.76) were associated with higher odds of IDA. CONCLUSIONS: H. pylori positivity was associated with a higher prevalence of IDA among pregnant women attending ANC at Mubende Regional Referral Hospital. Lack of deworming, tea or coffee consumption with meals, and inadequate handwashing were associated with IDA among H. pylori-positive women. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the subgroup findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of IDA cases.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations of functional capacity and medication adherence with self-care practices among older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus treated at a Peruvian national hospital. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 206 adults aged 60 years or older receiving outpatient diabetes care in Lima, Peru, during 2025. Self-care was classified as fair or good. Functional capacity was assessed using the Barthel Index, and medication adherence was assessed using the four-item Morisky, Green and Levine Medication Adherence Scale. Crude and mutually adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Poisson regression with robust variance. RESULTS: Fair self-care was observed in 69.9% of participants, and 74.3% were functionally independent. Compared with independent participants, moderate dependence was associated with a 40% higher prevalence of fair self-care (PR = 1.40; 95% CI: 1.17-1.69), severe dependence with a 48% higher prevalence (PR = 1.48; 95% CI: 1.24-1.77), and total dependence with a 56% higher prevalence (PR = 1.56; 95% CI: 1.37-1.78). Slight dependence was not associated with fair self-care. Low medication adherence was associated with fair self-care in crude analysis but not after mutual adjustment. CONCLUSION: Moderate, severe, and total functional dependence were associated with fair rather than good self-care. Interpretation should consider construct overlap, residual confounding, sparse data in the most dependent groups, and the inability of the cross-sectional design to establish directionality.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: People who use drugs (PWUD) are at increased risk of blood-borne viral infections. Evidence on hepatitis C virus (HCV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) among PWUD in Palestine is limited. This study determined the seroprevalence of HCV, HBV, and HIV among PWUD attending governmental substance use disorder (SUD) treatment centers in the West Bank. METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 397 PWUD in SUD treatment centers in the West Bank during 2019-2023. Serological results for anti-HCV, HBsAg, and anti-HIV were obtained from routine clinical records. Crude and adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) for the association between injecting drug use and anti-HCV seropositivity were estimated using modified Poisson regression. RESULTS: HCV seroprevalence was 23.0%, HBsAg prevalence was 2.0%, and no HIV was detected. HCV seroprevalence was 55.4% among injecting versus 6.7% among non-injecting users. After adjustment for age, education, employment status, and previous treatment attempts, injecting drug use remained strongly associated with HCV seropositivity (adjusted PR = 6.43, 95% CI 3.82-10.82). HCV prevalence increased with longer duration of drug use (p for trend <0.001), and varied significantly across governorates. CONCLUSIONS: HCV is the predominant infection among PWUD receiving SUD treatment in the West Bank, whereas HBV prevalence was low and HIV was not detected. Injecting drug use was strongly associated with HCV seropositivity, and prevalence increased with longer duration of drug use. Integrating HCV screening, RNA testing, antiviral treatment, and harm-reduction policies into SUD services is essential to achieve the WHO 2030 hepatitis elimination targets.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer screening (LCS) centers are unevenly distributed across the United States, with much lower access in rural than urban areas. It remains unknown whether geographic access to LCS centers is associated with early detection of lung cancer. METHODS: We used Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results data to identify patients aged 55-80 years diagnosed with lung cancer during 2015-2019. Geographic access to LCS centers was measured using the two-step floating catchment area method and categorized into quartiles. Modified Poisson regression with county-level clustering was used to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs) for early-stage diagnosis. RESULTS: Patients in counties with the least access to LCS were less likely to be diagnosed at an early stage than those in counties with the greatest access (PR=0.88, 95% CI 0.84-0.93; Ptrend<.001). The association varied by neighborhood socioeconomic status and census region, with significant associations observed only among patients living in less deprived counties and in the Western United States. County-level vehicle ownership did not significantly modify this association overall, but among Medicaid beneficiaries residing in metropolitan areas, local transportation resources significantly modified the association between geographic access and early-stage diagnosis. CONCLUSIONS: Limited geographic access to LCS centers was associated with a lower likelihood of early-stage lung cancer diagnosis, with variation according to neighborhood socioeconomic context, census region, and local transportation resource among Medicaid beneficiaries. IMPACT: Geographic access to LCS centers is necessary, but not sufficient, for equitable LCS, and the benefits of improving geographic access depend on the broader socioeconomic, regional, and transportation context.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background  Movement behaviors and sleep duration are associated with wellbeing in children; however, evidence regarding their relative contributions to different wellbeing dimensions remains limited. Therefore, this study explores the cross-sectional associations between device-measured movement and sleep behaviors and different wellbeing dimensions. Methods  A total of 792 Danish schoolchildren aged 6–9 years were included in the analyses. Moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), light physical activity (LPA), sedentary behavior (SB), and sleep time were measured using thigh-worn accelerometers (Axivity AX3) for seven consecutive days. Physical and psychological wellbeing were self-reported using the KIDSCREEN-VIDEO questionnaire. Internalizing problems, externalizing problems, and prosocial behavior were parent-reported using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire. Linear regression models were used to estimate the proportion of variance in each wellbeing dimension explained by movement behaviors (MVPA, LPA, and SB), sleep time, demographic variables, and school class. Results  The full models explained between 4.7% and 10.3% of the variance across the wellbeing dimensions. Movement behaviors and sleep time collectively accounted for the largest proportion of explained variance in physical wellbeing (3.9%). MVPA showed the strongest contribution to physical wellbeing and internalizing problems, whereas SB contributed most to externalizing problems. School class accounted for a similar proportion of variance in psychological wellbeing as the full model (~ 7.5%). Conclusion  Movement behaviors and sleep time explained only a limited proportion of the variance in wellbeing among children, with behavior-specific associations across dimensions. These findings suggest that physical activity interventions may benefit specific dimensions of wellbeing rather than wellbeing more broadly and that peer and classroom environments are important.  Clinical trial registration  : ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05940675; registered on 4 July 2023.

papers.abstract: Background  While bipolar disorder has a positive genetic correlation (r∼0.3) with educational attainment (EA), individuals with bipolar disorder diagnoses have lower EA in adulthood. papers.abstract_full: Background  While bipolar disorder has a positive genetic correlation (r∼0.3) with educational attainment (EA), individuals with bipolar disorder diagnoses have lower EA in adulthood. To clarify this paradox, we hypothesise that bipolar disorder and educational outcomes share a positive genetic association, reflected in high academic performance earlier in life, but that emerging bipolar disorder symptoms disrupt academic trajectories, leading to the observed poor long-term educational outcomes. Methods  We employed a sibling comparison design across four population-based cohorts (N  total = 1,145,795 siblings). First, we tested the association between bipolar disorder polygenic scores (PGS) and educational outcomes (EA and academic performance) in the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study (MoBa) and UK Biobank (UKB). Second, we examined associations between academic performance at ages 10, 12, 13, and 14 and subsequent bipolar disorder diagnosis using registry data from Statistics Netherlands and Statistics Norway (with the Norwegian Control and Payment of Health Reimbursements Databases).  Findings  Siblings with higher bipolar disorder PGS had significantly higher EA (β  W = 0.03, 95% CI [0.01, 0.05], N=16,746) as well as higher academic performance at age 10 (0.03 [0.01, 0.05], N=17,677) in MoBa. Secondly, individuals with bipolar disorder had better overall academic performance than their unaffected sibling at ages 10 (HR  W = 1.12 [1.02, 1.22], N=343,898) and 12 (1.59 [1.16, 2.19], N=619,796). However, individuals with bipolar disorder experienced a decline in academic performance at ages 13 (0.84 [0.73, 0.96], N=320,342) and 14 (0.72 [0.61, 0.85], N=299,039).  Interpretation  Bipolar disorder shares a positive genetic association with educational outcomes, reflected in early academic advantage. This is followed by an academic decline in mid-adolescence, highlighting the period of educational disruption associated with bipolar disorder. papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background:  Hypokalemia is an important electrolyte abnormality that may occur in patients with diabetes mellitus through renal potassium losses, osmotic diuresis, and intracellular potassium shifts associated with metabolic disturbances. However, evidence regarding its prevalence and associated factors among patients with diabetes in sub-Saharan Africa remains limited. This study determined the prevalence of hypokalemia and identified factors associated with hypokalemia among adults with diabetes mellitus in Eastern Uganda. Methods: A facility-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 374 adults with diabetes mellitus attending the Medical Outpatient and Diabetic Clinics of Jinja Regional Referral Hospital, Eastern Uganda, between 5 July and 31 August 2022. Sociodemographic, clinical, anthropometric, and treatment-related data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Serum potassium was measured using a Cobas C311 chemistry analyzer. Hypokalemia was defined as serum potassium Results: Among the 374 participants, 251 (67.1%) were female, and the median age was 50 years. Hypokalemia was identified in 10 participants, giving a prevalence of  2.7%  . In the multivariable analysis, urban residence was independently associated with a higher prevalence of hypokalemia compared with rural residence (aPR = 3.94, 95% CI: 1.13–13.82; p = 0.032). Participants receiving oral antidiabetic agents had a substantially higher prevalence of hypokalemia compared with those receiving insulin therapy (aPR = 13.94, 95% CI: 2.71–71.79; p = 0.002). Participants aged 31–45 years had a lower prevalence compared with those aged 16–30 years (aPR = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.05–0.97; p = 0.046). Uncontrolled random blood glucose (> 10 mmol/L) was associated with a higher prevalence of hypokalemia, although the association did not reach statistical significance (aPR = 2.99, 95% CI: 0.85–10.51; p = 0.088). Conclusion: Hypokalemia occurred in approximately 1 in 37 adults with diabetes mellitus attending this regional referral hospital. Urban residence and oral antidiabetic therapy were independently associated with hypokalemia, while uncontrolled glycemia showed a non-significant trend toward increased prevalence. Routine attention to potassium status may be warranted in selected patients with diabetes, particularly those with poor glycemic control or receiving oral therapy. However, the small number of hypokalemia cases warrants cautious interpretation, and larger studies are needed to confirm these associations.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Progressive stiffening of the extracellular matrix (ECM), driven by excessive collagen deposition and crosslinking, is a hallmark of breast cancer progression. While ECM mechanics profoundly influence tumor behavior and fate, the mechanisms by which matrix stiffening regulates exosome biogenesis and release remain poorly understood. METHODS: To investigate the impact of matrix stiffness on exosome secretion, polyacrylamide gels with defined stiffness were employed. Cancer cells-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEV) were characterized and quantified using nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), bead-based assays, and reporter cell systems. Mechanistic insights were obtained through immunofluorescence (IF), proximity ligation assay (PLA), TEM, immunoblotting, and immunoprecipitation. A stiffness-tunable NOD-SCID xenograft model was used to validate the effect of stiffness on exosome secretion in vivo. Additionally, human breast cancer tissue microarrays were analyzed to examine the associations among collagen remodeling, exosome secretion pathways, and clinical outcomes. RESULTS: We unravel a dual mechanism by which stiff ECM enhances exosome output. Increased matrix rigidity promotes intraluminal vesicle formation by enhancing HSP90-TSG101 association, thereby stimulating ESCRT-dependent exosome biogenesis, while simultaneously facilitating multivesicular body docking for fusion with the plasma membrane via upregulation of Rab27a. Rab27a expression is controlled by KIBRA, a regulator of YAP/TAZ mechanosignaling. Genetic depletion of KIBRA or Rab27a markedly suppresses stiffness-induced exosome secretion and abolishes ECM-driven motility and invasion in vitro. In stiffness-tunable xenograft models, stiff ECM accelerates tumor growth and elevates circulating sEV levels, effects reversed by Rab27a silencing. Furthermore, analysis of human breast tumor tissues revealed that a highly bundled and crosslinked collagen architecture - indicative of higher stiffness - correlated with increased colocalization of Rab27a and KIBRA, coupled with an unfavorable clinical prognosis. CONCLUSION: Collectively, our findings uncover a novel mechanoresponsive reliance of HSP90-TSG101 and KIBRA-Rab27a axes that link ECM stiffness to exosomes-driven tumor aggressiveness, highlighting new avenues for mechano-targeting of breast malignancies.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Cisplatin resistance in lung cancer, mechanistically rooted in glutathione (GSH)-mediated detoxification, enhanced nuclear DNA repair, and apoptotic evasion, remains a major therapeutic hurdle. Although Pt(IV) prodrugs can circumvent these barriers, conventional nanoformulations are frequently limited by low drug loading, carrier-associated toxicity, and inadequate tumor retention. METHODS: To address these challenges, a carrier-free, enzyme-instructed in situ self-assembly (EISA) Pt(IV) nanoprodrug (TPP-FFK(p)Y-Pt(IV)) was engineered to achieve hierarchical tumor-mitochondria targeting. The design exploits tumor-overexpressed alkaline phosphatase (ALP) to trigger dephosphorylation and nanofiber formation on cancer cell membranes, prolonging retention and enhancing internalization. Following triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-mediated mitochondrial delivery, the Pt(IV) core is selectively reduced by intratumoral GSH, releasing cytotoxic Pt(II) while depleting GSH (the "pull" effect). Liberated Pt(II) is accompanied by a mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) burst (the "push" effect). ALP inhibitor (levamisole hydrochloride) pretreatment, molecular TPP (methyltriphenylphosphonium bromide) competition, and Pearson's co-localization analysis were used to verify the necessity of EISA and mitochondrial targeting. RESULTS: ALP inhibitor pretreatment reduced cellular uptake and attenuated cytotoxicity (IC50 increased from 5.69 μM to 37.50 μM), confirming that EISA is ALP-dependent. Molecular TPP competition reduced mitochondrial co-localization (Pearson's coefficient decreased from 0.95 to 0.74) and attenuated cytotoxicity (IC50 increased from 5.69 μM to 22.60 μM), confirming that mitochondrial targeting independently contributes to the enhanced efficacy. This coordinated oxidative cascade was associated with mitochondrial dysfunction, including mitochondrial membrane potential collapse, ATP depletion, and lactate dehydrogenase leakage, consistent with bypassing nuclear DNA repair-dependent resistance pathways. In vitro, TPP-FFK(p)Y-Pt(IV) reduced the IC50 against A549/DDP cells to 5.46 μM, compared with 53.80 μM for cisplatin, yielding a resistance reversal index of 9.85. In A549/DDP cell-derived xenografts, the nanoprodrug exhibited significantly superior antitumor efficacy (81.7% tumor growth inhibition) versus free cisplatin (56.2%), with negligible hematotoxicity and hepatorenal toxicity over the 21-day observation period. CONCLUSION: By integrating EISA-mediated retention, TPP-directed mitochondrial delivery, and a GSH-depleting/ROS-amplifying cascade, this carrier-free platform targets organellar vulnerability to overcome chemoresistance. The data are consistent with a precision redox therapy strategy with potential for further development in refractory malignancies, offering a candidate alternative to conventional nanomedicines pending validation in additional models.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) modulate the breast cancer (BC) microenvironment, but their role in endocrine therapy resistance and clinical outcomes remains ill-defined. METHODS: By integrating single-cell and multi-cohort bulk RNA-seq data from ER⁺ BC patients, we built an ADSC-derived prognostic model via a four-dimensional filtering strategy and 10 machine-learning algorithms. Spatial transcriptomics, co-culture assays, and orthotopic mammary fat-pad model validated the hub gene's function and mechanism. RESULTS: ADSCs were enriched in non-responders and exhibited elevated stemness. A 17-gene Ridge regression model stratified patient risk across five cohorts, with high-risk tumors showing TP53 mutations and immunosuppression. EFHD1 emerged as the key hub gene spatially co-localized with ADSCs. Mechanistically, co-culture with ER⁺ BC cells upregulated EFHD1 in ADSCs by ∼2.0-fold, which triggered NF-κB/p65 nuclear translocation and a ∼1.5-fold increase in FN1 protein levels. Functionally, EFHD1-overexpressing ADSCs promoted BC proliferation and invasion. In an orthotopic xenograft model, tumors co-injected with control ADSCs reached ∼500 mm³ by day 30 and maintained robust growth under letrozole + ribociclib (∼350 mm³), compared with BC cells alone (∼300 mm³). In contrast, EFHD1 knockdown in ADSCs reduced tumor volume to ∼200 mm³ and further sensitized tumors to letrozole + ribociclib (∼150 mm³, a ∼40% reduction relative to the drug-only group), with Ki-67 positivity decreasing from ∼4.0% to ∼1.5%. CONCLUSION: We established a robust ADSC-based prognostic model and uncovered a novel stromal EFHD1/NF-κB/FN1 axis driving ER⁺ BC progression and endocrine therapy resistance, identifying stromal EFHD1 as a candidate target whose pharmacological validation remains to be established.

papers.abstract_full: Anatomical prevalence meta-analyses often combine studies that differ in population, modality, specimen source, variant definition, and observational unit. Funnel-plot asymmetry is frequently interpreted as publication bias, although it may reflect transformation, event yield, heterogeneity, or prevalence-study-size associations. We evaluated six two-stage procedure families and a one-stage binomial-normal mixed-effects framework (BN-GLMM) across rare/low (0.05-5%) and broader (5-50%) prevalence domains, each with a controlled heterogeneity anchor and stochastic module. The 80,000 meta-analyses yielded 240,000 transformation-specific analyses under ordinary arcsine-square-root (PAS), Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine (PFT), and continuity-corrected two-stage logit (PLO), plus 240,000 BN-GLMM fits. Among two-stage analyses, PAS and PFT were most stable. Under PLO, heterogeneity alone generated Egger, Begg, and LFK signals even at 5-50% prevalence, whereas study-size-based regressions were more stable. BN-GLMM directly modeled counts and was highly evaluable. In rare data, all-zero evidence bases were non-estimable, and moderator estimates were unstable when only one or two studies contained events. Wald-z BN inference was well calibrated without heterogeneity but mildly anti-conservative at K = 10 with heterogeneity. T-reference sensitivity improved calibration and coverage with modest power loss but did not consistently restore nominal performance. Direct BN signaling was 8.8% for selection alone versus 61.8% for a generated size-prevalence association alone in rare data, and 9.4% versus 82.1% at 5-50% prevalence. Correct-direction detection declined as heterogeneity increased, estimated I² did not map consistently to true logit-scale heterogeneity, and selection could shift observed prevalence without detectable asymmetry. Within the evaluated assumptions, the provisional roadmap supports count-based modeling and transformation-aware triangulation. Formal inference should require K ≥ 10, sufficient event information, and meaningful study-size variation. No asymmetry or moderator signal establishes publication bias.

papers.abstract_full: Histone variants play an important role in regulating chromatin dynamics of Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV). Here, we investigate the role of histone variant macroH2A in EBV chromatin structure, gene expression and copy number control during latent infection. ChIP-seq analysis in EBV + SNU719 gastric carcinoma and Mutu I Burkitt lymphoma cells revealed that macroH2A was most enriched at repetitive DNA elements, including oriLyt, BHLF1, LF3 and terminal repeat (TR) regions of the EBV genome. MacroH2A depletion in EBV-associated gastric cancer cell line SNU719 led to a small increase in some viral lytic genes and increase in viral DNA copy number. RNAseq transcriptomics after macroH2A depletion identified major perturbations in cellular gene pathways, including β-catenin/TCF signaling and chromatin remodeling. Depletion of macroH2A during EBV lytic reactivation reduced EBV lytic gene activation, but increased EBV DNA copy number. Previous study demonstrated a colocalization and cooperative binding between histone variant H2A.Z and EBNA1. We now show that depletion of macroH2A causes an increase in both H2A.Z and EBNA1 at oriP and cellular binding sites for EBNA1. We also found that γH2AX localizes to oriP and that this depends on macroH2A. Finally, we show that CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of macroH2A increases the replication and episome maintenance of oriP-containing plasmids. Taken together, these findings indicate that macroH2A localizes to the repetitive elements of EBV, including oriLyt, and can function to limit H2A.Z and EBNA1 binding at oriP, which alters DNA damage signaling at oriP and limits episomal replication. These findings provide a novel role for macroH2A in maintaining EBV copy number and genome integrity.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Background  Insomnia is consistently associated with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) in observational studies, but the causal relationship and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the causal relationship between insomnia and late-onset AD and to identify molecular pathways and candidate genes that may contribute to this association by integrating genetic causal inference with transcriptomics. Methods  Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) was performed using 28 single-nucleotide polymorphisms as instruments, with insomnia genome-wide association study summary statistics from UK Biobank (336,965 participants of European ancestry) and late-onset AD data from FinnGen (11,359 cases and 508,613 controls). Inverse-variance weighting was the primary method. Robustness was assessed using MR-Egger, weighted median, simple mode, and weighted mode estimates, together with pleiotropy, heterogeneity, and leave-one-out analyses. GEO datasets GSE122063 and GSE110226 were integrated for differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network, protein interaction, and functional enrichment analyses. Lasso regression and support vector machine recursive feature elimination were used to identify key candidate genes, whose discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves. Results  Inverse-variance weighting associated genetically predicted insomnia with higher odds of late-onset AD (OR = 3.36, 95% CI 1.02–10.99; P = 0.045). Other MR methods yielded directionally consistent but imprecise estimates. The MR-Egger intercept test found no evidence of directional pleiotropy (P = 0.939), and Cochran’s Q test was not statistically significant (P = 0.062). No individual instrument dominated the leave-one-out results. Transcriptomic analysis identified 1,616 differentially expressed genes and eight co-expression modules. MEpink, MEblack, and MEbrown showed the strongest associations with AD. Their intersection with 2,330 insomnia-related genes yielded 35 candidates, enriched mainly in neuroinflammation, cell adhesion, and lipid metabolism. Both machine learning algorithms selected seven key candidates. All seven were differentially expressed between AD and controls in the combined dataset, with individual AUCs above 0.75. Conclusion  Genetic liability to insomnia may be associated with an increased risk of late-onset AD. Neuroinflammation and lipid metabolism may link the two conditions, and seven candidate genes warrant further study. Given the borderline MR result, wide confidence interval, tissue heterogeneity, and absence of independent external validation, these findings require confirmation in larger multi-ancestry cohorts, independent transcriptomic datasets, and experimental studies.

papers.abstract_full: Genome-wide association studies have catalogued tens of thousands of trait-associated loci, most of them in non-coding DNA, yet for most loci the path from nucleotide to phenotype remains correlational. We propose a layered computational decomposition of the genome as a complement to data-driven approaches: sequence as formal language, sequence as information-bearing signal, mobile elements as runtime, compilation to interaction networks through thermodynamic and rule-based models, and execution as cellular and multicellular dynamics. Each layer is defined by its inputs, outputs and formalisms, and we set out where the frame breaks down, including the looseness of algorithmic-information estimates, the triviality of universality results and the failure of string grammars at the chromatin level. Synthetic-biology platforms serve as tests of whether the layers compose, and genomic foundation models and the AlphaGenome Atlas, which predicts effects for all nine billion possible single-nucleotide variants, serve as oracles whose coverage and limits we map onto the framework. We state five falsifiable predictions and test the first, that sequence compressibility carries information about regulatory function beyond composition and conservation, on 38,556 single-nucleotide variants from a saturation-mutagenesis reporter assay of 21 regulatory elements. In a pooled model, local compressibility is associated with measured effect size (standardized β = −0.030, p = 0.0014). The association roughly halves under full control for base composition, loses significance when composition, motif and noise adjustments are combined under locus-level inference (wild cluster bootstrap p = 0.11), and averages zero within loci (random-effects β = −0.0003, p = 0.90). The prediction is therefore not supported at the variant level in these data, which bound the effect a genome-wide test should expect. The argument is not that the genome "is" a program, but that treating it as one supplies formal tools whose predictions can be checked.

papers.abstract_full: The effectiveness of genomic prediction in forest trees is often constrained by genotype-by-environment (G×E) interactions, particularly when predicting performance in environments not represented in the training population. We evaluated the integration of genomic, enviromic (climatic and soil), and metabolomic (targeted monoterpene) information within multi-environment single-step genomic best linear unbiased prediction (ssGBLUP) reaction norm models to improve prediction in unobserved environments. Models incorporated environmental covariates (W) and genotype-specific responses using linear and nonlinear kernels, including Gaussian and Arc-Cosine formulations. The study examined 12 traits measured on 11,124 trees across four lodgepole pine progeny trials, with 1,490 trees genotyped with 25,099 SNPs. Predictive performance was assessed using leave-one-environment-out cross-validation. Additive genetic correlations among environments revealed substantial G×E for early-growth traits and drought-related decline, with correlations frequently below 0.65. Inclusion of environmental covariates reduced variance attributed to site effects, indicating that these descriptors captured environmental heterogeneity. Incorporating G×E and genotype-by-environmental covariate (G×W) interactions improved model performance, increasing explained phenotypic variance by up to 29.58% and reducing residual variance by up to 3.13% relative to baseline models. Across traits, G×E explained more phenotypic variation than G×W, contributing on average 2.31% and 0.60%, respectively. Predictive ability was high across models (0.688-0.701), with gains of up to 7.85% when nonlinear kernels were combined with metabolomic covariates, particularly for traits exhibiting stronger G×E. Monoterpene profiles yielded predictive performance comparable to climate and soil descriptors, highlighting the potential of integrating genomic, enviromic, and metabolomic information to improve prediction across environments and support climate-resilient forest tree breeding and deployment.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: There is a lack of effective molecular biomarkers for the early identification of the risk of cardiac arrest. Mitochondrial dysfunction is widely recognised as being involved in the pathophysiological process of cardiac arrest, but the upstream epigenetic regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. This study takes DNA methylation as its central focus. By systematically evaluating the genetic associations between methylation quantitative trait loci (mQTLs) in mitochondrial genes and the risk of cardiac arrest, and by tracking downstream changes in gene expression and protein abundance, the study aims to explore potential regulatory pathways linking epigenetic variations to molecular phenotypes and ultimately to disease. METHODS: The study utilised mitochondrial genes from MitoCarta 3.0, obtaining corresponding methylation quantitative trait loci (mQTL) from GoDMC, gene expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) from eQTLGen and GTEx, and protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) from UKB-PPP and deCODE. These were used as instrumental variables for Mendelian randomisation (MR), summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) and colocalisation analysis, to systematically screen for multi-omics genetic signals in mitochondrial genes associated with cardiac arrest (from FinnGen). Based on the analysis results, multi-omics evidence was categorised, and single-cell expression profiles and machine learning models were utilised to perform functional annotation and assess the discriminatory power of candidate genes. RESULTS: The analysis identified five mitochondrial genes with a directional genetic association with cardiac arrest: GATM, GRHPR, NDUFS6, PMAIP1 and AGXT. Among these, the cg10760299 locus of GATM was negatively associated with the risk of cardiac arrest (OR = 0.875, 95% CI 0.832-0.921, p < 0.001), whilst gene expression (OR = 1.396, 95% CI 1.194-1.633, p = 0.005) and protein abundance (OR = 1.513, 95% CI 1.228-1.863, p = 0.015) were positively associated with the risk of cardiac arrest. Single-cell expression profiles indicated that key genes exhibited expression differences between cardiomyocytes and fibroblasts, whilst integrated learning models suggested that these key genes possess potential for disease discrimination. CONCLUSION: Through multi-omics integration analysis, this study identified association signals between methylation sites such as GATM/cg10760299 and the risk of cardiac arrest, providing new candidate targets for research into epigenetic biomarkers of cardiac arrest.

papers.abstract_full: Aging is a complex biological process involving genomic, molecular, cellular, tissue, and systemic changes. In recent years, research evidence has accumulated showing that different dietary patterns can significantly influence the rate of aging at all these levels, the risk of developing age-related diseases, and life expectancy. Diets such as the Mediterranean diet, vegetarian diet, ketogenic diet, DASH, and eating patterns including intermittent fasting have been shown to reduce inflammation, improve metabolic markers, slow telomere shortening, reduce oxidative damage, and modulate other components of the aging process. Observational and interventional studies, including twin studies and long-term cohort studies, demonstrate that pro-healthy diets (rich in vegetables, fruits, fish, and whole grains) are associated with a slower epigenetic age compared to chronological age, reduced inflammation, and improved health profiles-both in younger and older adults. In contrast, Western dietary patterns characterized by processed foods, sugars, and saturated fats accelerate the aging process and increase the risk of age-related diseases. Technological advances, especially the introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) into nutritional research, are ushering in a new era of personalized medicine. AI enables the analysis of big data, identification of hidden patterns between diet, genetics, microbiome, and diseases, prediction of the future effects of dietary changes, and even the construction of personalized nutritional models based on each individual's genome, transcriptome, and microbiome. The vision for the future is that everyone will have a personal AI-based virtual assistant, which will create precise nutrition plans and predict how each dietary component will affect the aging process, disease risk, and quality of life. This will allow managing our aging process intelligently and data-driven, aiming not only for health maintenance, but also for longevity and aging in good health.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Psoriasis is a systemic, immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease strongly associated with metabolic syndrome and obesity. While dysregulation of systemic lipid metabolism is a known exacerbating factor, the localized metabolic reprogramming within the skin microenvironment and its specific role in driving intercellular crosstalk between structural and immune cells remain largely unknown. METHODS: We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of psoriatic and normal skin with bulk transcriptomic data. Lipid metabolic activity at the single-cell level was evaluated using AUCell. To identify diagnostic hub genes, three machine learning algorithms - LASSO regression, Random Forest (RF), and Boruta - were applied to the bulk dataset. T cell subpopulation heterogeneity and intercellular communication were assessed using Seurat and CellChat. To provide preliminary validation of our bioinformatics findings in vivo, we established an obese-psoriasis mouse model using a High-Fat Diet (HFD) combined with topical Imiquimod (IMQ), evaluated via histological staining, immunohistochemistry (IHC), immunofluorescence and ELISA. RESULTS: ScRNA-seq analysis characterized 8 major skin cell types, revealing a significant expansion of T cells and myeloid cells in psoriatic lesions. AUCell scoring demonstrated that psoriatic keratinocytes exhibited the highest lipid metabolic activity among all cell types, with a significant elevation compared to normal controls. Machine learning on bulk transcriptomics identified four core lipid metabolism genes (SQLE, SPTLC2, PLA2G4D, and PLBD1). SQLE was significantly upregulated in psoriatic keratinocytes and demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy. The analysis of the cell communication network suggested potential communication relationships between SQLE+ keratinocytes and Th17 cells, although the identified ligand-receptor pairs were not specific to Th17 cells. In vivo verification demonstrated that diet-induced obesity significantly exacerbated the psoriasis-like lesions induced by IMQ. Immunohistochemical results showed that high expression of SQLE was located in the keratinocytes area, and the infiltration of CD4+IL17A+ Th17 cells in the dermis increased. Additionally, in the obesity-psoriasis model, ELISA test results revealed that the levels of IL-17A and TNF-α were significantly elevated. CONCLUSION: Our findings identified SQLE as a candidate molecular link between keratinocyte lipid metabolic dysfunction and Th17 cell-mediated cutaneous inflammation in the context of obesity. Our findings suggest that the SQLE-Th17 pathway is potentially hyperactivated under obese conditions, contributing to psoriasis exacerbation. Targeting SQLE and its downstream metabolic-immune communication pathways represents a promising therapeutic frontier for psoriasis patients with comorbid metabolic syndrome, pending validation through functional studies.

papers.abstract_full: T1 high-grade bladder cancer presents a therapeutic dilemma, as current risk stratification fails to guide the choice between early cystectomy and bladder-preserving therapy. In our recent work, we defined a high-risk multiomic subtype driven by anoikis resistance and immune evasion and developed the T1HG-UCBguider framework for risk stratification; however, its reliance on multiomic sequencing limits clinical implementation. Here, we translate this framework into Guider, an artificial intelligence-driven reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) decision-aid designed for cost-conscious use in routine pathology workflows and integrating a 30-gene TaqMan assay with clinicopathological variables to predict progression and recurrence, with exploratory treatment-context modules for no instillation, Bacillus Calmette-Guérin, and intravesical chemotherapy. In a multicenter ambispective cohort of 1198 patients, Guider achieved > 10% higher absolute predictive performance than guideline-based risk groups and the published 12-gene progression score within this Chinese T1 high-grade cohort. Reclassification identified 82.5% of guideline-defined high-risk patients who progressed and 45.1% of very-high-risk nonprogressors who might be considered for bladder preservation. Guider could potentially support treatment de-escalation in 29.7% and escalation in 12.9% of patients. These findings establish a scalable translational framework bridging multiomic discovery and clinical decision support, warranting prospective interventional validation in geographically, ethnically, and demographically diverse populations.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden, with highly heterogeneous trajectories ranging from long-term stability to rapid progression towards kidney failure and kidney replacement therapy. Accurate prediction of CKD progression is essential to support personalised monitoring, timely therapeutic intensification, nephrology referral, and preparation for advanced kidney care. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) approaches may improve risk stratification by modelling complex, nonlinear, and time-dependent patterns in routinely collected clinical data, electronic health records, and potentially multimodal data sources. Nonetheless, it remains unclear how ready these AI-driven models are for clinical use. This structured narrative review aimed to map the current landscape of AI for predicting CKD progression, assess the robustness and clinical relevance of the evidence, and identify methodological and implementation gaps that must be addressed to translate technical accuracy into clinical impact. SUMMARY: This review synthesised 35 studies published between 2020 and 2025 that developed and evaluated models to predict CKD progression. Most studies used retrospective cohort designs and electronic health record data, relying mainly on demographic variables, laboratory measures, comorbidities, and clinical history. Tree-based models, random forests, boosting methods, regression-based approaches, and neural networks were the most commonly investigated methods. Overall, the reviewed models often achieved favourable discriminative performance, as measured by AUROC or C-index. Nevertheless, the evidence base remains limited by substantial heterogeneity in study designs, cohort compositions, prediction targets, time horizons, feature engineering, and validation strategies. External validation was reported in only about one-quarter of studies, while calibration, clinical utility, patient-level uncertainty, and implementation-oriented evaluation were inconsistently addressed. Prediction endpoints were predominantly kidney failure-related. Multimodal data, including imaging, genomics, and social determinants of health, were rarely used, and explainability methods were more often applied for model description than for clinician-facing decision support. KEY MESSAGES: AI models show substantial promise for predicting CKD progression, particularly when trained on routinely available clinical data. However, the field remains more advanced in model development than in clinical validation and implementation. Future research should prioritise external and temporal validation, systematic calibration assessment, decision-curve or net-benefit analysis, comparison with established clinical risk scores, clinically meaningful prediction horizons, subgroup and fairness evaluation, patient-level uncertainty estimation, and prospective testing of model-informed care. These steps are essential to move from statistically accurate models to reliable, interpretable, equitable, and actionable tools for CKD management.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Intratumor heterogeneity in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) profoundly influences tumor progression and immune evasion. However, current prognostic models largely fail to capture the complex cellular dynamics of the tumor microenvironment (TME) at single-cell resolution. METHODS: We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing with bulk transcriptomics to derive cell-type-specific signatures. A systematic evaluation of 101 machine learning algorithm combinations was performed across multiple independent cohorts to construct a robust prognostic model. Immune landscape, mutational features, intercellular communication, and immunotherapy responsiveness were comprehensively evaluated. The biological functions of the identified hub gene, transmembrane 4 L six family member 1 (TM4SF1), were rigorously validated in vitro. RESULTS: The optimal StepCox[forward]-Ridge model showed strong prognostic stratification in five cohorts. Low-risk tumors exhibited an immune-inflamed phenotype, suggesting greater predicted good responses to immune checkpoint blockade. In contrast, high-risk tumors had an immunosuppressive TME with overactive cell communication driven by fibroblasts and myeloid cells. TM4SF1 was a key driver in this high-risk signature. TM4SF1 silencing significantly inhibited LUAD cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and strongly induced apoptosis. TM4SF1 depletion reversed tumor immune evasion by reducing PD-L1, increasing MHC-I, and lowering the secretion of CCL5. CONCLUSIONS: This single-cell-guided machine-learning framework provides strong prognostic stratification in LUAD and captures immune phenotypes associated with potential immunotherapy responsiveness. TM4SF1 emerged as a candidate mediator associated with malignant progression and immune-related phenotypes in LUAD, warranting further mechanistic and in vivo investigation. This suggests it could be a useful therapeutic target.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants increasingly implicated in respiratory disorders. However, the systems-level connections among PFAS-associated molecular perturbations, immune dysregulation, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain poorly understood. This study aimed to prioritize candidate links between PFAS-associated target information and COPD-related transcriptional and inflammatory signatures. METHODS: PFAS-associated target information was integrated with bulk transcriptomic differential expression and weighted gene co-expression network analysis to identify overlapping candidate genes. Protein-protein interaction analysis and 113 machine-learning model combinations were used for candidate prioritization and cross-cohort classification evaluation. CIBERSORT and xCell provided computational immune-cell signatures, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction applied to group comparisons and gene-signature correlations; single-cell transcriptomics provided cell-type expression context. Candidate expression was examined in cigarette-smoke-extract-treated cells, clinical samples, and public human and murine datasets. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations explored candidate PFAS-protein interactions. RESULTS: HMOX1, JUNB, CXCL12, and PTGS2 were prioritized as candidate genes overlapping PFAS-associated target information and COPD-related expression patterns. Enrichment and immune-deconvolution analyses suggested associations with inflammatory and immune-related signatures, while single-cell analysis described their distribution across annotated cell types. Exploratory plasma ELISA measurements supported higher levels of the four candidate proteins in participants with COPD, with additional expression support varying by gene and experimental model. Docking and molecular dynamics generated structural hypotheses for PFOA/PFOS-protein interactions, including HMOX1. CONCLUSIONS: This integrative systems-immunology framework delineates immune-inflammatory signatures at the PFAS-COPD interface and identifies HMOX1, JUNB, CXCL12, and PTGS2 as convergent molecular nodes. The findings do not establish exposure causality but provide a multi-scale basis for future epidemiological and mechanistic studies of how persistent environmental pollutants may contribute to COPD-associated immune and inflammatory alterations.
