papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVES: Posttransplant diabetes mellitus is a key complication after kidney transplant, linked to increased cardiovascular, infection, graft loss, and death risks. Regional data on posttransplant diabetes mellitus remain absent in the Arab world. Regional factors like consanguinity, pharmacogenomics, and hypomagnesemia are not included in current risk models. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA 2020 and MOOSE guidelines, registered with PROSPERO. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science through March 1, 2025, for studies involving adult Arab kidney transplant recipients without preexisting diabetes. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated 12-month posttransplant diabetes mellitus incidence and risk factors. We also assessed evidence certainty. RESULTS: Our analyses included 16 studies comprising 3622 kidney transplant recipients from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Egypt, Sudan, and multicenter Arab cohorts. The pooled 12-month incidence of post-transplant diabetes mellitus was 19.8% (95% CI, 16.2-23.8%; I² = 89% ). Significant risk factors (as shown by odds ratio) included age per decade (1.49), body mass index ≥25 kg/m² (1.92), prediabetes (4.28), hypertension (2.56), hepatitis C virus seropositivity (2.31), and hypomagnesemia <1.9 mg/dL (5.11), with tacrolimus versus cyclosporine showing marginal increase in risk; exclusion of a Sudanese outlier strengthened this association but remained lower than in Western populations. No study evaluated consanguinity. Evidence certainty ranged from moderate (for age, body mass index, hypertension, and hepatitis C virus) to low/very low for other factors. CONCLUSIONS: Although traditional risk factors for posttransplant diabetes mellitus remain relevant, tacrolimus showed a weaker association, possibly due to genetic variants such as CYP3A5. Hypomagnesemia represented a key modifiable risk factor. Our findings support a precision-risk framework that incorporates regional data and call for multicenter Arab registries integrating genomics, glycemia, and machine learning to improve risk stratification of posttransplant diabetes mellitus. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate findings and establish causal relationships.

papers.abstract_full: Foundation models are advancing computational pathology by transferring knowledge from large datasets to diagnostic, prognostic and treatment response tasks. Most existing models, however, either operate at the patch level or learn slide-level representations using image-based objectives, coarse tissue labels or pathology reports that vary across institutions and reflect the subjectivity inherent in narrative reporting. Here we introduce THREADS, which instead learns general-purpose whole-slide representations by aligning tissue morphology with genomic or transcriptomic profiles. THREADS was pretrained on over 47,000 hematoxylin-and-eosin-stained tissue sections and evaluated across 107 oncology tasks spanning cancer subtyping and grading, tumor microenvironment characterization, treatment response prediction and survival analysis. THREADS consistently outperformed leading whole-slide foundation models and supervised baselines while demonstrating strong transfer across external cohorts and high label efficiency. These findings establish molecularly guided pretraining as an effective strategy for learning general-purpose whole-slide representations and motivate future extensions incorporating additional molecular, spatial and clinical modalities.

papers.abstract_full: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming drug design by enabling the systematic discovery of therapeutic targets and the prediction of drug response from complex biomedical data. In papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), lymph node metastasis remains a key determinant of poor outcome, yet targetable drivers and predictive models for metastasis are lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as a functionally validated driver of lymph node metastasis in PTC. Using single-cell and spatial analyses, we show that SPP1⁺ TAMs engage TM4SF1⁺ malignant epithelial cells via the SPP1-CD44 axis within a hypoxic niche, driving tumor stemness, invasion, and metastatic progression. SPP1⁺ TAMs exhibit a hypoxic, M2-polarized phenotype and their abundance correlates with worse overall and progression‑free survival in metastatic PTC patients. We further develop an integrative machine-learning model based on SPP1⁺ TAM‑derived molecular features that predicts lymph node status with high accuracy. Preclinically, pharmacological targeting of SPP1 attenuates tumor cell migration, invasion, and lung metastasis, supporting its candidacy as a therapeutic target. Collectively, this study demonstrates how AI‑driven multi‑omics analysis can jointly identify a functionally validated target and generate a clinically deployable predictive model, illustrating a framework for bridging computational discovery with translational oncology.

papers.abstract_full: ABSTRACT  Background and Aims  Crohn’s disease and disorders of gut-brain interaction present with overlapping symptoms, and distinguishing them often requires endoscopy. We assessed whether the whole-blood transcriptome at presentation distinguishes these conditions and reflects disease activity. Methods  In a prospective two-center cohort, whole-blood RNA sequencing was performed in 425 treatment-naïve participants aged 5 to 25 years (112 Crohn’s disease, 313 disorders of gut-brain interaction). Differential expression was modeled for diagnosis and, within Crohn’s disease, for the Pediatric Crohn’s Disease Activity Index. Co-expression modules were integrated with protein–protein interaction networks, and machine learning distilled network genes into a diagnostic panel, evaluated internally and in an independent pediatric cohort. Results  Of 1,095 diagnosis-associated genes, 377 were also associated with disease activity, all with concordant direction. Five co-expression networks were perturbed, spanning neutrophil degranulation, hemostasis, interferon signaling, and T-cell and cytotoxic lymphocyte programs. A 4-gene panel (  PSTPIP2 ,  CLIC4 ,  CACNB4 ,  GZMK ) drawn from 4 networks achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of up to 0.96 in held-out samples and up to 0.93 externally, with external specificity and positive predictive value of up to 0.95 and 0.93, respectively. The panel matched or exceeded every single-network panel with fewer genes, and minimally active Crohn’s disease overlapped transcriptionally with disorders of gut-brain interaction.  Conclusions  At diagnosis, Crohn’s disease is distinguished from disorders of gut-brain interaction by a systemic signature of neutrophil and platelet activation and lymphocyte depletion that scales with disease activity. A 4-gene whole-blood panel may help prioritize symptomatic children for endoscopy and warrants prospective validation.

papers.title: AlphaGenome 2 predicts regulatory activity and variant effects across cell states
papers.abstract: Most genetic variants associated with human traits and diseases lie in non-coding DNA, where they can alter gene regulation in specific cell types and states. Single-cell atlases chart these states across tissues and development, but rarely profile enough donors to associate variants with expression directly. papers.abstract_full: Most genetic variants associated with human traits and diseases lie in non-coding DNA, where they can alter gene regulation in specific cell types and states. Single-cell atlases chart these states across tissues and development, but rarely profile enough donors to associate variants with expression directly. Deep learning models could bridge this gap by predicting variant effects from DNA sequence, yet they poorly distinguish related cell states and require fine-tuning for new datasets. Here we present AlphaGenome 2 (AG2), which substantially advances cell-type-specific prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects for gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Trained on organism-wide human and mouse single-cell atlases and bulk functional genomics data, AG2 takes as input a 1-Mb DNA sequence and a condition specifying a target tissue, cell type, or cell state. Conditioning enables AG2 to impute unmeasured epigenomic tracks and predict multimodal variant effects across cell types. Inferring this condition directly from gene expression extends AG2 to unseen datasets and cell states without fine-tuning. AG2 outperforms fine-tuned AlphaGenome 1 and specialized models trained on target datasets, doubling recall of causal single-cell eQTLs at 90% precision. AG2 also achieves state-of-the-art enhancer–gene linking and can pinpoint causal variants at complex trait loci. Across hundreds of human cell types, we generated an atlas of enhancer–gene links and scores for 7 million common variants. As single-cell profiling expands across development, tissues, and disease cohorts, AG2 provides a blueprint for turning observational atlases into variant effect maps.

papers.abstract: Abstract  Multimodal survival prediction using whole-slide images (WSIs) and genomic profiles is important for cancer prognosis; however, integrating gigapixel histopathology with high-dimensional molecular data remains challenging. papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Multimodal survival prediction using whole-slide images (WSIs) and genomic profiles is important for cancer prognosis; however, integrating gigapixel histopathology with high-dimensional molecular data remains challenging. Existing methods often rely on dense or fixed fusion strategies that may introduce redundant interactions and inadequately capture patient-specific pathology--molecular associations. We propose a sample-adaptive WSI-omics framework that constructs sparse pathway--patch interactions and combines graph-based refinement with selective state-space aggregation for patient-level survival prediction. The framework was evaluated on five TCGA cohorts using patient-level 5-fold cross-validation. Compared with SurvPath, the proposed method improved the average C-index from 0.609 to 0.638, corresponding to an absolute gain of 0.029. The improvement reached significance only in BLCA under the paired \((t)\)-test, indicating cohort-dependent statistical support. Matched profiling showed lower memory consumption than the Transformer replacement, while case-level visualizations provided model-derived pathway--patch associations. These results support sample-adaptive sparse interaction modeling for WSI-omics survival prediction. External validation, repeated-seed evaluation, and pathologist-guided interpretation remain necessary before clinical application.
bullets: Matched profiling showed lower memory consumption than the Transformer replacement, while case-level visualizations provided model-derived pathway--patch associations.
These results support sample-adaptive sparse interaction modeling for WSI-omics survival prediction.
External validation, repeated-seed evaluation, and pathologist-guided interpretation remain necessary before clinical application.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Background  Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) involves diffuse, cell-type-specific transcriptomic dysregulation in the cerebral cortex. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) has begun to resolve it, but analysis is dominated by per-gene differential expression, which tests one gene at a time and ignores the manifold structure that separates patient from control cells. Graph neural networks offer an alternative, but most approaches place genes at graph nodes and score them by local co-expression rather than by deviation from healthy cell states. Results  We present scRED, a graph-convolutional autoencoder built on a cell–cell similarity graph rather than a gene–gene graph. The model is trained on control cortical cells; the per-gene deviation in reconstruction error between patient and control cells provides the ranking statistic. Applied to the Velmeshev ASD cortex cohort across 17 cell types, scRED recovered SFARI-curated risk genes in neuronal populations at 1.98-fold enrichment against a matched, donor-disjoint control-versus-control negative control of 1.44-fold, exceeding that control in all 9 neuronal contexts (Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 0.0039); glial and endothelial populations showed no separation. Across all 17 contexts the disease contrast exceeded its negative control (p = 0.0061). The cell-graph and gene-graph formulations performed comparably (mean difference − 0.2%, p = 0.82); both exceeded a same-shape multilayer perceptron, though the primary-depth difference did not survive Holm correction. A curated gene-symbol filter applied before highly variable gene selection improved enrichment consistently (scRED vs no-filter + 1.9%, p = 0.035). Conclusions  scRED extracts cell-type-conditional disease signal concentrated in cortical neurons and not detected in the examined glial populations. The negative control shows that roughly 45% of the raw enrichment is reproduced by the matched control — reflecting scoring asymmetry together with between-donor and technical variation — leaving a residual enrichment consistent with disease, a decomposition ordinary overlap statistics do not provide. Graph-based formulations outperformed a non-graph baseline, though not after Holm correction at the primary depth, while node choice did not matter and a simple Wilcoxon rank-sum test remained competitive; we report these results without minimisation.

papers.abstract_full: Channelopathies, diseases with ion channel perturbations, are a major cause of sudden cardiac death in athletes. Advances in genetic testing have identified a growing population of athletes carrying (likely) pathogenic variants in cardiac ion channel genes who remain phenotypically silent. These genotype-positive/phenotype-negative (G+/P-) individuals present a distinct clinical challenge. Standard preparticipation screening, designed around phenotypic findings, provides little guidance for their management. A critical gap exists in providing prognostic guidance based on the involved gene, specific variants, and its molecular consequences. Beyond a critical review of existing literature, we provide a mechanistically anchored framework for variant-specific arrhythmic risk stratification across the major channelopathy genes. For each gene, we translate molecular pathophysiology into clinically actionable risk profiles and examine how exercise-specific triggers, including adrenergic surge, electrolyte shifts, and sympathovagal imbalance, interact with the underlying molecular substrate to modulate arrhythmic vulnerability. Standard diagnostic tools ranging from electro- and echocardiography, exercise stress testing, and pharmacological provocation to emerging modalities such as electroanatomic mapping and magnetocardiography are evaluated for their capacity to unmask subclinical disease and refine sports eligibility decisions. The case for an interdisciplinary sports-cardio-genetic board is made alongside a call for international collaborative registries, as existing evidence in G+/P- athletes is largely absent. The integration of artificial intelligence and telemonitoring into longitudinal athletic surveillance is discussed as a pragmatic strategy for early phenotype detection. Ultimately, guidance for the G+/P- athlete rests on a thorough understanding of the causative genetic variant and its pathophysiological consequences.
bullets: Advances in genetic testing have identified a growing population of athletes carrying (likely) pathogenic variants in cardiac ion channel genes who remain phenotypically silent.
The integration of artificial intelligence and telemonitoring into longitudinal athletic surveillance is discussed as a pragmatic strategy for early phenotype detection.
Ultimately, guidance for the G+/P- athlete rests on a thorough understanding of the causative genetic variant and its pathophysiological consequences.

papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-visualization of one or both inferior thyroid arteries (ITAs) on B-mode ultrasound is regarded as an anatomical variant, but its clinical significance remains unclear. METHODS: ITA assessment was validated against computed tomography (CT) in 47 clinically referred participa…
papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Non-visualization of one or both inferior thyroid arteries (ITAs) on B-mode ultrasound is regarded as an anatomical variant, but its clinical significance remains unclear. We investigated whether ITA non-visualization reflects structural arterial abnormality and whether it is associated with carotid ultrasound markers of vascular phenotype and an adverse cardiometabolic profile. METHODS: ITA assessment was validated against computed tomography (CT) in 47 clinically referred participants who had undergone both examinations. Reproducibility was assessed in 201 participants from the IMPROVE cohort. Cross-sectional associations with cardiovascular risk factors, carotid ultrasound phenotypes, and cardiovascular risk scores were examined in 2843 participants from the same cohort without thyroid disease, classified according to the number of non-visible ITAs (0, 1, or 2). Final ITA classification was based on artificial intelligence-assisted, human-validated review. RESULTS: ITA non-visualization frequently corresponded to arterial absence, marked caliber reduction, or aberrant anatomy. After anatomical adjudication, ultrasound-CT agreement was excellent (overall concordance 0.95; Cohen's kappa 0.84). Scan-rescan reproducibility was excellent. Increasing numbers of non-visible ITAs were associated with older age (β = 0.08, P = 0.0014), higher mean carotid intima-media thickness (β = 0.046, P = 0.044), greater vascular risk-factor burden (β = 0.09, P = 0.0004), a less favorable cardiometabolic profile, and higher cardiovascular risk scores across algorithms (all P-trend <0.01). CONCLUSIONS: ITA non-visualization is unlikely to represent only an anatomical variant. It frequently reflects structural ITA abnormalities and is associated with higher mean carotid intima-media thickness and a more adverse cardiometabolic profile. These findings support evaluation of ITA non-visualization as an adjunctive descriptor of an adverse vascular phenotype.

papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Females are under-represented in cardiac amyloidosis (CA), but whether this reflects sex-associated phenotypic heterogeneity or differences in disease prevalence remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to characterize sex-associated differences in presentation and prognosis across CA subtypes using unsupervised clustering. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 2,216 patients with confirmed CA enrolled between 2010 and 2022: light-chain amyloidosis (AL) (n = 583), …
papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Females are under-represented in cardiac amyloidosis (CA), but whether this reflects sex-associated phenotypic heterogeneity or differences in disease prevalence remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to characterize sex-associated differences in presentation and prognosis across CA subtypes using unsupervised clustering. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 2,216 patients with confirmed CA enrolled between 2010 and 2022: light-chain amyloidosis (AL) (n = 583), variant transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) (n = 432), and wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRwt) (n = 1,201). Self-organizing maps with k-means partitioning were applied separately to each subtype, and conditional inference trees identified key phenotypic discriminators. RESULTS: Females represented 40.8%, 33.8%, and 15.9% of AL, ATTRv, and ATTRwt cohorts, respectively. Clustering identified 4 AL, 6 ATTRv, and 6 ATTRwt phenotypes. Across subtypes, female-predominant clusters generally showed preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, lower cardiac remodeling burden, and less pronounced biomarker elevation. Female-predominant AL clusters included preserved-function and multisystem profiles, whereas ATTRv clusters included neurologic-dominant and older cardiometabolic profiles. In ATTRwt, females were predominantly represented in a phenotype characterized by preserved systolic function and less structural remodeling. Conditional inference trees identified sex as the first discriminator in ATTRwt and a secondary discriminator in AL, whereas ATTRv clusters were primarily discriminated by cardiac variables and sex was not selected. CONCLUSIONS: Unsupervised clustering identified female-predominant phenotypes with less structural cardiac remodeling but distinct multisystem characteristics across CA subtypes. These findings support sex-associated phenotypic heterogeneity in CA and generate hypotheses regarding female underrepresentation in contemporary CA cohorts.

Clustering identified 4 AL, 6 ATTRv, and 6 ATTRwt phenotypes.
Across subtypes, female-predominant clusters generally showed preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, lower cardiac remodeling burden, and less pronounced biomarker elevation.

papers.abstract_full: Histone deacetylase 1 (HDAC1) is an important epigenetic regulatory enzyme and plays a key role in cancer development. This highlights the need for novel inhibitors targeting the HDAC1 isoform of the histone deacetylase family of proteins. Traditional high-throughput screening requires a lot of resources, and current clinical inhibitors often have poor pharmacokinetics and off-target side effects. In this study, we introduce a machine learning-driven screening pipeline that can identify novel scaffolds from large chemical libraries that are structurally viable potential HDAC1 inhibitor candidates. After comprehensive testing of machine learning models with multiple input training features, an XGBoost model combined with high-resolution ECFP6 topological fingerprints was found to be the best option for inhibitor identification. SHAP analysis revealed a strong statistical correlation between the model's highest-weighted predictive ECFP6 bits and the established Cap-Linker-ZBG pharmacophore. This understanding allowed for successful scaffold hopping by the ML model, leading to a new carboxylate-based lead (CX-2) and hydroxamate-based (HX-1 and HX-2) compounds as potential inhibitor candidates. Further molecular docking and 200 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations showed that these compounds perform comparably to existing HDAC1 inhibitors (Vorinostat and Valproic acid). MM-PBSA energy approximations showed a potential (pharmacophoric compensation) profile for the carboxylate-based CX-2, where favorable Van der Waals interactions from its cap and linker regions theoretically compensate for a weaker zinc-binding group to maintain comparable estimated binding free energies. Furthermore, in-silico ADME profiling indicated that the prioritized candidates comply with Lipinski's rule of five and exhibit favorable predicted physicochemical properties. This integrated ML and cheminformatics workflow successfully identified novel in-silico candidate scaffolds against HDAC1, demonstrating an efficient computational pipeline to accelerate the discovery and prioritization of epigenetic inhibitor candidates.

papers.abstract_full: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force in oncology, fundamentally shifting cancer care from empirical paradigms to data-driven precision medicine. Modern oncology generates unprecedented volumes of high-dimensional data, including radiomics, digital pathology, and multiomics, which are increasingly harnessed by deep learning architectures like Vision Transformers and U-Nets to characterize tumor phenotypes and heterogeneity. However, despite these algorithmic breakthroughs, critical translational bottlenecks-such as "black box" opacity, cross-institutional batch effects, and the lack of integration into electronic health records-severely impede real-world clinical deployment. This structured narrative review synthesizes the application of multimodal AI frameworks across the entire oncological continuum, from CRISPR-based target discovery and morphological-genomic bridging to reinforcement learning-driven intelligent radiotherapy and clinical decision support systems. We further evaluate emerging paradigms, including federated learning, explainable AI, and patient digital twins, as emerging approaches to address key translational challenges. By bridging the gap between in silico discovery and prospective validation, this review provides a strategic roadmap for the integration of robust, mechanistically transparent AI frameworks. Ultimately, this synthesis underscores the potential for AI to deliver dynamic, life-cycle-managed care, supporting the future translation of patient-centered precision oncology into routine clinical practice.
bullets: We further evaluate emerging paradigms, including federated learning, explainable AI, and patient digital twins, as emerging approaches to address key translational challenges.
By bridging the gap between in silico discovery and prospective validation, this review provides a strategic roadmap for the integration of robust, mechanistically transparent AI frameworks.

Ultimately, this synthesis underscores the potential for AI to deliver dynamic, life-cycle-managed care, supporting the future translation of patient-centered precision oncology into routine clinical practice.

papers.abstract_full: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory bowel disease characterised by continuous inflammation and ulceration of the colonic mucosa, resulting from complex interactions among genetic susceptibility, environmental factors, intestinal barrier dysfunction, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and dysregulated immune responses. Although conventional therapies, including aminosalicylates, corticosteroids, immunomodulators, biologics, and small-molecule drugs have improved disease control, their clinical utility remains limited by incomplete therapeutic responses, adverse effects, loss of efficacy, and difficulties in achieving sustained remission. The present review offers an in-depth view of the emerging trends in molecular pharmacology and future drug-delivery systems for UC. UC-relevant molecular targets and pathological features of the colonic microenvironment be matched to site-specific or stimulus-responsive delivery strategies to improve local therapeutic exposure while limiting systemic toxicity, and clinical translation have been described. We discuss recent therapeutic advances targeting key inflammatory pathways (e.g. TNF-α, JAK-STAT, TYK2, IL-23/Th17, S1P receptors and PPAR-γ) and microbiome-directed approaches (e.g. faecal microbiota transplantation, microbial metabolites and postbiotics). Biomarker-driven approaches, such as faecal calprotectin and microbiota profiling, are emphasised as key components of precision medicine and treatment monitoring. Advanced Drug delivery mechanisms such as liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, solid lipid nanoparticles, hydrogels, microparticles, nanogels and multifunctional theranostic systems provide opportunities for colon-specific drug delivery, controlled release, improved bioavailability, improved mucosal targeting and decreased systemic exposure. New approaches based on RNA-based therapeutics, CRISPR/Cas technologies and artificial intelligence-assisted drug delivery system design further increase the possibilities of personalised treatment. To summarise, the combination of molecularly targeted pharmacology with intelligent and site-specific drug-delivery technologies is an exciting avenue for enhancing therapeutic efficacy and reducing treatment-related toxicity and for furthering personalised management of UC. However, translation to widespread clinical practice will need to overcome challenges related to biocompatibility, gastrointestinal variability, scalability, manufacturing, controlled release, and regulatory approval.

papers.abstract_full: Liquid biopsy has developed rapidly over the past decade and now contributes to several defined areas of oncology practice. Here, we offer an expert opinion on the biological foundations, technological platforms, clinical evidence base, commercial ecosystem and market trajectory of blood-based cancer diagnostics as of mid-2026. We critically evaluate the four principal circulating analytes, cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and its tumour-shed fraction circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA), circulating tumour cells (CTCs), extracellular vesicles (EVs) and tumour-educated platelets (TEPs), alongside the analytical platforms that extract clinically actionable signals from them, including high-sensitivity next-generation sequencing, digital droplet polymerase chain reaction, enzymatic and immunoprecipitation-based methylome profiling, genome-wide fragmentomics, long-read sequencing platforms and the increasingly central role of artificial intelligence in multi-omic signal integration. The principal prospective trials are appraised with attention to both their findings and their limitations, including DYNAMIC, TRACERx, IMvigor011, PATHFINDER 2, the National Health Service (NHS)-Galleri and ECLIPSE. The full spectrum of Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved companion diagnostics is reviewed in conjunction with the rapidly maturing startup ecosystem, which spans multi-cancer early detection, minimal residual disease monitoring and circulating-tumour-cell-based multi-omics, alongside the consolidating mergers and acquisitions landscape, with explicit reference to announcements made at the 2026 meetings of the American Society of Clinical Oncology and the American Association for Cancer Research. Non-plasma biofluid substrates including cerebrospinal fluid, urine, saliva and pleural fluid are also discussed for tumour-type-specific applications. The global liquid biopsy market, projected to grow from US$6.17 billion in 2024 to approximately US$22.69 billion by 2034, is analysed by technology, application and geography. We argue that, despite the technical progress documented herein, three structural barriers, namely reimbursement fragmentation, clonal-haematopoiesis-driven biological noise and the persistent absence of prospective mortality data for multi-cancer early detection, together with the fundamental biological limits on ctDNA shedding in low-shedding tumour types and in early-stage disease, must be resolved before liquid biopsy can be applied effectively at the population level.

papers.abstract_full: Plants, being sessile organisms, have to endure unfavourable environmental conditions, thus they have developed exceptionally refined molecular systems that can sense, react and even recall stress signals. Stress memory, the ability to store information about previous stress treatments for faster and stronger reactions in the case of new exposures, is an indispensable adaptive mechanism that not only increases plant survival but also their overall fitness. Over the past few years, a considerable amount of evidence has been indicating the significance of epigenetic control in both the formation and the sustainability of stress memory, especially in the case of abiotic stress. This article presents an overview of the latest development on the epigenetic origin of plant stress memory with a focus on the mechanisms that play key role in the acclimatization to abiotic stress. The various molecular layers that are involved in the formation of stress memory viz. DNA methylation, chromatin remodelling, modifications of histones at post-translational level and the regulatory activities of non-coding RNAs have been elaborated. The stress specific epigenetic reactions due to abiotic stresses have been discussed to uncover regulatory attributes. Moreover, the review discusses the merging of cutting-edge technologies such as multi-omics tactics, the CRISPR/dCas9-targeted epigenome editing and machine learning solutions, with the aim of developing stress tolerant and high yielding crops. Despite the substantial progress made in identifying key epigenetic components, the major hurdles exist such as causal relationships being unclear, transgenerational stress memory over multiple generations being stable over time and eventually converting lab results into practical use in agriculture.

papers.abstract_full: P-type ATPases are conserved ATP-driven ion transporters that maintain cellular ion homeostasis. Plant P-type IIB Ca2+-ATPases, known as autoinhibited Ca2+-ATPases (ACAs), are key regulators of Ca2+ signaling networks. This review summarizes the structural features, Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent regulation, evolutionary diversification, and biological functions of plant ACAs. By contributing to cytosolic Ca2+ clearance and the restoration of basal Ca2+ levels, ACAs may modulate stimulus-specific Ca2+ dynamics and participate in diverse physiological processes, including plant growth, development, stomatal movement, immunity, and abiotic stress adaptation. Comparative analyses across plant species highlight functional specialization of ACA isoforms and their potential value for crop improvement. We further discuss current challenges in ACA functional characterization, particularly the complexity of Ca2+ signaling networks and the limited understanding of ACA-associated genetic variation. Emerging approaches integrating multi-omics, artificial intelligence, and precision genome editing provide new opportunities for identifying and designing ACA alleles for climate-resilient crop breeding.

papers.abstract_full: Mycoplasma species are the minimal-genome pathogens that elicit complex host immune responses involving both protective and pathogenic inflammation. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are pivotal components of the immune system, recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and damage-associated molecular patterns to initiate immune responses. TLRs recognize Mycoplasma-derived lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA motifs, initiating NF-κB and MAPK signaling cascades. While these pathways are indispensable for microbial clearance, their dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammation, autoimmunity, and tissue damage. Consequently, selective modulation of TLR signaling has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for restoring immune homeostasis. In this study, we summarized the recent advances in delineating the molecular crosstalk between TLRs and Mycoplasma, emphasizing the distinct roles of TLRs in pathogen recognition and immunopathology. In parallel, it integrates a cheminformatics-based analysis of TLR inhibitory ligands retrieved from the ChEMBL database, encompassing over 230 compounds across TLR1-5. Multivariate visualization techniques such as principal component analysis (PCA), uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP), and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) were employed to map the chemical space and reveal receptor-specific clustering patterns. The analysis identified TLR2 and TLR4 inhibitors as occupying distinct but overlapping chemical regions, characterized by higher molecular weight, lipophilicity, and structural complexity. Correlation and similarity mapping further highlighted scaffold conservation among active ligands, providing a quantitative foundation for rational drug design and structure-activity modeling. Furthermore, we explore how machine learning (ML) and computational modeling are reshaping TLR-targeted drug discovery. ML-driven frameworks facilitate ligand prediction, virtual screening, and structure-activity optimization through deep docking and transformer-based scoring models. Integrative ML approaches also extend beyond ligand discovery to encompass multiomics data integration, biomarker identification, and predictive modeling of host-pathogen interactions and immune responses. By bridging immunological insight with cheminformatics and ML-based analytics, this article outlines a multidisciplinary roadmap for precision immunomodulation in Mycoplasma-associated diseases. The convergence of experimental pharmacology and computational intelligence holds the potential to accelerate the discovery of next-generation TLR-targeted therapeutics, advancing personalized strategies for immune regulation and infection control.

papers.abstract_full: PURPOSE: Obesity is a heterogeneous, chronic metabolic disease driven by dysregulation of energy homeostasis across interconnected central nervous system, gastrointestinal, adipose, endocrine, immune, and mitochondrial networks. Despite the established roles of lifestyle intervention and metabolic/bariatric surgery, limitations in accessibility, durability, and interindividual response have stimulated the development of mechanism-based pharmacotherapies. This review critically examines emerging therapeutic strategies targeting integrated energy-regulatory pathways and evaluates their translational potential for precision obesity management. METHODS: Current evidence was synthesized across major biological systems governing appetite, energy expenditure, and metabolic adaptation. Central melanocortin, Neuropeptide Y (NPY)/ Agouti-related peptide (AgRP), serotonergic, dopaminergic, and endocannabinoid pathways were considered alongside gut-derived incretin, amylin, Peptide YY (PYY), ghrelin, Fibroblast Growth Factor (FGF), and bile acid signaling. Emerging approaches targeting adipose remodeling, thermogenesis, mitochondrial energetics, AMPK-mTOR-sirtuin signaling, inflammation, and fibrosis were also evaluated. Genetic, epigenetic, and artificial intelligence-based approaches to patient stratification were incorporated to assess prospects for precision therapy. RESULTS: Obesity pharmacotherapy is shifting from conventional appetite suppression toward coordinated modulation of interconnected metabolic pathways. Incretin-based and multi-agonist therapies provide the strongest clinical evidence for substantial weight reduction and metabolic improvement. However, treatment discontinuation, weight regain, adverse effects, cost, and heterogeneous therapeutic responses remain major challenges. Strategies targeting adipose tissue dysfunction, mitochondrial metabolism, thermogenesis, immune-metabolic signaling, and fibrosis offer additional opportunities for disease modification, although many remain in preclinical or early clinical development. Increasing evidence for biological heterogeneity supports individualized therapeutic selection. CONCLUSION: The emerging therapeutic paradigm positions obesity as a systems-level disorder requiring mechanism-informed, individualized intervention. Integrating CNS-gut-adipose-mitochondrial biology with multi-omics, biomarkers, and artificial intelligence may enable more durable and precise treatment. Long-term safety, durability, affordability, equitable access, and clinical validation remain essential for translation.

papers.abstract_full: Liquid biopsy offers repeated, minimally invasive molecular profiling of cancer, but its clinical value depends on the analyte, analytical platform, and intended use. In this Review, we evaluate current liquid-biopsy technologies for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment guidance, with a particular emphasize on tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (TDEVs) as a bridge between biomarker detection and therapeutic intervention. We examine genomic and epigenomic profiling, single-cell and single-vesicle analysis, and multi-omics integration as complementary approaches for assessing tumour burden, heterogeneity and treatment response. Circulating tumor DNA genotyping guides targeted therapy in selected advanced cancers, whereas many early-detection and vesicle-based applications require prospective validation. We highlight how the TDEV lipid bilayer protects diverse molecular cargo that reflects evolving tumour phenotypes and how TDEV-mediated communication contributes to metastasis, immune evasion and therapeutic resistance, creating opportunities to target pathogenic vesicle signalling. We also assess engineered vesicles from malignant and non-malignant cells as drug-delivery and cancer-vaccination platforms, while noting that tumour-derived carriers may retain oncogenic or immunosuppressive cargo. Most candidate vesicle biomarkers remain supported by retrospective studies, and therapeutic platforms are largely preclinical or in early clinical testing. We discuss the requirements for clinical translation, including reliable identification of tumour-derived vesicles, standardized workflows and prospective multicentre validation for diagnostics, and reproducible manufacturing, cargo characterization, potency testing and product-specific pharmacokinetic and safety evaluation for therapeutics. Finally, we consider how multimodal profiling and artificial intelligence might improve signal integration, and argue that clinical adoption will depend on demonstrating that vesicle-guided decisions and interventions improve patient outcomes.

papers.abstract_full: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming prostate cancer screening and early detection through the integration of clinical-risk calculators, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), digital pathology, genomics, biomarkers, and liquid biopsies. AI-enhanced risk models may improve biopsy decisions, while AI-assisted MRI interpretation can increase the detection of clinically significant disease and reduce false positives, unnecessary biopsies, and overdiagnosis. Digital pathology algorithms may support more reproducible tumor identification, Gleason grading, and prognostic stratification. Genomic risk scores, kallikrein-based tests, and emerging circulating biomarkers further enable precision screening by identifying men at elevated risk and refining the selection for imaging or biopsy. However, most available systems address isolated components of the diagnostic pathway, and evidence from prospective, real-world screening populations remains limited. Clinical implementation therefore requires external validation, screening-specific calibration, implemented reference standards, and workflow integration. Ultimately, multimodal AI may enable a "virtual biopsy" that combines imaging, molecular, pathological, and clinical data to deliver personalized, noninvasive prostate cancer assessment.

papers.abstract_full: Thermophilic fungi are eukaryotic microorganisms adapted to elevated temperatures, occupying niches such as composts, self-heating plant residues, soils, animal-associated habitats, and other thermally enriched environments. Their capacity to survive and remain metabolically active under thermal stress rests on physiological and molecular adaptations, including membrane stabilization, heat-shock responses, genome compaction, and the production of thermostable enzymes (thermozymes). These fungi produce a wide repertoire of industrially important enzymes, among them cellulases, xylanases, beta-glucosidases, mannanases, proteases, amylases, pullulanases, lipases, laccases, phytases, and pectinases, which retain catalytic activity under harsh processing conditions. Thermozymes are applied in biomass conversion, biofuel production, food and feed processing, pulp and paper manufacturing, textile processing, and environmental biotechnology. This chapter reviews the diversity, taxonomy, ecology, physiology, and adaptive mechanisms of thermophilic fungi, with particular emphasis on the molecular basis of enzyme thermostability. It then surveys fungal isolation, enzyme screening, fermentation-based production, downstream processing, heterologous expression, and the use of agro-industrial residues as sustainable substrates. Emerging tools, including genome mining, metagenomics, protein engineering, synthetic biology, artificial intelligence, and multi-omics approaches, are examined as accelerators of thermozyme discovery and optimization. Major gaps persist in the exploration and functional characterization of thermophilic fungal biodiversity. Integrating genomics, bioinformatics, and industrial bioprocess engineering should further advance the discovery, development, and commercialization of these enzymes in support of sustainable biotechnology and the emerging bioeconomy.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Continuous ambient air quality networks in riverine megacities exhibit multi-scale spatial dependencies poorly captured by isotropic geostatistics. We establish a Topological Data Analysis (TDA) and spatial graph framework evaluating sensor network geometry across 13 regulatory stations bisecting the lower Hooghly River conurbation. Using spherical Haversine metrics and Gaussian radial basis functions, we benchmark the network against classical graph hierarchies (Delaunay, Gabriel, Relative Neighborhood, and Minimum Spanning Tree) alongside Ripley K and Besag L-functions. Vietoris-Rips simplicial filtration yields exact persistent homology invariants. Zero-dimensional homology (H0) reveals three-stage hierarchical percolation with conurbation consolidation at eps = 14.50 km (mean lifespan L0 = 4.16 km; persistent entropy E0 = 3.18 bits), verifying Kruskal/Boruvka duality with the MST edge spectrum (L = 49.88 km). One-dimensional homology (H1) isolates a transient trans-river 1-cycle (Delta eps = 25.1 m), confirmed via Monte Carlo coordinate perturbation (sigma_jitter in [10, 500] m) as an ephemeral coordinate discretization artifact. Grounding the filtration in empirical telemetry (PM2.5, PM10, NO2), Moran I(eps) transitions from localized clustering (I = +1.017 at eps = 2.0 km) to random expectation (I = -0.083) at the eps = 7.0 km consolidation scale, aligning with semivariogram practical range (a_prac = 5.29 km). Finally, on binary filtration graphs, we prove combinatorial Laplacian proportionality to Geary contiguity ratio C(eps), and formulate a topological embedding tensor H_TDA in R^(13x6) for topology-aware graph neural networks.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Carotid atherosclerosis remains a major contributor to cerebrovascular events, with macrophage-driven inflammation playing a pivotal role in disease progression. This study employed an integrative multi-omics approach combining bulk RNA sequencing and weighted gene correlation network analysis to identify critical differential expression genes in atherogenesis. Machine learning algorithms (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator, random forest and artificial neural network) prioritized Toll Like Receptor 1 as the most significant risk gene. Single-cell sequencing of carotid plaques demonstrated TLR1 was predominantly distributed in macrophages. Experimental validation in mouse bone marrow primary macrophages confirmed that coriander inhibits TLR1-mediated macrophage inflammatory response in carotid plaques. Immune infiltration analysis showed that TLR1 was closely related to neutrophil and macrophage activation. Our findings establish TLR1 as a macrophage-specific diagnostic biomarker and suggest that ingestion of coriander supplementation inhibits the inflammatory amplification circuit in TLR1-mediated advanced atherosclerosis.

papers.abstract: Abstract  Background  Single-cell genetic variation research has expanded rapidly with advances in sequencing technologies and computational approaches and is increasingly important for investigating cellular heterogeneity, clonal evolution, and disease-associated genomic alterations. papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Background  Single-cell genetic variation research has expanded rapidly with advances in sequencing technologies and computational approaches and is increasingly important for investigating cellular heterogeneity, clonal evolution, and disease-associated genomic alterations. However, key methodological and experimental information is often dispersed across full-text publications, limiting systematic characterization of the field. To address this, we combined large-scale literature analysis with full-text structured information extraction assisted by the large language model (LLM) ChatGPT-4o to characterize technological, methodological, and application trends in single-cell genetic variation research. Results  Information on sequencing technologies, variant types, disease applications, species, and variant detection tools was systematically extracted and organized. ChatGPT-4o-assisted extraction achieved a mean correctness of 82.50% and a mean completeness of 83.05% compared with manually curated annotations. Single-cell genetic variation research has expanded rapidly, accompanied by increasing international and institutional collaboration. scRNA-seq remains the predominant technology, while scATAC-seq, scDNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and multi-omics combinations are increasingly adopted. Cancer is the major application area, with tumor microenvironment, prognosis, and immunotherapy as prominent themes. SNVs remain the most extensively studied variant type, whereas combined SNV-CNV analyses are becoming more common, particularly in cancer studies. Bulk-oriented tools such as GATK remain widely used, while single-cell-specific methods are increasingly adopted to address low coverage, allelic dropout, and technical noise. Conclusions  Single-cell genetic variation research is evolving toward integrated multi-omics, multi-variant analysis, and more specialized single-cell computational strategies. The increasing adoption of multi-omics technologies and single-cell-specific methods reflects the growing complexity and maturity of the field. Combining large-scale literature analysis with LLM-assisted full-text information extraction provides a systematic approach for capturing complex methodological and biological information and identifying emerging directions in single-cell genomics.

papers.abstract_full: Rice blast caused by Magnaporthe oryzae threatens rice production, and genomic prediction may accelerate identification of resistant germplasm. We evaluated classical machine-learning and simulated quantum-kernel models for binary and three-class prediction of leaf blast (BL) and panicle blast (PB) resistance in 204 rice accessions with 2,120 repeated phenotypic observations. Models used 328,597 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), 104,068 phased haplotypes, or 49,451 unphased haplotypes. Binary prediction outperformed three-class prediction. The highest binary macro-F1 scores were 0.87 for BL and 0.73 for PB. Phased and unphased haplotypes reduced predictor dimensionality by 68.3% and 85.0%, respectively, while retaining broadly comparable performance. Quantum support vector classification achieved competitive results in selected binary tasks but did not consistently exceed the strongest classical models. These findings establish a benchmark for SNP- and haplotype-based prediction of rice blast resistance and for evaluation of quantum machine learning in crop genomics.

papers.title: Sparrowhawk: harnessing WebAssembly for private microbial genomics, and beyond
papers.abstract: Computational methods are a growing component of every scientific discipline, but the pace of training and expertise for using these methods has not kept up with their widening usage. Researchers expect state-of-the-art methods to be able to independently explore their results, and do so dynamically and interactively. papers.abstract_full: Computational methods are a growing component of every scientific discipline, but the pace of training and expertise for using these methods has not kept up with their widening usage. Researchers expect state-of-the-art methods to be able to independently explore their results, and do so dynamically and interactively. Producing such an application which implements a new algorithm, even though it would access a much wider audience, is typically beyond the expertise and time constraints of computational method developers. Here, we show our Sparrowhawk framework can rapidly create an interactive web application to run interactive analysis on a user's machine, across a wide range of algorithms.  Focusing first on genomic epidemiology, a domain with a specific need for such methods, we created novel lightweight methods for genome assembly, antimicrobial resistance gene annotation, and taxonomic identification. Our results exceed performance of previous lightweight methods, and produce results that reproduce or closely match previous analysis pipelines. By using WebAssembly, our framework benefits from not requiring installation, command line knowledge, or transferring sensitive data over an internet connection.  We show how algorithms from other researchers, and spanning fields from machine learning to physics, can rapidly be ported to web tools using our framework. We demonstrate an immediate impact on microbial bioinformatics, but expect that uptake of Sparrowhawk by developers of other tools broadly will help other researchers, and create new tools for teaching and public engagement. Thanks to the broad availability and familiarity with web browser tools across society, Sparrowhawk has the potential to significantly lower the barrier to entry to advanced computational methods.

papers.abstract: The CRISPR/Cas9 system has emerged as a revolutionary tool with diverse applications in genome engineering; however, the role of nanoscale hydrogen bonds between single nucleotides in precision editing remains unknown. We showed that the A-rich Cas9 editors exhibit stronger editing ou…
papers.abstract_full: The CRISPR/Cas9 system has emerged as a revolutionary tool with diverse applications in genome engineering; however, the role of nanoscale hydrogen bonds between single nucleotides in precision editing remains unknown. Here we systematically compared A-rich and G-rich PAM-recognizing Cas9 editors through comprehensive analyses of ~37,000 targeting sites with about half million libraries of ~0.36 billion types of editing outcomes. We showed that the A-rich Cas9 editors exhibit stronger editing outcome predictability in comparison with the conventional Cas9 editor of the G-rich PAM. In addition, the A-rich Cas9 editors induce a higher frequency of staggered cleavages, resulting in predictable editing with donor-independent templated insertions. Moreover, we identified distinct DNA sequence motifs for predictable insertions with the A-rich Cas9 editors. In particular, we revealed single nucleotides at the -4 position as MMEJ microhomologies in precision engineering via two or three hydrogen bonds with A-rich or G-rich PAM, respectively. Furthermore, we found that PolQ plays a key role in enhanced random insertions. Finally, we developed a discrete-space diffusion model CRIfuser of deep learning for predicting editing outcomes with staggered cleavage. Together, these findings establish PAM-dependent cleavage geometry as a tunable determinant of Cas9 editing outcomes and provide a framework for predictive and precision genome engineering.
bullets: Moreover, we identified distinct DNA sequence motifs for predictable insertions with the A-rich Cas9 editors.
Furthermore, we found that PolQ plays a key role in enhanced random insertions.
Together, these findings establish PAM-dependent cleavage geometry as a tunable determinant of Cas9 editing outcomes and provide a framework for predictive and precision genome engineering.

papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) complicates bacterial infection management, motivating genomic approaches to predicting antibiotic susceptibility. This study assessed the predictive performance and generalisability of machine-learning models using resistance-associated genomic features from Escherichia coli. papers.abstract_full: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) complicates bacterial infection management, motivating genomic approaches to predicting antibiotic susceptibility. This study assessed the predictive performance and generalisability of machine-learning models using resistance-associated genomic features from Escherichia coli. Publicly available genomic and phenotypic records yielded 446 genomes, 252 binary genomic features and 1,935 susceptibility observations across nine antibiotics. Logistic Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost classifiers were compared using validation ROC-AUC, followed by evaluation on held-out test subsets. Additional analyses examined identical genomic feature profiles across partitions, performance across source publications and feature redundancy. Ampicillin and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole achieved held-out accuracies of 93.98% and 93.59%, ROC-AUC values of 0.912 and 0.954, and resistant-isolate recall of 95.16% and 94.55%, respectively. In contrast, ceftazidime achieved 88.52% accuracy and 0.940 ROC-AUC but identified only 22.22% of resistant isolates. Seventy-four held-out observations shared identical 252-feature profiles with training isolates; all were correctly classified. After excluding overlapping observations without retraining, ROC-AUC decreased from 0.912 to 0.848 for ampicillin and from 0.954 to 0.901 for trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Exploratory cross-publication evaluations showed variable performance, with shared multilocus sequence types in 16 of 18 comparisons. Reducing genomic features did not materially alter validation performance in the two antibiotics examined. These findings indicate that genomic predictors can discriminate resistance phenotypes, but aggregate accuracy may obscure poor resistant-isolate detection. The findings also distinguish performance on conventionally held-out isolates from performance on previously unseen resistance-feature profiles, an important consideration when bacterial population structure and correlated determinants substantially influence model evaluation. Independent phylogenetic and prospective validation remains necessary before clinical use.

papers.abstract_full: Many bacterial human pathogens infect not only humans but also other species, and source attribution has been very useful for studying transmission among the different sources. Yet, critical pathogens such as  Acinetobacter baumannii have not been studied using source attribution approaches. Here, we conducted machine source attribution using the resistome of almost 1200  A. baumannii genomes from four sources: humans, companion animals , soil, and white storks. Of note, no other study has used the resistome as input data before. First, we selected the best model among 168 parameter combinations, which was Random Forest, with 5-fold cross-validation and chi2 for feature selection. The model shows a reasonably good accuracy with an F1 weighted score = 0.744, yet class accuracy was dependent on the source. Whereas for companion animals and humans, 93% and 86% of the predictions were correct, respectively; the other two categories (soil and white stork) show correct predictions below 50%. Yet, a core phylogeny and ST assignment reveal that the wrong predictions are associated with multi-host lineages. Finally, we identify the most important ARGs contributing to each class prediction and, in the case of companion animals,  tet genes, which confer resistance to tetracycline, were among the top contributors. Our study shows the resistome's potential for developing models to predict source associations. More broadly, this study shows how integrating machine learning and phylogenomics can help us understand multi-host transmission dynamics.

papers.abstract_full: Large-scale pretraining can improve scRNA-seq representations through  measurement enrichment : estimating what the same measurement would reveal at greater UMI depth under the same measurement process. We introduce scUNVEIL, a self-supervised model trained through next-UMI prediction. We show that the Bayes-optimal next-UMI predictor is the posterior mean of the transcriptome composition that arbitrarily deep sequencing would reveal. Because UMI identities are exchangeable conditional on transcriptome composition, scUNVEIL operates directly on count vectors using a residual multilayer perceptron, without attention over gene tokens. The measurement-enriched transcriptome composition is predicted from a single low-dimensional hidden state, which therefore serves naturally as the cell embedding. The same model provides both reusable cell representations and measurement-enriched gene-expression estimates. scUNVEIL was pretrained without labels or auxiliary metadata on approximately 92 million human cells spanning diverse tissues. Under linear evaluation on fine-grained cell-type annotation, its zero-shot representations achieved the best performance among the evaluated methods, while providing over 1000× faster inference than the strongest evaluated transformer-based foundation model and matching that model’s predictive performance using 88% fewer input UMIs per cell. Further evaluations show that these representations improve prediction of tumor reactivity, mitochondrial membrane potential, cell morphology, and lineage-associated treatment outcomes.

papers.abstract_full: Single-cell multi-omics data offer an opportunity to resolve how gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are rewired during cell-fate transitions, but most existing methods infer static snapshots, ignore temporal dependencies or assume linear regulation. Here we present DRAFT, a deep learning framework that combines graph attention with recurrent temporal memory to infer dynamic GRNs from time-resolved single-cell multi-omics data. On simulated data, DRAFT outperforms existing methods in accuracy and temporal smoothness. In mouse cellular reprogramming and  Drosophila adult spermatogenesis, it recovers interactions supported by independent ChIP-seq, perturbation and Hi-C data, together with known stage-specific regulators. By inferring regulatory activity from dynamic network structure rather than expression alone, DRAFT identifies regulators whose activity precedes their transcriptional peak, including the candidate early germline regulator  Mondo . Germline-specific  Mondo knockdown alters germline stem cell number and expression of the predicted targets  kuz and  mamo . DRAFT also enables nonlinear alignment of co-developing lineages and reveals stage-specific cell–cell communication.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background  Accurate prediction of single-guide RNA (sgRNA) activity is critical for effective CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing. Despite substantial advances in computational modeling, existing approaches remain limited by suboptimal predictive performance, restricted generalizability across diverse Cas9 variants, and insufficient interpretability. Results  We present TransformerCas9, an interpretable Transformer-based framework that integrates multi-scale K-mer encoding with a hierarchical attention mechanism to simultaneously capture local sequence features and long-range contextual dependencies, offering a new framework for accurate sgRNA activity prediction. Systematic analyses of the contributions of key architectural components and biological features further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. On the HT_Cas9_Test benchmark dataset, TransformerCas9 achieves a Spearman correlation coefficient of 0.788 and a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.790, surpassing all evaluated baseline models. Furthermore, across seven datasets encompassing wild-type, high-fidelity, and PAM-flexible SpCas9 variants, TransformerCas9 consistently outperforms six state-of-the-art approaches, achieving the highest performance on five datasets and the best overall ranking among all evaluated methods. Interpretability analyses leveraging intrinsic attention weights, Integrated Gradients attribution paired with in silico perturbation, and complementary explanation approaches consistently highlight biologically relevant sequence determinants associated with sgRNA activity, supporting the biological plausibility of the learned representations. Conclusions  O  ur work introduces TransformerCas9 as an accurate, robust, and interpretable framework for sgRNA activity prediction, which adopts multi-scale K-mer encoding, multi-head self-attention mechanism and a tailored MLA module to learn comprehensive sequence representations, providing a practical tool for CRISPR guide RNA design.

papers.abstract_full: ABSTRACT  De novo peptide sequencing reads peptides directly from tandem mass spectra, but none of the released deep learning models can sequence peptides labeled with isobaric tags such as TMTpro, which are widely used for multiplexed quantitative proteomics. We extended the residue vocabulary of Casanovo with TMTpro tags and phosphorylation, fine-tuned it on 21 million spectra from our laboratory, most of them TMTpro-labeled, and re-ranked the candidates in the beam by their agreement with the measured precursor mass. The resulting model, Casanovo-TMT, predicted the exact peptidoform for 84.7% of the TMTpro-labeled spectra in our test set and for 87.4 and 79.6% of the spectra in two public global-proteome datasets from other laboratories, whereas the extended vocabulary without fine-tuning gave 0.3%. Discarding the lowest-scoring predictions raised precision to 95% while retaining 81.7% of the test spectra. Casanovo-TMT also predicted the exact peptidoform for 69.2% of the spectra in a public phosphopeptide-enriched dataset and for 66 to 72% of the phosphopeptide spectra in three phosphoproteomic studies from our laboratory that were not used for training. In these studies, it identified numbers of phosphopeptides comparable to or larger than those of database search engines, and proportionally more where database search identified fewer. For the phosphopeptides identified only by Casanovo-TMT, entrapment estimated that more than 90% were correct, and an independent search engine assigned the same sequence to 95 to 98% of the spectra that it identified with confidence. Casanovo-TMT can therefore extend database search in TMTpro-based quantitative proteomics, particularly in studies in which database search identifies few phosphopeptides.

papers.abstract_full: How transcription factors (TFs) selectively recognize their genomic targets among numerous sites containing similar DNA motifs remains an open question. Cooperative binding at neighboring motif sites is widely considered a key mechanism of TF specificity, yet its genome-wide contribution remains unclear. Machine learning models can now predict TF binding directly from DNA sequence, providing opportunities to investigate its underlying determinants. Here, we leveraged BPNet models trained on ∼2,000 ENCODE TF binding profiles to systematically assess motif cooperativity. Although detected at individual loci, cooperativity made a negligible contribution to genome-wide binding predictions. Nevertheless, the models captured differences in binding preferences between TFs with similar motif preferences, even within the same cellular environment. These findings highlight the need to critically assess prevailing assumptions and explore alternative mechanisms underlying selective TF binding.

papers.abstract_full: Identifying essential genes in bacteria is crucial for drug discovery and synthetic biology. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) evaluated via flux balance analysis remain standard, yet they rely on the often-invalid premise that mutant strains optimize for maximum growth. Recent machine learning approaches circumvent this limitation using random forests or graph neural networks on mass flow graphs (MFGs). However, data-driven tools like random forests discard network topology, while graph-based tools like MFGs decompose multi-component biochemical reactions into pairwise interactions, misrepresenting complex stoichiometry and limiting interpretability. Furthermore, existing methods remain largely uncharacterised in data-scarce regimes and cross-environmental conditions. Here, we introduce HyperGenie, a framework that integrates genome-scale metabolic models with directed hypergraph neural networks by representing metabolites as nodes and reactions as hyperedges. Operating directly on wild-type flux features, HyperGenie eliminates post-knockout optimality assumptions, achieves a 13% PR-AUC improvement over prior objective-dependent methods, and matches computationally demanding, state-of-the-art flux-sampling baselines. Using HyperGenie to guide targeted growth curve assays, we identified latent essentiality misannotations across three genes in the benchmark iML1515 dataset, which we then reconciled and validated experimentally via PCR. In data-scarce regimes, HyperGenie retained robust predictive performance (> 90% PR-AUC) when trained on as little as 40% of the data. To isolate the value of hypergraph message passing, we benchmarked HyperGenie against an independent-reaction multilayer perceptron (MLPGenie) across diverse nutrient environments and uptake rates, where HyperGenie’s hypergraph inductive bias yielded consistent accuracy gains (> 2% in glucose; > 4% across six alternative carbon sources). Notably, HyperGenie exhibits robust zero-shot cross-nutrient generalization, accurately forecasting gain-of-essentiality phenotypes on novel carbon sources, though loss-of-essentiality remains challenging. Finally, coupling hypergraph representations with SHAP attribution provides actionable mechanistic insights into metabolic rewiring, establishing a data-efficient, interpretable platform for discovering novel antibiotic targets.

papers.abstract: Missense variants in the KCNQ family of voltage-gated potassium channel genes are associated with a broad spectrum of neurological and cardiac disorders for which computational tools capable of differentiating benign and pathogenic variants are essential. papers.abstract_full: Missense variants in the KCNQ family of voltage-gated potassium channel genes are associated with a broad spectrum of neurological and cardiac disorders for which computational tools capable of differentiating benign and pathogenic variants are essential. Here, we present, to our knowledge, the first application of quantum machine learning (QML) to missense pathogenicity prediction. We employ a hybrid quantum framework combining data re-uploading quantum neural networks with quantum support vector machines and applied it to pathogenicity classification across the full KCNQ gene family. Systematic exploration of circuit architectures revealed that optimal hyperparameter choices enable the proposed quantum model to achieve predictive performance superior to or comparable to state-of-the-art classical machine learning approaches, reaching AUC-ROC values of approximately 0.94 across the full dataset. Although no clear quantum advantage is observed at present, these results demonstrate that quantum feature representations can effectively capture biologically relevant patterns in variant data and establish QML as a viable framework for future applications in computational genomics and precision medicine.

papers.abstract: Abstract  Universities need to know which factors raise students’ intention to use generative artificial intelligence and which must be present before high intention can occur. We re-analyzed an open survey of 1,242 ChatGPT-using university students from 78 Philippine institutions…
papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Universities need to know which factors raise students’ intention to use generative artificial intelligence and which must be present before high intention can occur. The hybrid structural equation and neural network analyses that dominate this literature address only the first question, rank predictors with a heuristic importance index and rarely test prediction on new respondents. We re-analyzed an open survey of 1,242 ChatGPT-using university students from 78 Philippine institutions, combining partial least squares structural equation modeling, necessary condition analysis, gradient boosting explained with Shapley values and cross-validated predictive tests. Habit was the strongest unique predictor of intention to use ChatGPT yet ranked sixth or seventh of seven on necessity under every scoring, whereas effort expectancy, with no detectable unique effect, ranked among the top three. Necessity magnitudes depended on the Likert response distributions and fell below conventional thresholds after rank transformation, so the robust result is this inverted ordering rather than the magnitudes. The three importance rankings agreed at the top and bottom, and neither the structural model nor the boosted ensemble predicted new respondents better than a linear benchmark. Separating predictors that raise intention from those that must be present gives institutions a clearer basis for sequencing support.

papers.abstract_full: Molecular and clinical profiling increasingly informs patient stratification and treatment selection in precision medicine. This transition is largely driven by high-throughput omics technologies-spanning genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiomics. These technologies provide complementary information on molecular variation in health and disease. Although analyzing a single omics layer is informative, it does not fully describe the interactions among different molecular layers. Integrating data across multiple molecular layers provides a much broader context. This multi-omics approach helps researchers map complex regulatory networks, identify candidate biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. This review outlines the current state of multi-omics in personalized medicine. We detail the basic principles and recent progress in core technologies, highlighting rapidly developing areas such as single-cell multi-omics, spatial omics, and liquid biopsies. The chapter discusses key applications in oncology, cardiovascular disease, neurodegenerative disorders, and rare diseases, showing how multi-omics improves molecular subtyping, target identification, disease mechanism analysis, and diagnostics. Furthermore, we examine the computational strategies required to integrate these large datasets, specifically addressing issues like high dimensionality, data heterogeneity, and missing values. Significant technical and translational barriers are also evaluated, alongside ethical, legal, and social implications (ELSI)-such as data quality, clinical validation, cost-effectiveness, privacy, and healthcare equity. Finally, the review looks at future directions, focusing on ongoing technological innovations, the expanding role of artificial intelligence, and the integration of digital health data. We conclude by assessing both the practical hurdles and the long-term impact of multi-omics on delivering individualized patient care.

papers.abstract_full: Aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Disulfidptosis, a novel disulfide stress-induced cell death, remains unexplored in AD. We investigated whether solute carrier family 3 member 2 (SLC3A2), a disulfidptosis-related gene, contributes to AD pathogenesis. Bioinformatic analyses of Gene Expression Omnibus datasets combined machine learning algorithms to identify SLC3A2 as a core gene. A murine AD model was established using β-aminopropionitrile and angiotensin II, with lentiviral knockdown of SLC3A2. Human aortic vascular smooth muscle cells (HAVSMCs) were challenged with BAY-876 to induce disulfidptosis. Histological staining evaluated medial degeneration and elastic fiber integrity. Disulfidptosis was assessed by measuring cystine accumulation and the protein expression of filamin A (FLNA) and NCK-associated protein 1 (NCKAP1). The involvement of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)-protein kinase A (PKA) signaling was verified by genetic knockdown of its catalytic subunit (PRKACA). We observed SLC3A2 was upregulated in AD. SLC3A2 knockdown delayed lethal aortic rupture, reduced aortic medial degeneration, decreased reactive oxygen species and cystine, while restoring glutathione and free thiols. In HAVSMCs, SLC3A2 silencing preserved filamentous actin integrity, reversed the BAY-876-induced downregulation of α-smooth muscle actin and smooth muscle 22 alpha, and restored the aberrant expression of FLNA and NCKAP1. Mechanistically, SLC3A2 knockdown reactivated the cAMP-PKA signaling axis suppressed by BAY-876, and PRKACA knockdown abrogated the protective effects of SLC3A2 silencing on oxidative stress, cytoskeletal integrity, and disulfidptosis. In conclusion, SLC3A2 drives AD progression by suppressing cAMP-PKA signaling, thereby exacerbating oxidative stress and disulfidptotic cytoskeletal collapse. Targeting the SLC3A2/cAMP-PKA axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy for AD.

Targeting the SLC3A2/cAMP-PKA axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy for AD.

papers.abstract: Sarcopenia is an age-related syndrome characterized by progressive declines in muscle mass, strength, and physical performance. To investigate the shared genetic architecture of quantitative traits relevant to sarcopenia, we integrated genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for appendicular lean mass, hand grip strength, and walking pace from the UK Biobank. papers.abstract_full: Sarcopenia is an age-related syndrome characterized by progressive declines in muscle mass, strength, and physical performance. To investigate the shared genetic architecture of quantitative traits relevant to sarcopenia, we integrated genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for appendicular lean mass, hand grip strength, and walking pace from the UK Biobank. Significant genetic correlations among these traits supported multi-trait integration, resulting in an integrated GWAS termed mtMuscleAging. A total of 405 associated loci were identified, including 78 loci with enhanced significance and 33 loci that did not reach genome-wide significance in any individual trait GWAS. Fine-mapping prioritized 538 candidate variants, while integrative post-GWAS analyses identified prioritized genes and highlighted conserved coding regions and biological pathways related to muscle, heart, pancreas, fibroblasts, and aging. Single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic analyses further contextualized these genetic findings in aging skeletal muscle and identified alterations in midkine and pleiotrophin signaling and intercellular communication. Phenome-wide association analyses identified genetic relationships between mtMuscleAging and multiple health phenotypes, including cardiovascular disorders. Machine-learning analyses based on prioritized genes captured age-associated skeletal muscle expression patterns, while drug repurposing analyses nominated candidate compounds for further experimental evaluation. Collectively, our findings characterize shared genetic variation across sarcopenia-related traits and provide loci, genes, cellular contexts, and candidate compounds relevant to muscle aging.

papers.title: Mechanomedicine in Selected Cardiovascular Diseases: From Mechanobiological Principles to Therapeutic Translation.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of death worldwide and impose a substantial socioeconomic burden. Although pharmacological and interventional therapies have advanced considerably, major gaps remain in understanding disease-driving mechanisms and preventing adverse remodeling and recurrence.
