papers.abstract_full: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of death worldwide and impose a substantial socioeconomic burden. Although pharmacological and interventional therapies have advanced considerably, major gaps remain in understanding disease-driving mechanisms and preventing adverse remodeling and recurrence. Mechanomedicine is an emerging interdisciplinary field that integrates biomechanics, mechanobiology, engineering, and clinical medicine to determine how mechanical forces regulate physiology and pathology and to translate these insights into diagnostic and therapeutic tools. The cardiovascular system is intrinsically mechanosensitive: endothelial cells, vascular smooth muscle cells, macrophages, cardiac fibroblasts, and cardiomyocytes sense shear stress, cyclic stretch, membrane tension, compression, and matrix stiffness and convert these cues into biochemical programs that shape cell phenotype, intercellular communication, inflammation, and tissue remodeling. Recent advances have enabled the characterization of disease-specific mechanical signatures, pharmacological and genetic modulation of mechanotransduction pathways, and the development of mechanically responsive biomaterials, nanomedicines, bioelectronic devices, and ultrasound-based interventions. This focused narrative review outlines the fundamental principles of cardiovascular mechanobiology and summarizes mechanomedicine strategies for atherosclerosis, myocardial infarction and adverse remodeling, hypertension, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. Evidence is predominantly preclinical, and controlled human benefit has not been established for most targeted approaches. We further discuss barriers to clinical translation-including biosafety, biomarker standardization, data integration, manufacturability, and cost-and highlight future opportunities in mechanical biomarkers, artificial intelligence-assisted personalization, and multidisciplinary therapeutic design. Mechanomedicine provides a framework for investigation, but clinical use requires validated measurements, safety, and benefit over established care.

papers.abstract_full: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality despite major advances in pharmacological therapy, interventional cardiology, and lifestyle-based prevention. Although many current treatments reduce disease burden and improve outcomes, they often fail to address the underlying molecular and genetic mechanisms driving disease progression dot CRISPR hyphen-based gene- editing systems (Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats) have introduced the possibility of directly correcting, silencing, or modulating pathogenic genetic determinants involved in cardiovascular pathology. When integrated with artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled design, prediction, and optimization tools, an AI-guided CRISPR framework may assist in prioritizing editing strategies, predicting editing outcomes, and informing delivery design, although cardiovascular-specific validation of these applications remains limited. This narrative review examines the potential role of AI-guided CRISPR technologies in cardiovascular disease. It first outlines the major pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying CVD, then reviews molecular and genetic targets that may be amenable to editing. Current CRISPR applications in cardiometabolic and cardiovascular disorders are discussed, followed by an evaluation of how AI may support guide RNA design, off-target prediction, vector engineering, and therapeutic prioritization. Finally, major translational barriers are examined, including tissue-specific delivery, editing in non-dividing cells, long-term genomic safety, disease complexity, and regulatory implementation. Although early preclinical findings are encouraging, most cardiovascular applications remain in the experimental or early translational stage, and direct evidence for integrated AI-guided CRISPR applications in cardiovascular disease remains limited and largely preclinical. Progress in this field will depend on advances in delivery science, genome engineering, computational modelling, and long-term safety validation. AI-guided CRISPR should therefore be regarded as a developing precision medicine strategy with substantial future potential rather than an immediately deployable clinical solution.

papers.abstract_full: Malignant tumors remain a major global health challenge due to their heterogeneity, poor therapeutic specificity, and frequent development of multidrug resistance. Conventional treatment strategies are often hindered by limited tumor penetration, systemic toxicity, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In recent years, nanorobots-engineered nanoscale devices with autonomous or guided navigation capabilities-have emerged as a transformative platform in precision oncology. These intelligent systems integrate active targeting, stimulus-responsive drug release, and multifunctional therapeutic modules, enabling dynamic interactions with the tumor milieu. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in nanorobot materials, modular design strategies, and propulsion mechanisms, and highlights their applications across central nervous system, breast, urological, and gastrointestinal tumors. Furthermore, we address key translational barriers, including biosafety, navigation precision, and regulatory challenges, and propose future directions leveraging artificial intelligence and clinical trial integration. By bridging materials science, robotics, and biomedicine, nanorobots hold promise to redefine minimally invasive cancer treatment paradigms.

papers.abstract_full: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remains one of the most prevalent yet underdiagnosed chronic disorders worldwide, with persistent challenges in timely diagnosis and long-term adherence to continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. Artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) have emerged as promising digital health technologies that address complementary aspects of OSA management. AI has demonstrated strong diagnostic performance under controlled conditions in automated OSA detection, severity classification, and physiological signal analysis, whereas AR is being tested as a way to improve CPAP mask fitting, patient education, and treatment engagement. However, the integration of these technologies has received little attention in either the scientific literature or clinical practice. This commentary highlights the emerging convergence of AI and AR as a novel paradigm for OSA diagnosis, treatment initiation, and self-management. Current evidence indicates that AI-driven AR applications are beginning to appear at the commercial level, yet robust OSA-specific clinical evidence remains limited. Potential applications include AR-guided home diagnostic setup, AI-assisted CPAP mask fitting and desensitization, and personalized AR-based coaching to support long-term treatment adherence. We also discuss key barriers to implementation, including the limited evidence base, algorithmic bias from training data that underrepresent some populations, the privacy of sleep and facial data, the digital divide that affects older and low-income patients, regulatory pathways, and uncertainties regarding clinical integration. Finally, we propose a research agenda, guided by implementation science frameworks, focused on feasibility, usability, patient acceptability, and comparative effectiveness against existing educational and telemedicine approaches, to determine whether AI-driven AR represents a meaningful advance in OSA care. Establishing this evidence base will be essential for translating this emerging technological convergence into routine clinical practice.

papers.abstract: Targeted drug delivery aims to enhance therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity, yet its clinical translation remains limited by the unpredictable in vivo behaviour of nanocarriers. Although a broad range of nanocarrier platforms-including lipid-, polymer-, protein-, inorganic- and biomimetic-based systems-can improve drug solubility, pharmacokinetics, lesion-site accumulation and controlled release, their performance is frequently constrained by heterogeneous disease biology, ins…
papers.abstract_full: Targeted drug delivery aims to enhance therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity, yet its clinical translation remains limited by the unpredictable in vivo behaviour of nanocarriers. Although a broad range of nanocarrier platforms-including lipid-, polymer-, protein-, inorganic- and biomimetic-based systems-can improve drug solubility, pharmacokinetics, lesion-site accumulation and controlled release, their performance is frequently constrained by heterogeneous disease biology, insufficient tissue penetration, premature clearance, immune recognition and manufacturing variability. Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a powerful strategy to address these multidimensional challenges. Machine learning, deep learning and computational modelling can support prediction of formulation-property relationships, release kinetics, nano- bio interactions, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, toxicity and patient-specific therapeutic responses. In this Review, we propose an integrated, AI-guided framework that connects rational nanocarrier design, biological-fate prediction, controlled-release engineering and clinical translation within a single development pipeline. We further articulate a "translation-by-design" principle and the concept of minimum sufficient complexity, which together distinguish this Review from earlier surveys that address these stages separately. Finally, we examine key translational barriers-including data standardization, model interpretability, scalable manufacturing, safety assessment, regulatory uncertainty and the gap between preclinical efficacy and clinical outcomes-and propose that future targeted nanomedicine should move beyond increasingly complex carrier architectures toward predictive, interpretable and clinically validated AI-integrated development pipelines. Despite these capabilities, most reported models are validated on internal or closely related data; independent external and prospective validation-the evidence required before a prediction can reliably influence formulation, manufacturing or patient-level decisions-remains the principal gap in the field.

papers.abstract: Cancer remains a foremost global public-health burden, and the inherent drawbacks of conventional treatments such as poor targeting, pronounced systemic toxicity, and frequent therapeutic resistance continue to constrain clinical outcomes. papers.abstract_full: Cancer remains a foremost global public-health burden, and the inherent drawbacks of conventional treatments such as poor targeting, pronounced systemic toxicity, and frequent therapeutic resistance continue to constrain clinical outcomes. Nanocarrier-based platforms have gained traction in precision cancer theranostics (PCT) because their size-dependent features, adaptable surface chemistry, and stimuli-responsive behavior enable more selective intervention. The present review surveys recent progress in such delivery systems, with emphasis on the design logic and functional traits of principal nanoplatforms, namely liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, inorganic nanoparticles, and biomimetic carriers. We further examine the predominant delivery mechanisms, spanning passive accumulation via the enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect, ligand-receptor-mediated active targeting, and stimuli-responsive control. The clinical maturity of different anticancer nanocarrier delivery systems is not uniform. Among these, PEGylated liposomes (Doxil®) and paclitaxel micelles (Genexol-PM®) have been successively granted marketing approval as chemotherapeutic drug delivery carriers, whereas delivery systems for gene therapy, immunotherapy, and theranostics remain largely confined to preclinical studies and early-phase clinical trials. We also appraise the key barriers to clinical translation, including biosafety assessment, scalable manufacturing, immune clearance, and regulatory evaluation, and we outline emerging directions such as personalized precision medicine, artificial intelligence-assisted design, and multimodal synergistic therapy. This review aims to inform both fundamental investigation and the clinical development of nanomedicines for precision cancer theranostics.

papers.abstract_full: With the forthcoming Euro 7 regulation, the representativeness of brake particle emissions measured under the WLTP-Brake cycle has received increasing attention. In this study, two pad materials from different vehicles were tested on a brake dynamometer under multiple driving conditions. Although PM10 emissions under the WLTP-Brake cycle complied with the regulatory limit, exceedances occurred under other conditions. Variations in PN emissions among cycles reflected the cumulative effects of preceding brake events, indicating strong temporal dependence. Machine-learning models were therefore developed to predict PN emissions and identify influential brake features. Under time-series inputs, the Transformer achieved the best predictive performance, with an R2 of 0.85 ± 0.03, while XGBoost also showed acceptable accuracy. SHAP analysis showed that high-emission tests were mainly associated with positive contributions from temperature and brake power, whereas low-emission tests were characterized by negative contributions from features such as vehicle speed. Speed was positively related to PN emissions, and brake power amplified its influence. Overall, the proposed approach enables brake particle emissions to be evaluated under diverse driving conditions and may support future brake-emission assessment and regulation.

papers.abstract_full: Decision-making in acute and critical care relies on interpretation of heterogeneous information sources under substantial time pressure. Large language models (LLMs) have been proposed as clinical decision support systems (CDSS) to aid in triage, diagnosis generation, and treatment planning. This scoping review maps the current landscape of LLM-based CDSS in acute and critical care and assesses their readiness for clinical implementation. A PRISMA-ScR-guided search of four databases (January 2026) yielded 62 studies, including 15 medical domain-adapted LLMs. Technology Readiness Levels were assigned across all 62 studies; none has progressed to clinical deployment. Within the medical LLM subgroup, medical LLMs generally outperformed their foundation model counterparts, although the evidence was heterogeneous. An exploratory PROBAST + AI-informed appraisal identified recurring methodological concerns, and thematic synthesis of implementation determinants identified regulatory constraints, workflow integration, and insufficient understanding of human-AI interaction as key barriers. This review highlights priorities for prospective validation using real-world institutional data.

papers.abstract_full: STUDY QUESTION: Can maternal biomarkers of maternal-fetal physiologic integration predict the fetal fraction of cell-free DNA in pregnancy loss? SUMMARY ANSWER: Maternal organ system biomarkers, including cardiometabolic, hepatic, renal, and thyroid markers, substantially predict fetal fraction in pregnancy loss (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristics Curve (AUC-ROC) 0.77-0.80), indicating that fetal fraction may reflect integrated maternal-fetal physiology. WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Fetal fraction, which is the proportion of cell-free DNA in maternal plasma derived from the placenta, increases with gestational age and decreases with higher maternal BMI. Existing prediction models on fetal fraction rely mainly on demographics and placental hormones, and the contribution of broader maternal organ-system biomarkers remains unclear. STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: Prospective multi-center cohort study within the Copenhagen Pregnancy Loss study with development cohort (n = 992) from a tertiary university hospital and external validation cohorts from two secondary university hospitals (n = 275 and n = 241). Enrollment was from November 2020 to February 2023. PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: Women ≥18 years with confirmed intrauterine pregnancy loss before 22 weeks at three Danish university hospitals were included. Fetal fraction was estimated from cfDNA sequencing using SeqFF. Six clinical characteristics and 36 biochemistry measurements, selected to reflect physiological domains implicated in placentation including thyroid, renal, lipid, and inflammatory markers, were analyzed using Bayesian Hurdle lognormal regression and gradient boosting models with external validation. MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: In adjusted hurdle models, higher total thyroid hormone levels were associated with adequate fetal fraction (e.g. total triiodothyronine (TT3) Odds Ratio (OR) 2.76 (95% CI 1.31-5.87); total thyroxine (TT4) OR 2.42 (95% CI 1.43-4.29)), while higher levels of creatinine and uric acid were inversely associated (e.g. creatinine OR 0.39 (95% CI 0.17-0.91); uric acid OR 0.47 (95% CI 0.26-0.90)). The magnitude of fetal fraction was additionally associated with HDL cholesterol/total cholesterol ratio, uric acid, and creatinine. A gradient-boosting model achieved AUC-ROC 0.77 in internal cross-validation and 0.80/0.78 in external validation (two secondary university hospitals), with aspartate transaminase (AST)/alanine transaminase (ALT) ratio among the strongest predictors alongside beta subunit of human chorionic gonadotropin (βhCG) and gestational age. LIMITATIONS REASONS FOR CAUTION: The cross-sectional design and pregnancy loss focus limit inference regarding the directionality between maternal biomarkers, placental health, and fetal fraction. SeqFF-based fetal fraction estimation adds measurement noise versus genotype methods, while our pre-specified biomarker panel limits scope to investigated parameters. Our findings require validation in ongoing pregnancies. WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: The findings suggest fetal fraction may reflect maternal-fetal physiologic integration rather than merely a technical quality-control parameter. The associations between fetal fraction and cardiometabolic, thyroid, hepatic, and renal markers suggest that fetal fraction may offer broader insights into maternal physiology and maternal organ system adaptation during pregnancy, influencing cell-free DNA dynamics (reflecting placental shedding, maternal clearance, and dilution). The model enables personalized clinical decision-making regarding cell-free fetal DNA test timing in pregnancy loss and thereby improving the efficiency and success rate of cell-free fetal DNA testing. Moller Foundation, the Independent Research Fund Denmark (6215-00037B), and the Pioneer Center for Statistical and Computational Methods for Advanced Research to Transform Biomedicine (SMARTbiomed), DNRF grant numbers 10.46540/6215-00037B and P4. papers.abstract_full: Phage display can identify ligands that target distinctive cell surface phenotypes, but selection outputs are often complex and difficult to interpret. Here, we developed an integrated workflow combining phage display biopanning, next-generation sequencing (NGS), machine learning (ML), and flow cytometry to discover short peptide binders associated with genotype-defined cancer contexts. Phage display was performed on lung cancer cell lines representing KRAS wild-type (WT), G12C, G12D, and G12V backgrounds, and experimental outputs were used to train a multimodal probabilistic model. From the resulting model-generated candidates, 98 nonredundant heptapeptides were selected for synthesis, and 88 were successfully solubilized and tested experimentally. Flow cytometry validation revealed heterogeneous binding behaviors, including broad pan-cellular binders and candidates with mutant-vs-WT binding preference. Extended dose-response profiling and normal-cell counter-screening enabled prioritization based on binding magnitude, curve behavior, normal-cell reactivity, and sequence developability. Overall, this study shows how whole-cell selection data sets can be analyzed computationally and experimentally to identify and prioritize peptide candidates for targeting strategies.

papers.abstract_full: The molecular mechanism of pseudoexfoliation glaucoma (PXG) is still unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate biomarkers of PXG, with the goal of providing a theoretical basis. Ten blood samples from patients with pseudoexfoliation syndrome (PEX), 10 blood samples from PXG patients, and 10 control blood samples were collected for transcriptome sequencing. A total of three candidate biomarkers (ACTA2, IL1RN, and MMP9) were identified. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that the three candidate biomarkers were involved in the regulation of the actin cytoskeleton and the leukocyte transendothelial migration pathway. The results of the peripheral immune cell proportion analysis suggested altered peripheral immune profiles among the three groups, involving memory B-cells, CD8+ T-cells, regulatory T-cells, M0 macrophages, and resting CD4+ memory T-cells. Correlation analysis further revealed associations between the candidate biomarkers and these differential immune cell subsets. Exploratory drug‒gene interaction analysis provided preliminary insights for future therapeutic investigations. In an RT-qPCR validation set consisting of 15 peripheral whole blood samples (5 PEX, 5 PXG, and 5 control samples), the mRNA expression levels of the candidate biomarkers were assessed across the three groups. RT-qPCR validation revealed that ACTA2 and MMP9 were significantly upregulated in PXG patients compared with controls, whereas ACTA2, MMP9, and IL1RN were elevated in PEX patients compared with both controls and PXG patients. Collectively, these findings suggest that the three candidate biomarkers may be associated with PEX/PXG-related molecular alterations.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) arises at a microbially exposed mucosa, but the relationship between tumor transcriptional programs and host responses to Candida albicans is uncertain. We sought direction-consistent genes shared with short-term C. albicans stimulation and assessed their diagnostic, cellular, pathway, and tissue contexts. METHODS: We directionally integrated four paired C. albicans-stimulated/control oral-epithelial experiments (GSE56091) with 40 paired OSCC/adjacent tissues (GSE37991). Four machine-learning methods prioritized candidates, and independent bulk validation used 167 OSCCs and 45 controls (GSE30784). An exploratory ridge score was fixed in the discovery cohort and applied to the external cohort. Cellular localization and state were examined in paired single-cell profiles from seven patients (GSE198315) and an external oral-cavity subset of 10 carcinomas and three normal-mucosa samples (GSE181919). Qualitative PAS and IHC assessment used archival oral tissues from three groups, with four cases per group. RESULTS: Candida stimulation yielded 508 exploratory differentially expressed genes, and OSCC yielded 1,850; 26 of 35 overlapping genes changed concordantly. The four-method intersection comprised MMP10, CA9, and STC2; external single-gene AUCs were 0.968, 0.714, and 0.907, respectively. The three-gene score achieved an external AUC of 0.959 (95% CI 0.935-0.983), but at the discovery-derived cutoff sensitivity was 0.605 and specificity was 1.000; calibration was poor, and discrimination did not exceed MMP10 alone (DeLong P = 0.365). In GSE198315, paired epithelial pseudobulk supported MMP10 and CA9 under prespecified targeted three-gene correction (FDR = 0.0455 for both), whereas STC2 was directional but nonsignificant (FDR = 0.0665). Genome-wide FDR was approximately 0.892 for each gene, so the single-cell findings support localization and directional consistency rather than definitive genome-wide differential expression. The q95 calls showed modest overlap with CopyKAT and inferCNV (Jaccard=0.141 and 0.254, respectively). MMP10 and CA9 showed stronger pooled descriptive localization than STC2; CA9 remained hypoxia-associated. Fungal-element-compatible PAS staining provided morphological context but could neither identify species nor quantify burden. CONCLUSIONS: MMP10 and CA9 had the strongest multi-level support as direction-consistent Candida-responsive OSCC candidates, while STC2 remains exploratory. The three-gene combination is not yet a calibrated clinical model, and the 26-gene overlap defines a shared host-response pattern rather than evidence that C. albicans causes the OSCC transcriptional state.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) exhibits substantial variation in treatment response. In the phase 2 NeoSAC trial, higher baseline oxeiptosis-associated transcriptional activity was associated with pathological complete response (pCR). However, the malignant-cell and immune features underlying this transcriptional state remain poorly defined, as do the molecular factors that influence cellular susceptibility to oxidative stress. METHODS: We integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses to characterize oxeiptosis-associated tumor states and immune features in TNBC. CellChat was used to infer candidate intercellular communication patterns. An oxeiptosis-associated prognostic model was developed and evaluated in breast cancer cohorts. In MDA-MB-231 cells, ALG3 loss- and gain-of-function experiments were used to assess cellular responses to the KEAP1 activator VVD-130037. We also examined the effects of VVD-130037 alone and in combination with docetaxel on tumor-cell growth. RESULTS: TNBCs with higher oxeiptosis-associated transcriptional scores showed greater representation of memory T cells and selected dendritic and inflammatory myeloid populations. CellChat inferred differences in candidate MIF-related, SPP1-CD44, and MHC-associated communication patterns between the score-defined groups, suggesting the coexistence of immune engagement and regulatory features. A five-gene model comprising MAL2, TYMP, LIMCH1, ALG3, and PDLIM4 showed prognostic value across breast cancer cohorts, with moderate performance that varied between cohorts. VVD-130037 increased intracellular ROS and reduced AIFM1 Ser116 phosphorylation. N-acetyl-L-cysteine attenuated these responses and the accompanying growth inhibition, whereas z-VAD-fmk did not provide comparable protection against growth inhibition. ALG3 depletion reduced VVD-130037-induced ROS accumulation, attenuated AIFM1 Ser116 dephosphorylation, and decreased sensitivity to VVD-containing treatment. ALG3 overexpression promoted the VVD-associated decrease in AIFM1 Ser116 phosphorylation. VVD-130037 combined with docetaxel produced greater growth inhibition than either agent alone. CONCLUSION: Oxeiptosis-associated transcriptional states were associated with distinct malignant-cell and immune features in TNBC. In MDA-MB-231 cells, ALG3 expression modified the cellular response to VVD-130037-induced oxidative stress. These findings warrant further investigation in independent clinical and experimental models.

papers.abstract_full: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is a complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy driven by excessive complement activation. Genetic abnormalities in complement-related genes are detected in approximately half of the patients with aHUS. CD46 (membrane cofactor protein, MCP) is a transmembrane cofactor for factor I that facilitates inactivation of C3b and C4b on the cell surface. Among CD46 variants associated with aHUS, intronic variants can cause aberrant splicing and loss of cell-surface CD46. However, it is challenging to predict the pathogenicity of noncanonical splice-site variants, even with machine-learning-based algorithms. In this study, we investigated the potential pathogenicity of a novel intronic CD46 variant identified in a patient with aHUS. A 27-year-old woman presented with recurrent aHUS triggered by COVID-19 infection and was treated with eculizumab. She had no family history of aHUS. Following treatment with eculizumab and methylprednisolone pulse therapy, her laboratory findings improved, and she was discharged on day 15 of hospitalization. Genetic analysis revealed a homozygous intronic variant, c.287-5T>C, in the CD46 gene. Although in silico analysis predicted a low likelihood of pathogenicity, we performed further genetic and expression analysis of CD46 in the patient and her asymptomatic heterozygous mother. Flow cytometry showed markedly reduced CD46 expression on peripheral blood mononuclear cells, whereas her heterozygous mother exhibited decreased but detectable expression. RT-PCR demonstrated exon 3 skipping in the patient's transcript, resulting in a premature termination codon. A minigene splicing assay reproduced the same exon-skipping event observed in the peripheral blood cDNA. These findings indicate that the novel homozygous CD46 intronic variant c.287-5T>C, whose pathogenicity could not be established by in silico prediction alone, causes aHUS via aberrant splicing and loss of cell-surface CD46 expression. This study highlights the crucial role of functional validation in interpreting noncanonical splice-site variants in complement-mediated diseases.

papers.abstract_full: The widespread use of antibiotics in various fields has resulted in rising contamination of environmental and food systems. Antibiotic residues accumulation poses serious risks like antimicrobial resistance, ecological imbalance, allergic reactions, and long term toxicity. Consequently, the accurate and precise quantification of antibiotic ion various samples are very important. Gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) have unique properties and emerged as one of the most promising nanomaterials having extensive application in various fields. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in AuNPs based optical sensors for quantification of antibiotics. At first, the fundamental optical and physicochemical properties of AuNPs are discussed, followed by an overview of surface modification strategies and molecular recognition approaches. Subsequently, the major signal amplification mechanisms including aggregation-induced plasmonic shifts, fluorescence quenching/enhancement, hot-spot engineering, catalytic amplification, and enzyme-assisted systems are critically examined. Recent progress in spectrophotometric, SERS, fluorescence, and chemiluminescence sensors is systematically reviewed with emphasis on sensing mechanisms, analytical performance, and practical applications. In addition, attention is devoted to portable and point-of-care sensing platforms such as paper based devices, lateral flow immunoassays (LFIA), smartphone integrated systems, wearable sensors, and microfluidic analytical systems. Comparative evaluation of different sensing approaches highlights their strengths and limitations regarding sensitivity, reproducibility, cost, portability, multiplexing capability, and commercialization potential. Finally, current challenges including nanoparticles stability, matrix interferences, reproducibility, regulatory approval, and large-scale production are discussed together with future perspectives focusing on artificial intelligence assisted sensing, multifunctional nanostructures, integrated microfluidics, and next-generation smart diagnostic systems.

papers.abstract: Emerging and re-emerging viral diseases represent one of the most significant threats to global health security in the 21st century. Viruses, and RNA viruses in particular, exploit distinctive evolutionary mechanisms-including high mutation rates, recombination, and reassortment-to cross species barriers, adapt to novel hosts, and achieve pandemic potential. papers.abstract_full: Emerging and re-emerging viral diseases represent one of the most significant threats to global health security in the 21st century. Viruses, and RNA viruses in particular, exploit distinctive evolutionary mechanisms-including high mutation rates, recombination, and reassortment-to cross species barriers, adapt to novel hosts, and achieve pandemic potential. This narrative review examines the virological underpinnings of viral emergence and re-emergence, with particular focus on RNA virus biology, host adaptation dynamics, zoonotic spillover events, and the anthropogenic drivers-deforestation, agriculture, mining, and urbanisation-that create opportunities for spillover. Evidence was identified through a structured narrative search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (January 2000-October 2026). We analyse five case studies-SARS-CoV-2, influenza A (with emphasis on H5N1 in cattle), Ebola virus disease (including the 2026 Bundibugyo virus epidemic), Nipah virus, and Zika virus-to illustrate how genomic plasticity and ecological disruption interact to generate novel threats. The review critically evaluates the WHO R&D Blueprint priority pathogen framework-which prioritises viral threats including Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus, filoviruses, coronaviruses (MERS-CoV, SARS), henipaviruses (Nipah, Hendra), Lassa fever virus, Rift Valley fever virus, Zika virus, and the placeholder 'Disease X'-and assesses current global surveillance, genomic sequencing, artificial-intelligence (AI)-enabled analytics, and preparedness strategies. We identify critical gaps including inequitable access, fragmented One Health governance, underdeveloped broad-spectrum antiviral pipelines, and the uneven deployment of AI-enabled surveillance. We recommend integrating virological intelligence into pandemic preparedness frameworks to enable earlier and more targeted responses to emerging viral threats.

papers.abstract_full: Recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) vectors are the predominant modality for delivering gene therapies to treat genetic diseases across multiple organ types. Capsid and genomic payload designs ultimately define the optimal efficacious dose that is potent and safe. Vector doses are dependent on calculated titers, which are typically defined by the abundance of encapsidated vector genomes detected in a purified production batch. Over the last ten years, advanced sequencing methods have been developed to characterize individual molecular species that are packaged into rAAV particles. These approaches have revealed that every vector production batch can harbor vector genomes that deviate from the expected full-length sequence. Unfortunately, the molecular heterogeneity of a production batch is concealed by only depending on a vector's titer to determine an effective dose. Unaccounted for molecular sub-species in vectors may have unknown biological consequences. Here, we review genetic and manufacturing influences on genome integrity, the analytics and bioinformatic tools developed to characterize genome integrity, potential biological outcomes associated with different molecular populations, and the implementation of machine-learning approaches that can expedite the development of optimal vector designs during early research phases of testing novel rAAVs.

papers.abstract: Hypoxia is a key feature of the bladder cancer tumor microenvironment, but its cellular organization, prognostic value, and functional effectors remain incompletely defined. papers.abstract_full: Hypoxia is a key feature of the bladder cancer tumor microenvironment, but its cellular organization, prognostic value, and functional effectors remain incompletely defined. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk transcriptomic cohorts, machine-learning modeling, immune deconvolution, spatial transcriptomics, and functional experiments to characterize hypoxia-driven tumor microenvironment remodeling in bladder cancer. Single-cell analysis showed that hypoxia-related activity was enriched in malignant epithelial and stromal compartments and was associated with altered tumor-stromal communication. In bulk cohorts, high hypoxia activity was linked to poor overall survival and activation of aggressive biological programs. By integrating hypoxia-associated differentially expressed genes, WGCNA-derived module genes, and survival-related genes, we developed a six-gene Bladder Cancer Hypoxia-Related Signature (BCHRS) using an optimized CoxBoost plus stepwise Cox model. BCHRS consistently stratified patient survival across TCGA-BLCA and two independent validation cohorts and provided prognostic information beyond conventional clinicopathological variables. High BCHRS scores were associated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition, extracellular matrix remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, and an immunosuppressive immune microenvironment. Spatial transcriptomics further prioritized TPST1 as a tumor-localized hypoxia-associated effector. Functional experiments confirmed that TPST1 promoted bladder cancer cell proliferation, migration, invasion, EMT-related changes, xenograft tumor growth, and experimental lung colonization. These findings define BCHRS as a hypoxia-related prognostic framework and identify TPST1 as a functional effector of aggressive bladder cancer progression.

papers.abstract_full: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into veterinary diagnostic imaging, yet robust regulatory oversight, validation standards, and governance frameworks remain limited. This review examines the current landscape of veterinary radiology AI, emphasizing differences between AI-generated outputs and comprehensive radiologist interpretations. It highlights key sources of algorithmic and human cognitive bias, explains AI development and validation processes, and outlines common pitfalls in interpreting performance metrics. The article stresses that veterinarians retain responsibility for clinical decisions and should critically evaluate AI tools for transparency, intended use, validation, and clinical utility. Responsible implementation requires human oversight, documentation, education, and ongoing monitoring.

METHODS: Synovial biopsies from etanercept-treated patients with RA in the Stratification of Biologic Therapies for Rheumatoid Arthritis by Pathobiology (STRAP) randomised controlled trial (RCT) underwent baseline genome-wide DN…
papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess how effectively baseline synovial DNA methylation and transcriptomic data capture inflammatory states relevant to tumour necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) response in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and to compare their predictive utility. METHODS: Synovial biopsies from etanercept-treated patients with RA in the Stratification of Biologic Therapies for Rheumatoid Arthritis by Pathobiology (STRAP) randomised controlled trial (RCT) underwent baseline genome-wide DNA methylation profiling (n = 54) and RNA sequencing (n = 67), with paired 16-week samples analysed in a subset (methylation: n = 14; RNA sequencing: n = 20). Differential methylation and transcriptomics were assessed by histological pathotype and response. Hierarchical clustering identified molecular subgroups, longitudinal analyses examined post-treatment changes by response, and baseline data were used to train machine-learning models using a nested cross-validation framework. RESULTS: Baseline synovial DNA methylation captures regulatory states reflecting tumour necrosis factor α (TNF-α)-driven inflammation across pathotypes and in subsequent responders. Forty-four significant response-associated differentially methylated regions were identified. Promoter hypomethylation of genes relevant to TNF-α signalling (IL32, ARID5B, and PRKCZ) was found in responders. Hierarchical clustering of DNA methylation and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) independently identified responder-enriched subgroups. TNFi treatment induced coordinated promoter hypermethylation of key TNF-α and interleukin-6 pathway genes in responders, whereas RNA-seq longitudinal changes reflected inflammatory resolution. A DNA methylation-only machine-learning model showed the highest performance for predicting TNFi response (median area under the curve (AUC) 0.83) compared to transcriptomic and multiomic models, with prediction driven by a compact 25-probe panel including probes at RA-relevant loci. CONCLUSIONS: Synovial DNA methylation captures stable baseline regulatory states reflecting TNF-α-driven inflammation that predispose to TNFi response and shows superior predictive performance compared with transcriptomics, supporting its utility for TNFi stratification.

papers.abstract_full: Background:  Patients' difficulties with illness and care (not understanding a result, distress, daily restrictions, not knowing where to go, family strain) may not surface in clinical encounters or records. Regulatory guidance on patient-focused drug development recognizes social-media listening as a source of patient experience data, but no systematic framework exists for Traditional Chinese discussions in Taiwan, and keyword pipelines measure such content poorly. Objective: To characterize patient-expressed needs, burdens and barriers ("frictions") in Taiwanese online health discussions with an eight-domain, Taiwan-contextualized framework, identify whose frictions they are, and assess how securely each is measured. Methods: From a 13.6-million-unit archive of the PTT forum and three ask-a-physician services, seeded samples of 9,131 pipeline-flagged units and 1,000 unflagged forum articles (10,130 distinct units) were read in full by a large language model under rubrics for relevance, author (patient or family member) and eight domains: information gap, emotional burden, lifestyle burden, medication experience, system navigation, access barrier, caregiver burden and cost burden. Profiles were reported separately for forum articles and physician submissions and checked against a second vendor, two physicians' independent labels of 160 accepted and rejected units, and the archive's keyword pipeline. Results: Among 2,395 model-confirmed forum articles, 83.1% voiced at least one friction: information gap 59.5% (physicians 86%-93%), emotional burden 39.0%, medication experience 24.1%, lifestyle burden 22.2% and system navigation 16.3%; access barrier, caregiver burden and cost burden were each below 7%. Of 3,105 submissions, nearly all were questions and 53.8% also carried a burden. Navigation rarely concerned insurance (9.1%). Family-authored forum articles (14.5%) more often voiced emotional burden (54.9% vs 36.3%), navigation (34.8% vs 13.2%; instrument-dependent) and access barriers (16.4% vs 4.7%), and patient-authored articles lifestyle burden (24.8% vs 6.9%); caregiver burden came with emotional burden in 86.0% of articles voicing it. Emotional and lifestyle burden were commoner in forum articles than submissions under the model, a second vendor and both physicians; medication experience and navigation were instrument-dependent, and physicians disagreed on cost (32% vs 4%). papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Ground-level ozone (O3) in tropical urban airsheds exhibits non-linear dependencies on volatile organic compound (VOC) and nitrogen oxide (NOx) precursors. We establish a parametric distributional fitting and machine-learning generalization framework across a 13-station continuous regulatory monitoring network (26 station-years; 16.1 million raw readings) during 2024-2025. Maximum likelihood estimation across 182 spatiotemporal series (seven monitored pollutant variables x 13 stations x two annual cycles) identifies the Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) and log-logistic distributions as optimal models for heavy-tailed ozone exceedances (minimum Akaike and Bayesian Information Criteria across 78.6% of station-years), whereas traditional Gaussian and lognormal approximations underestimate statutory threshold breach probabilities. The 13 stations exhibit severe nitrogen dioxide titration and secondary photochemical transformation gradients, dividing the conurbation into urban-industrial NOx-saturated regimes (VOC-limited) in western Howrah and photochemical accumulation hotspots across eastern Kolkata. Random Forest models trained under rigorous spatial block holdout cross-validation eliminate feature leakage between adjacent microenvironments (test R2 = 0.81-0.89 across stations). Spatial feature importance identifies atmospheric boundary layer height, ambient temperature, and non-methane hydrocarbons as primary non-linear drivers of diurnal ozone production. The parametric tail parameters and spatial machine-learning models provide regulatory authorities with an interpretable, transferable decision framework for photochemical risk mitigation, air pollution forecasting, and precursor reduction policy across dynamic tropical megacity airsheds.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Global pesticide use exceeded 3.7 million tonnes in 2023, and residues that persist beyond the treated field drive diffuse soil, surface water, and groundwater contamination linked to ecological harm and an estimated 150,000 pesticide poisoning deaths annually. Because field monitoring of pesticide fate across every soil, climate, and hydrological setting is logistically and financially infeasible at regulatory scale, predictive modelling has become the primary tool for estimating environmental concentrations and associated risk. This review traces the development of the field from traditional process-based mechanisms to hybrid AI frameworks by synthesizing 81 peer-reviewed and technical sources from an initial pool of 1,450 records screened across Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect (2005–2026). We look at the physicochemical and degradation principles that determine the fate of pesticides; the deterministic, mechanistic, process-based, empirical, and statistical models that support the current regulatory risk assessment; the hydrological and transport models that function at the soil profile to watershed scale; and the expanding array of machine learning, deep learning, fuzzy logic, GIS, remote sensing, and IoT-enabled techniques that are transforming precision agriculture and prediction. Case studies from India and other countries demonstrate real-world uses in addition to ongoing limitations in data accessibility and cross-context transferability. We point out important gaps, such as persistent data scarcity in low- and middle-income regions, limited coupling of fate models to downscaled climate projections, and inadequate integration of explainable AI to foster regulatory trust. We identify calibration and validation, particularly probabilistic uncertainty quantification, as essential to the responsible use of both conventional and data-driven models. We conclude that creating accurate, transferable pesticide prediction systems that support the Sustainable Development Goals and safeguard human and environmental health requires combining mechanistic understanding with hybrid, physics-informed AI and climate-resilient precision agriculture technologies.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Background  Protein dephosphorylation is a reversible post-translational event that influences signaling networks, cellular fate, and adaptation to therapy. However, whether dephosphorylation-related genes (DRGs) have prognostic utility in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains unclear. Methods  The Cancer Genome Atlas colon adenocarcinoma (TCGA-COAD) and TCGA-rectum adenocarcinoma (READ) were combined as the training cohort, and GSE17537 as the validation cohort. Prognostic DRGs were screened by differential-expression analysis and univariate Cox regression, followed by proportional-hazards assessment and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. A risk model was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Further analyses comprised gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), immune infiltration analysis, tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion (TIDE) scoring, reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), and drug-sensitivity prediction. Results  SNAI1, TCF7L1, and TIMP1 formed the prognostic signature, and survival differed significantly between high- and low-risk patients. The training cohort yielded 1-, 2-, and 3-year areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.604, 0.626, and 0.658, and validation-cohort values of 0.687, 0.764, and 0.652. In high-risk tumors, extracellular-matrix and cell-adhesion programs were preferentially enriched, alongside broad immune-infiltration differences. The low-risk group showed greater predicted immunotherapy response potential and distinct drug sensitivity. Experimental validation confirmed higher SNAI1 expression in tumor tissues and higher TCF7L1 expression in adjacent non-tumor tissues, whereas TIMP1 did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusion  This three-gene dephosphorylation-related signature stratified colorectal cancer prognosis and linked dephosphorylation signaling to extracellular-matrix remodeling, immune features, and treatment sensitivity; further validation is warranted

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Megacities represent a paradigmatic nexus of anthropogenic density and resource accretion, wherein the proliferation of PM₂.₅ aerosols, characterized by their polymorphic chemical speciation, exerts multifactorial pathophysiological burdens on urban cohorts. Prevailing regulatory frameworks, which homogenize monitoring and management protocols across urban hierarchies, fail to accommodate the spatiotemporal heterogeneities inherent to hypermetropolises, where the confluence of stationary point sources and high‑flux mobile emitters generates non‑Gaussian dispersion fields. To redress this lacuna, we introduce a hybrid CNN-Transformer ensemble engineered to concurrently resolve high‑frequency, localized emission pulses via hierarchical convolutional filters and protracted autocorrelative regimes through multi‑head self‑attention layers. Leveraging a sextennial dataset of meteorological covariates and station‑based PM₂.₅ readings across thirteen delineated districts of the Tehran megacity, our model extends predictive horizons to 72 hours, quadrupling the temporal ambit of antecedent sub‑6‑hour studies, while preserving sub‑3 µg/m³ error magnitudes. The network attained an R² exceeding 0.95, an RMSE of 3.372 µg/m³, and an MSE of 11.37 µg/m³, marking the most stringent performance metrics reported to date in urban air‑quality prognostication. Spatioclustering analyses revealed discordance between administrative zoning and aerosol concentration gradients, underscoring the necessity for delineating LEZs within megacities to enable targeted mitigation. Moreover, the model’s granular outputs facilitate the construction of dynamic public‑health protection maps, enabling preemptive exposure abatement for vulnerable demographics, particularly pediatric cohorts, and the temporal‑spatial identification of low‑pollution refugia. these findings advance the methodological frontier of precision air quality management and furnish a robust decision‑support scaffold for the formulation of bespoke regulatory standards tailored to the idiosyncratic pollutant topographies of megacities.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    As malaria transmission declines, determining where an infection was acquired becomes central to elimination, yet human mobility moves parasites between communities and makes their genetic profiles more similar. We asked whether genome-wide variation could assign  Plasmodium vivax  infections to one of two neighboring communities with residual transmission in the Peruvian Amazon, and how far this depended on sample composition. We analyzed 47 infections, 12 of them from people reporting recent local travel, using a machine-learning classifier (penalized logistic regression) with repeated nested cross-validation. Discrimination was modest (area under the curve 0.625, 95% interval 0.522–0.724) and close to chance once travelers were excluded (0.529, 0.402–0.657), although the two analyses used different, overlapping sets of infections. The most informative variants also differed, mapping to  msp7  -like genes and a putative multidrug resistance protein when travelers were included, and to merozoite surface protein 3 when they were not. Fine-scale genomic assignment in connected endemic communities is therefore limited, and sensitive to sample composition.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Much of the world's reinforced concrete (RC) building stock predates modern seismic codes, so engineers must decide which frames to brace, and with what, across inventories too large for case-by-case nonlinear analysis. Machine learning promises that speed, but current models learn retrofit decisions from data correlations alone. They can therefore recommend an intervention whose implied drift violates the very code limit that justifies retrofitting, they degrade without warning outside their training range, and they report one class label with no measure of confidence. None of these behaviours survives regulatory review, which is why such advice has not entered practice. We address this gap with a physics-informed machine learning framework that treats mechanics as a training constraint rather than a post-hoc check. We build a composite loss from four terms: data misfit, a response-spectrum drift residual that enforces equilibrium, a hinge penalty on the code drift limit, and a Monte Carlo variance term that stabilises the predicted probabilities. We train the model on 800 physics-consistent synthetic RC frames spanning four seismic zones, three soil classes and two irregularity indices. The model reaches 88 to 92% accuracy and a macro F1 of 0.86 to 0.90. Conventional models score marginally higher in distribution yet violate monotonic drift scaling under extrapolation, while our model cuts the mechanics residual by about 70%. Propagating the predicted post-retrofit drifts into lognormal fragility functions lowers cumulative collapse vulnerability by about 62%. We conclude that physical consistency, not accuracy, is the binding requirement for deployable retrofit models.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Petrophysical rock typing (PRT) is the cornerstone of reservoir characterization, bridging microscopic pore-throat morphology and macroscopic dynamic flow behavior to control hydrocarbon-in-place estimates, saturation–height functions, and numerical simulation grid-block properties. For over five decades, reservoir workflows have relied on conventional frameworks rooted in capillary pressure curves (Leverett, 1941; Thomeer, 1960), pore-throat size calibrations (Winland R₃₅; Pittman, 1992), and the modified Kozeny-Carman formulation, most notably the Reservoir Quality Index (RQI) and Flow Zone Indicator (FZI) proposed by Amaefule et al. (1993). However, these classical formulations frequently struggle in complex carbonate systems, tight gas sandstones, and multi-modal reservoirs due to fundamental physical limitations, including the conflation of static capillary storage with dynamic flow capacity, non-Darcy flow regimes, and unresolved multi-scale heterogeneity. This review systematically traces the methodological evolution of rock typing from its historical foundations to the contemporary ascent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). We first evaluate advanced conventional advancements that address classical shortcomings, including the rigorous decoupling of Petrophysical Static Rock Types (PSRT) from Petrophysical Dynamic Rock Types (PDRT), the calibration of effective flow porosity (PHIZ) via Purcell-PSKT porosimetry, and fractal bound-water models for low-permeability rocks. We then conduct an in-depth critical analysis of data-driven AI, examining how unsupervised clustering (Self-Organizing Maps, K-Means, Fuzzy C-Means, DBSCAN) automates electrofacies discovery from multi-well wireline logs, and how supervised tree-based ensembles (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM) and deep architectures predict rock classes and continuous permeability. Crucially, we highlight the paradigm shift toward Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML), where non-Darcy flow physics and mass conservation are embedded directly into loss functions, and Explainable AI (SHAP, LIME) is leveraged to eliminate black-box opacity. We further analyze the revolution in Digital Rock Physics (DRP) and Image-based Microscale Rock Typing (IMRT), which combines micro-CT, FIB-SEM, and deep learning segmentation (PRRT and TSRT) with Lattice Boltzmann flow simulation to provide verifiable ground truth. Finally, we replace speculative risks with an industry-grounded audit of genuine operational pitfalls in AI petrophysics — including spatial autocorrelation data leakage, out-of-distribution extrapolation failure, core-to-log depth-matching errors, and regulatory compliance — and synthesize these insights into a unified, multi-scale, physics-informed digital rock typing roadmap for resilient reservoir modeling.

papers.abstract_full: Background:  The development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has dramatically advanced the capabilities of Natural Language Processing (NLP), enabling breakthroughs in text understanding, generation, and reasoning. However, the success of these models hinges on access to massive, diverse, and high-quality labeled datasets. In many real-world scenarios, such as specialized domains (e.g., healthcare, law), low-resource languages, and privacy-sensitive applications, curating such data remains prohibitively expensive, time-consuming, or infeasible due to regulatory or ethical constraints. Moreover, as LLMs continue to scale in size and complexity, the demand for training and evaluation data grows disproportionately, exacerbating annotation bottlenecks and domain coverage gaps. Synthetic Data Generation (SDG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm to address these challenges by programmatically producing task-specific or domain-adapted examples that complement or replace manually labeled data. Initially grounded in statistical modeling and deep generative architectures, SDG has evolved into a central strategy for improving data efficiency, mitigating distributional shifts, and enabling scalable supervision in modern NLP pipelines, especially in conjunction with LLM-driven prompt-based learning and self-supervised generation. Objectives: This survey provides a comprehensive overview of SDG techniques up to November 2026, with a particular focus on LLM-oriented pipelines. We categorize generative approaches for synthetic text, identify trends in controllability, verification and automation, and highlight open challenges in evaluation, fairness, privacy and scalability. Methods: We review the model families used to generate synthetic text, including probabilistic models, autoencoders and variational autoencoders, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), transformers, diffusion language models and mixtures of experts, as background for LLM-based pipelines such as instruction synthesis, Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), prompt evolution, feedback loops and multi-agent generation, together with toolkits such as PromptSource [1], Self-Instruct [2] and LM-Debugger [3]. The original literature was collected informally; we extended it with a documented search run on 14 November 2026 (49 queries, 78 candidate records, 47 works added) covering 2025–2026 work on reasoning traces and verifiable rewards, model collapse and data quality, agentic and multi-agent pipelines, and evaluation, privacy and multilingual generation. The scope is text and language data, with other data types only where an LLM generates or directs their generation, and every reference was checked against arXiv, Crossref or the publisher. Results: Our synthesis traces an evolution from static, single-model pipelines to modular, verifier-centred and agentic systems in which LLMs plan, generate, critique and check data. Since 2025, synthetic data has become central to teaching models to reason: verifiable rewards move the bottleneck from preference labels to problems with checkable answers, which procedural generators, rephrased web text and self-play now supply. Studies of model collapse show that accumulating real and synthetic data avoids collapse while replacing real data does not, but also that even small synthetic fractions and recursive training can degrade models and their fairness. Synthetic text can leak membership information about its source data, and differentially private generation methods are narrowing the utility gap. Evaluation practice remains fragmented, and multilingual generation increasingly relies on culturally grounded rather than translated data. Conclusions: LLM-driven SDG is rapidly transforming data creation, making it more scalable, controllable and adaptive, but its reliability now depends on verification, provenance and privacy safeguards. This survey offers a taxonomy and a roadmap for building trustworthy synthetic data systems, and it motivates future work on verifiers beyond checkable domains, standardized evaluation of data generators, collapse-aware data practice and formal privacy guarantees.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Generative artificial intelligence complicates the relationship between news credibility and demands for regulation. Caution about substantially AI-generated news need not imply rejection of editorially supervised assistance, while support for accountability need not imply support for unrestricted content controls. This study examines these distinctions in 385 adult, AI-aware questionnaire records supplied as empirical data from Bangladesh. It analyses five separate statements concerning caution, labelling, accuracy accountability, oversight-related trust and proportionate regulation, with supporting awareness and verification items. Low five-item block reliabilities preclude treating the questionnaire as a validated latent-variable model. Analyses combine response distributions, paired contrasts, joint endorsement patterns, rank correlations and exploratory adjusted logistic regression. Accuracy accountability received 84.2% endorsement and oversight-related trust 83.1%, compared with 69.4% for caution, 68.8% for appropriate labelling and 66.8% for proportionate rules respecting lawful expression. Caution and oversight-related trust were jointly endorsed by 57.7%. Accountability exceeded rules endorsement by 17.4 percentage points, while similar aggregate labelling and rules percentages concealed differing responses in 170 records. No selected correlation or focal binary-model coefficient met the 5% threshold after Holm adjustment. The oversight coefficient was positive but sensitive to response coding and sample restriction. The findings distinguish epistemic caution, editorial responsibility and conditional regulatory support rather than demonstrating a causal trust-to-regulation pathway. They support evaluating particular disclosures and oversight procedures against both informational outcomes and expressive rights. Mixed respondent status, undocumented recruitment and fieldwork dates, single-item measurement and unresolved source-documentation labels constrain generalisation. The contribution is an item-specific account of news governance preferences that does not equate favourable survey responses with verified competence or a mandate for coercive regulation.

papers.abstract_full: Enhancers encode tissue-specific gene expression through the combinatorial identity, number, and arrangement of transcription factor motifs, collectively known as regulatory grammar. However, existing deep-learning methods directly optimize nucleotide sequences, leaving enhancer regulatory grammar implicit. Here we introduce REgulatory Grammar Architecture via reinforcement Learning (REGAL), a framework that explicitly programs enhancer grammar under sequence-to-function oracles. REGAL generated tissue-specific enhancers across species using the same placement architecture with interchangeable oracles and motif vocabularies. Experimental validation and perturbation revealed that tissue specificity requires coordinated target-tissue activation and off-target repression, depends on both motif composition and spatial organization, and employs distinct regulatory strategies across tissues. REGAL-designed enhancers drove predicted lineage-specific expression in transgenic mouse embryos, outperformed a nucleotide-level optimizer in human cells, and matched or exceeded leading designs in zebrafish and  Drosophila at notably shorter length. Together, these findings establish regulatory grammar as a programmable and experimentally testable substrate underlying enhancer design and specificity.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) exhibits substantial molecular and immune heterogeneity, yet the role of integrated cell death- and senescence-associated (CDS) programs remains incompletely understood. We characterized 21 CDS transcriptional signatures using multicohort transcriptomic, clinical, pharmacogenomic, and single-cell data. Consensus clustering of 538 TCGA-KIRC tumors identified three subtypes characterized by metabolic–proliferative, immune–inflammatory, and hypoxia–angiogenesis-associated profiles. The immune-enriched C2 subtype showed the poorest survival with elevated exhausted and regulatory T-cell signatures. Focusing on C2, edge perturbation analysis identified 246 network-associated genes, which were narrowed to 23 CDS-related candidates and 12 survival-associated genes. Among 101 machine-learning combinations, CoxBoost followed by random survival forest achieved the best performance, generating a ten-gene prognostic signature with a mean C-index of 0.733 across five cohorts. The resulting risk score was associated with survival outcomes and adverse clinicopathological characteristics. Among the ten genes, LMNB1, LY96, and HSPA8 were further investigated based on their differential expression and high tumor–normal discrimination AUCs. Single-cell profiling and virtual knockout analyses linked LMNB1 to T-cell cytotoxicity-associated networks, LY96 to macrophage antigen-presentation programs, and HSPA8 to T-cell cytokine signaling. Pharmacogenomic analysis identified nine compounds with differential predicted drug responses in C2. Across three independent treatment cohorts, C2 consistently exhibited the lowest response rates. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that integrated CDS transcriptional profiling delineates prognostically distinct molecular states in ccRCC, revealing an immune-enriched yet unfavorable subtype and identifying candidate genes that link cellular stress-associated programs to tumor immune heterogeneity.

papers.abstract_full: Objective  Biopsies are examined under the microscope by a pathologist, giving a diagnosis, which guides treatment and predicts prognosis. A shortage of pathologists and increasing workload leads to diagnostic delays, while for duodenal (small intestinal) biopsies, variable diagnostic concordance between pathologists limits accuracy. These challenges have motivated us to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated approach for the automated diagnosis of up to 80% of duodenal biopsies (i.e., most cases of the two most frequent diagnoses: coeliac disease and “normal”). We set out to understand patient, carer and stakeholder views regarding the adoption of such technology. Methods and Analysis  We conducted mixed-methods stakeholder engagement (February 2024 to June 2026). We ran a national online patients’ and carers’ questionnaire (n=231 respondents) and four UK focus-group workshops, one of which additionally captured Likert-scale attitudes  1 immediately before and after a structured educational session (n=34 matched pairs). Healthcare professionals completed an online questionnaire (n=37) and took part in a structured workshop. Quantitative data were summarised descriptively; free-text and workshop data were analysed thematically and triangulated across all sources.  Results  Most patients and carers supported AI-reliant diagnosis (68.4%) and would strongly trust systems with formal regulatory approval (66.7%). Most wanted to be informed if AI was used (73.6%), but only 52.4% felt explicit permission was necessary. Qualitative themes centred on clear and available evidence of accuracy, human oversight, transparent communication and clear terminology, with the term ‘machine learning’ being preferred to ‘artificial intelligence’. Agreement (‘agree’ or ‘strongly agree’ combined) with statements relating to trust, acceptance and perceived benefit of AI was significantly higher after a structured educational session (38.2% to 67.6%, 85.3% to 97.1%, and 52.9% to 97.1% respectively; all p≤0.003). Healthcare professionals favoured an AI ‘assistant’ model over full automation, citing the need for validation, explainability, data governance and workflow integration. Patients also preferred some level of human oversight. Conclusion  Patients and healthcare professionals are cautiously supportive of AI-assisted diagnosis of duodenal biopsies, conditional upon demonstration of accuracy, appropriate human oversight and transparent communication. Attitudes towards AI-assisted diagnosis were more favourable after structured explanation. Key Messages  What is already known on this topic  Very little is known about patients’, carers’ or healthcare professionals’ views about the automation of diagnosis in pathology, using AI-based software solutions. What this study adds  ⇒ This is the first study to investigate patient, carer and healthcare professional attitudes specifically to AI-mediated duodenal biopsy diagnosis. Around two-thirds of respondents supported AI-assisted diagnosis, contingent upon clear and available evidence of accuracy, appropriate human oversight and transparent communication, together with appropriate regulatory approval of the technology. ⇒ Attitudes were markedly more favourable after a single structured educational session: agreement that AI could improve duodenal biopsy diagnosis nearly doubled and trust in healthcare AI rose substantially, suggesting that public views of AI in diagnosis can be influenced by clear explanation. ⇒ Patients and healthcare professionals both favour some ongoing level of human oversight of any AI-based diagnostic approach. How this study might affect research, practice or policy  ⇒ Our study suggests that a phased, AI-assistant-first deployment model with defined validation and audit checkpoints would be most readily acceptable when introducing diagnostic AI into histopathology. ⇒ It indicates that appropriate information and education, for example, a patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) session, can increase trust in AI in healthcare. ⇒ It shows that patients and the public are more trusting of technology for which the term machine learning is used, rather than artificial intelligence (AI). ⇒ It offers a stakeholder-engagement template for use by others introducing AI-based diagnostics.

papers.abstract_full: ABSTRACT  Accurate genetic characterization is central to modern acute myeloid leukemia (AML) diagnostics, yet current standard-of-care (SoC) testing relies on multiple complementary assays. We compared paired tumor–normal whole-genome sequencing (WGS) with SoC diagnostics in a population-based cohort of 109 adult AML patients, assessing variant detection, disease classification according to ICC 2022 and WHO 2022, and risk stratification according to ELN 2022. WGS showed high concordance with SoC across variant classes. When considering all reported SoC variants together with high-confidence WGS variants as true positives, WGS showed equal to higher sensitivity than SoC for single-nucleotide variants and small insertions/deletions (97% vs 92%), structural variants (SVs; 100% vs 87%), and copy-number alterations (CNAs; 88.5% both). WGS identified clinically important lesions missed by SoC in 16 cases (15%), including  FLT3 -ITDs and  KMT2A ,  NUP98 and  MECOM rearrangements. Classification and risk assignments were 95–96% concordant, with WGS-driven reclassifications in 4-5% of cases, primarily through detection of cryptic SVs and myelodysplasia-related lesions. Integrated analysis of genomic alterations, including copy-neutral loss-of-heterozygosity, refined  TP53 allelic state assessment and demonstrated increased genomic complexity in AML with biallelic  TP53 alterations. We developed a supervised machine-learning model for complex karyotype (CK) probability, based on WGS-derived copy-number and SV burden, enabling automated identification of CK cases from WGS data. Collectively, these results support paired tumor– normal WGS as a single comprehensive assay well suited for AML diagnostics according to current classification and risk-stratification systems, while refining assessment of  TP53 allelic state and karyotypic complexity.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Some environmental regulators now trigger restrictions on forecasts before exceedances occur, while machine-learning methods are proposed for the forecasting pipelines behind them. Delhi-NCR’s Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) directs advance invocation on numerical air-quality forecasts, yet reported practice often followed observed readings. Judicial and regulatory directions demand anticipatory action, yet none reviewed here specifies the confidence a forecast must carry before it justifies coercion. This article asks what validation, reproducibility and uncertainty-quantification thresholds an AI-enabled forecast must meet before triggering binding restrictions. Using a functional comparative method, it separates physics-based forecasts and digital dissemination from the machine-learning layer that makes a pipeline AI-enabled. GRAP, with the Supreme Court’s timing orders, is the single test case. Instruments from India, China, France and California’s air districts are coded for observed, forecast-based and discretionary triggers and read alongside forecast-verification studies. This article argues that proportionality and reasoned decision-making require restrictions to reflect forecast confidence as well as predicted severity, and that precaution licenses early action only if uncertainty is disclosed. One implication is that legal reliance on an AI-enabled forecast should depend on a disclosed validation dossier, because machine-learning layers add opacity and drift. Disclosure supports human oversight and lets affected people contest restrictions built on overconfident models. The contribution is a test mapping calibrated confidence onto the intensity of proportionality review. The assessment is prospective and doctrinal, evaluating design adequacy rather than operational performance; conclusions remain contingent.

papers.abstract_full: The DNA/RNA binding protein TARDBP or TDP-43 is a key driver of pathology in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), a motor neuron disease with no known cure. In >97% of sporadic ALS patients, nuclear TDP-43 in motor neurons mislocalizes and aggregates in the cellular cytoplasm (gain-of-function). A parallel reduction in nuclear TDP-43 in ALS patients leads to a loss-of-function in mRNA binding and splicing regulation. Using our machine learning platform, we discovered ACE-339, a novel, orally bioavailable small molecule that disrupts insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Using  in vitro ,  in vivo and  in silico models, we show that ACE-339 directly targets aggregated forms of TDP-43. ACE-339 interacts directly with TDP-43 hexamers, disaggregates recombinant TDP-43 and rescues both gain- and loss-of-function phenotypes of TDP-43 in cells. ACE-339 functionally rescues TDP-43 dependent mis-splicing and synaptic activity. Lastly, ACE-339 rescues disease associated phenotypes in two independent mouse models of TDP-43 pathology. In addition, we now have a catalog of TDP-43 disaggregating compounds that are being developed further to be tested in clinical trials in patients with ALS and other TDP-43 proteinopathies.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background.  Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital transformation are promoted as ways to close gaps in Latin American health systems, but the obstacles to routine clinical use are scattered across a multilingual literature.  Objective.  To map evidence on barriers to implementing AI, and the digital infrastructure it depends on, in Latin American healthcare, 2016 to 2026.  Methods.  Joanna Briggs Institute methodology, PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews reporting, Open Science Framework registration. Five databases were searched in English, Spanish and Portuguese, with duplicate screening. Sources were charted under a manual frozen before charting: verified against the full text by one reviewer, reviewed by a second. Barriers traceable to data the source collected were counted as empirically studied.  Results.  Of 2,742 records, 43 sources were included, contributing 1,031 barrier instances concentrated in Brazil, Peru, and Colombia. Sixteen of the 43 sources measured none of the barriers they reported; all 13 primary empirical studies measured something, 11 of the 12 narrative reviews nothing. At instance level 328 (31.8%) were empirically studied, 703 (68.2%) asserted without supporting data. Instances clustered at the health-system (374) and regulatory/political (217) levels, dominated by infrastructural (140) and regulatory (165) barriers. The pattern held among the 813 AI-specific instances (63.3% asserted) and strengthened among the 16 exclusively Latin American sources (76.8%).  Conclusions.  The regional evidence describes implementation barriers far more often than it measures them: more than a third of the included sources measured none of what they reported. Prospective implementation studies, not further assertion, will close the gap.
