papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) may facilitate detection of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), but its ability to identify higher-risk patients undergoing clinical evaluation for HCM remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic performance of a commercially available AI-ECG algorithm among patients undergoing cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) for suspected or established HCM. METHODS: We studied 102 patients with HCM and 302 age-, sex-, and year-matched controls without HCM who underwent clinically indicated CMR. An AI-ECG algorithm was applied to the first available ECG preceding CMR. Diagnostic performance, incremental value beyond standard ECG features, and associations with clinical outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: ECGs preceded CMR by a median of 1.1 years. AI-ECG demonstrated moderate sensitivity (51.1%) and high specificity (96.1%) for identification of phenotypic HCM and incrementally improved discrimination and reclassification beyond demographic and conventional ECG variables (net reclassification improvement 0.19, p<0.001). Within one year of CMR, a positive AI-ECG was independently associated with the composite outcome (adjusted HR 2.68, 95% CI 1.42-5.09; p=0.003), driven by ICD placement and septal reduction therapy. Among patients with HCM, while exploratory, an AI-ECG probability ≥ 0.99 identified those at highest risk for subsequent events (HR 2.92, 95% CI 1.59-5.35; p=0.011). CONCLUSION: In conclusion, among patients undergoing clinical evaluation for HCM, AI-ECG provided incremental diagnostic value beyond conventional ECG parameters and identified individuals at increased risk for subsequent treatment-related clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract_full: Fungi encode diverse carbohydrate-processing functions, yet the genomic basis of their lignocellulose-degradation potential and its relevance to the human gut remain poorly understood. Here, we experimentally assessed cellulase-, xylanase-, and laccase-associated activities across 762 environmentally derived fungal isolates and sequenced 170 representative strains, retaining 160 genomes for genome-phenotype analyses. By integrating functional annotations with orthogroup presence-absence variation and machine-learning models, we identified lignocellulose-degradation-associated genomic features that improved phenotype prediction beyond conventional annotation alone. We then applied this framework to 2,116 publicly available fungal genomes and 704 cultivated gut fungal genomes from a previously published collection to construct a non-redundant catalogue of lignocellulose-degradation-associated genes (LDAGs), comprising canonical degradative enzymes, annotated phenotype-associated features, and candidate orthogroups. Across fungal lineages, xylanase-associated potential was broadly distributed, cellulase-associated potential showed an intermediate pattern, whereas laccase-associated oxidative potential was concentrated in a more restricted subset of taxa. Analysis of approximately 1,500 publicly available human gut metagenomes identified disease-associated differences in LDAG profiles in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ACVD), inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and obesity. papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Out-of-hospital cardiac (OHCA) arrest is a frequent emergency, and few patients will survive with good neurological outcome. Identification of patients with a low likelihood of meaningful recovery represents a major clinical challenge. Numerous scores have been developed to guide decision-making after OHCA, with variable goals and targets, but most of them have been validated on small cohorts, integrates variables not available in the prehospital field, or do have low prediction values. MIRA-29 score aimed to only rely on simple clinical variables, available in the prehospital setting. We hypothetized that such score will provide incremental neurological prognosis value at an early-stage following OHCA. METHODS: MIRA-29 score was derived and internally validated over a five-year period on a prospective cohort of 1099 adult patients, including all OHCA treated by our territory dispatch center. Multivariate analysis identified independent variables within the database, that were used to optimize the prediction model using machine-learning and genetic algorithms. The score was subsequently validated externally on 82 696 patients extracted from the French national cardiac arrest registry (RéAC). RESULTS: Out from the 1099 patients, 85 patients (7.7%) had a favorable neurological outcome. Multivariate analysis identified five independent variables associated with neurological outcome: age, low-flow duration, number of external electric shock, epinephrine dose, and the OHCA site (street, public facility, home). After model optimization and machine-learning, age was not retained within the final model. External validation depicted a precision of 0.86 and a recall of 0.88 of the model. The F1-Score and accuracy are respectively 0.87 and 0.88, and specificity for a bad neurological prognosis is 0.99. CONCLUSION: MIRA‑29 strength lies on its ability to reliably identify patients with extremely high probability of poor neurological outcome, while being based on four simple clinical variables. The prospective validation of MIRA-29 in the clinical setting may evaluate its impact on clinical decision making.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the most common birth defect, with the genetic defects remaining unknown in many patients. NR2F2 is a transcription factor that regulates cardiac endocardial development in a dosage-sensitive manner; however, the association between non-coding NR2F2 variants and CHD risk remains unclear. In this study, we performed a case-control analysis of the NR2F2 promoter, and identified four rare variants in isolated CHD patients with a frequency over 3% but undetected in controls. Histone modification analysis showed that two of the candidate variants, g.96330105C > T and g.96330128C > T, overlapped with active promoter-associated histone marks. Functionally, these two variants significantly reduced NR2F2 promoter transcriptional activity and protein expression. In addition, the variant g.96330128C > T abrogated ETS1 binding, thereby impairing ETS1-mediated positive transcriptional regulation of NR2F2. These findings highlight that loss-of-function (LOF) variants in the NR2F2 promoter, particularly g.96330128C > T, confer CHD susceptibility by reducing NR2F2 expression.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Survival into adulthood is now the norm for individuals born with congenital heart disease, with over 90% of children reaching adult life. Yet for many, particularly those with complex lesions, childhood intervention does not equate to a cure. Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) face ongoing risks of haemodynamic complications, end-organ dysfunction, and premature morbidity. In this review, we present recent advances in ACHD care across five domains: lifelong care models, diagnostic techniques, management strategies, genetic and precision medicine, and machine learning. We highlight the pivotal role of specialized, multidisciplinary care in improving outcomes, and the need for structured transition programmes to ensure continuity from paediatric to adult services. Emerging priorities include reproductive counselling, exercise prescription, and psychosocial support. Advances in cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging, electrophysiological mapping, and four-dimensional flow imaging now offer unprecedented anatomical and haemodynamic insights. Recent trials have demonstrated encouraging results for novel heart failure therapies and pulmonary vasodilators in lesion-specific subgroups, while transcatheter technologies continue to expand therapeutic options for patients with complex anatomy. Genetic testing and machine learning are beginning to reshape risk stratification and workflow efficiency, though challenges remain in their implementation. As this population ages and acquires new comorbidities, care models must evolve to move beyond just survival, but towards improving quality of life, preserving organ function, and anticipating future needs. This review aims to support clinicians and researchers in meeting these challenges and advancing the next era of ACHD care.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmia (MVA) and end-stage heart failure (ESHF) in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) may vary by genotype. Comparative analyses remain limited. The aim of this study was to compare clinical outcomes and risk predictors across genotypes. METHODS AND RESULTS: Carriers of pathogenic variants in DCM-associated genes were identified from a dedicated database. Clinically affected variant-carriers from the five most prevalent genotypes were compared with genotype-negative patients. A composite primary endpoint consisted of MVA or ESHF. Secondary endpoints were MVA and ESHF individually. Incidence rates and baseline variables associated with outcomes were evaluated.Among 484 patients, 57 (11.8%) met the primary endpoint after 5 years. Genotype-negative patients had the lowest primary endpoint incidence rates [1.4 (0.7-2.1) per 100 person-years], whereas LMNA had the highest [6.2 (3.0-9.5)]. With a genotype-negative reference, incidence rate ratios were 1.3 for TTN, 1.7 for FLNC, 2.0 for DSP, 2.7 for RBM20 and 4.4 for LMNA. Rates were higher in LMNA and RBM20 than genotype-negative patients (P < .001 and P = .003, respectively) and higher in LMNA than TTN (P = .001). Results were similar for MVA. LMNA had higher ESHF rates than genotype-negative, TTN and DSP.Left ventricular diastolic diameter, LMNA variants and late gadolinium enhancement were independently associated with the primary endpoint. Baseline predictors varied by genotype. CONCLUSION: Genotype stratification in DCM reveals a risk hierarchy with risk lowest in genotype-negative and TTN patients, two-fold higher in DSP and FLNC, and three- and four-fold higher in RBM20 and LMNA, respectively. Accounting for genotype improves risk prediction.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Genomic studies in hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) are limited by sample sizes and targeted approaches. METHODS: The Genomic Studies in Blood and Marrow Transplantation (GS-BMT) project is a collaboration between the National Cancer Institute (NCI) and the CIBMTR® designed to investigate recipient and donor determinants of HCT outcomes. We are generating genome-wide SNP-array genotyping for all samples, and sequencing and methylation profiling for selected subsets. We report study design and cohort characteristics and present two proof-of-concept analyses: comparison of conventional and machine learning prediction of overall survival after HCT in 9,262 patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and assessment of inherited susceptibility to clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) among 19,750 HCT donors using polygenic scores (PGS). RESULTS: GS-BMT includes 30,718 donor-recipient pairs who received allogeneic HCT in the United States between 2000 and 2019. In AML, clinical variables alone provided modest prediction for post-transplant survival, with similar performance for Cox proportional hazards, random survival forest, and deep neural network survival models (C-index=0.63, 0.62, and 0.62, respectively). In donors, CHIP-PGS did not differ by age (p=0.76) but was modestly lower in unrelated vs . related donors (-0.06 standard deviation [SD]; p=0.002). In an illustrative analysis assuming risk of event increases by 50% or 80% per PGS-SD, the top 5.2% and 12.3% of the donors, respectively, would have at least twice the risk of a donor with the average PGS. CONCLUSIONS: GS-BMT establishes a large genomic platform aiming to improve individualized risk prediction, donor selection, and precision medicine in HCT.

selected_papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVES: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) arises from complex interactions between genetic and environmental factors, creating a need for approaches that integrate inherited susceptibility and cumulative environmental exposure. Previous models have focused on clinical or genetic data and provided limited mechanistic insight. This study developed a machine-learning model that integrated a polygenic risk score (PRS) and DNA methylation to classify prevalent T2DM and assessed their individual and combined contributions to classification performance. METHODS: Models were developed and validated using data from the Ansan/Ansung cohort (n = 1,318) and the independent Health Examinee cohort (n = 358). PRS was calculated using external genome-wide association study summary statistics, and DNA methylation features were represented by β-values at T2DM-related cytosine-phosphate-guanine sites. Three feature sets were compared: Base, Base + PRS, and Base + PRS + DNA methylation. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Decision curve analysis assessed clinical utility, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were used to interpret the models. RESULTS: Adding PRS and then DNA methylation features progressively increased AUROC across algorithms. The linear support vector machine with the fully integrated feature set achieved the highest discrimination (AUROC = 0.896, AUPRC = 0.801). PRS improved accuracy, and DNA methylation data produced further gains, particularly in recall and F1-score. Decision curve analysis showed that the integrated model provided greater net benefit across clinically relevant threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis identified PRS as the most influential individual feature and DNA methylation features as the largest contributors at the group level. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating PRS and DNA methylation improves the performance of machine-learning models for T2DM classification. Genetic and epigenetic factors thus provide complementary information for characterizing prevalent T2DM.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) hold promise for stratifying inherited disease risk, yet their clinical adoption remains constrained by poor transferability across populations and cohorts. To bridge this gap, we propose a pragmatic framework that recalibrates externally derived PRSs to local datasets through machine learning-based optimization. This post-PRS calibration approach integrates multiple published PRSs for a given disease and reweighs them based on predictive performance in the target cohort, generating composite locally optimized PRS that is fine-tuned to local disease risk. We test local optimization on three diseases currently under active clinical trials for PRS utility (coronary artery disease [CAD], breast cancer [BC], and prostate cancer [PC]). Local optimization achieves substantial C-statistic improvements across diseases in MGB Biobank, with C-statistics improving by an average of 19.8% for CAD, 9.4% for PC, and 8.3% for BC. The locally optimized CAD PRS identifies 27.7% of CAD cases compared with 17.8% by the top-performing published CAD PRS, and improvements in case enrichment are more pronounced for breast cancer (20.8% vs. 7.1%) and prostate cancer (16.4% vs. 8.8%). This low-complexity post hoc calibration approach enables scalable implementation of PRS across diverse health systems without new GWAS discovery or complex upstream algorithmic innovations. By treating PRS as adaptable rather than static, the locally optimized PRS framework provides a practical blueprint for clinical adoption of PRS in diverse local settings and helps mitigate disparities stemming from one-size-fits-all applications of externally derived PRS.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been instrumental in uncovering the genetic basis of complex traits, yet classical single-variant testing remains limited in power and biological interpretability. Over the past decade, GWAS methodology has expanded from purely statistical association frameworks toward integrative models that incorporate functional annotations, multi-trait information, and data-driven prioritization strategies. Early developments leveraged regulatory genomics and cross-phenotype statistics to improve locus discovery, while machine learning approaches enabled systematic ranking of sub-threshold variants. More recently, deep learning architectures, including Transformer-based frameworks, have been introduced to integrate GWAS summary signals with linkage disequilibrium patterns and diverse genomic annotations. In parallel, multi-omics integration and transfer learning across related traits have emerged as practical solutions for limited sample sizes and population heterogeneity. This chapter reviews the evolving methodological landscape of AI-enabled GWAS, highlights key advances in variant discovery and functional interpretation, and discusses remaining challenges such as ancestry bias, interpretability, and the need for biological validation. Together, these approaches provide a foundation for more context-aware and scalable genetic studies of complex disease.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) perform strongly on medical specialty board multiple-choice questions (MCQs) but underperform in complex medical reasoning. This gap indicates a need to improve LLM medical reasoning and evaluation paradigms. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and evaluate MedEvalArena, a dynamically regenerable benchmark for assessing medical reasoning in LLMs. METHODS: In a symmetric round-robin format, 6 frontier LLMs from the OpenAI, Grok, Gemini, Claude, Kimi, and DeepSeek families generated challenging board-style medical MCQs, adjudicated question validity on an ensemble LLM-as-judge panel, and answered the validated examination. Candidate items were generated until each model contributed 50 validated questions according to Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC)/American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS) physician specialty distributions, yielding a 300-question examination. Judges adjudicated candidate questions' logical validity and medical accuracy. We compared question-generation validity rates, assessed leave-one-out judge agreement, and tested for self-judging preference. Questions were audited for overlap with public MedQA (medical question-answering) benchmarks. We tested question-answering (QA) accuracy across LLMs using a binomial-logit generalized linear mixed model likelihood-ratio test. A generator-stratified 90-question subset was completed by 5 board-certified physicians for paired human-LLM analysis. We evaluated inference cost-accuracy tradeoffs. Multiple comparisons were adjusted by the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure. RESULTS: Judge-panel validity rates were significantly higher for questions generated by OpenAI (94.8%, Wilson 95% CI 85.9%-98.2%), Gemini (92.3%, 95% CI 83.2%-96.7%), and Claude (83.3%, 95% CI 72.6%-90.4%) models than those generated by Kimi (63.8%, 95% CI 54.3%-72.4%), Grok (56%, 95% CI 45.8%-65.8%), and DeepSeek (46.0%, 95% CI 37.4%-54.7%). Kimi also demonstrated significantly higher validity than DeepSeek (2-sample tests of proportions; BH-adjusted P=.01). The public-source similarity audit found no exact or near-duplicate matches. Leave-one-out judge agreement was moderate. Generator-specific same-family judging coefficients were nonnegative (0 to 11.0 percentage points); however, none remained significant after BH adjustment. There was no significant difference between the 6 frontier LLM QA accuracies, which ranged from 85.7% (257/300) to 91.7% (275/300), on the 300-question examination (generalized linear mixed model likelihood-ratio test P=.07). The study had 80% power to detect LLM accuracy differences of 9.2 percentage points; nonsignificance did not establish equivalence. On the 90-question subset, physician accuracy was 85.6% (95% CI 79.4%-91.7%; stratified normal with finite-population correction), compared with aggregate LLM performance of 94.4% (85/90; Wilson 95% CI 87.6%-97.6%). This difference was not significant (McNemar test, P=.08); however, the study was powered to detect a human vs LLM accuracy difference of 14% to 15%. selected_papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Background  Insomnia is consistently associated with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) in observational studies, but the causal relationship and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the causal relationship between insomnia and late-onset AD and to identify molecular pathways and candidate genes that may contribute to this association by integrating genetic causal inference with transcriptomics. Methods  Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) was performed using 28 single-nucleotide polymorphisms as instruments, with insomnia genome-wide association study summary statistics from UK Biobank (336,965 participants of European ancestry) and late-onset AD data from FinnGen (11,359 cases and 508,613 controls). Inverse-variance weighting was the primary method. Robustness was assessed using MR-Egger, weighted median, simple mode, and weighted mode estimates, together with pleiotropy, heterogeneity, and leave-one-out analyses. GEO datasets GSE122063 and GSE110226 were integrated for differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network, protein interaction, and functional enrichment analyses. Lasso regression and support vector machine recursive feature elimination were used to identify key candidate genes, whose discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves. Results  Inverse-variance weighting associated genetically predicted insomnia with higher odds of late-onset AD (OR = 3.36, 95% CI 1.02–10.99; P = 0.045). Other MR methods yielded directionally consistent but imprecise estimates. The MR-Egger intercept test found no evidence of directional pleiotropy (P = 0.939), and Cochran’s Q test was not statistically significant (P = 0.062). No individual instrument dominated the leave-one-out results. Transcriptomic analysis identified 1,616 differentially expressed genes and eight co-expression modules. MEpink, MEblack, and MEbrown showed the strongest associations with AD. Their intersection with 2,330 insomnia-related genes yielded 35 candidates, enriched mainly in neuroinflammation, cell adhesion, and lipid metabolism. Both machine learning algorithms selected seven key candidates. All seven were differentially expressed between AD and controls in the combined dataset, with individual AUCs above 0.75. Conclusion  Genetic liability to insomnia may be associated with an increased risk of late-onset AD. Neuroinflammation and lipid metabolism may link the two conditions, and seven candidate genes warrant further study. Given the borderline MR result, wide confidence interval, tissue heterogeneity, and absence of independent external validation, these findings require confirmation in larger multi-ancestry cohorts, independent transcriptomic datasets, and experimental studies.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Genome-wide association studies have catalogued tens of thousands of trait-associated loci, most of them in non-coding DNA, yet for most loci the path from nucleotide to phenotype remains correlational. We propose a layered computational decomposition of the genome as a complement to data-driven approaches: sequence as formal language, sequence as information-bearing signal, mobile elements as runtime, compilation to interaction networks through thermodynamic and rule-based models, and execution as cellular and multicellular dynamics. Each layer is defined by its inputs, outputs and formalisms, and we set out where the frame breaks down, including the looseness of algorithmic-information estimates, the triviality of universality results and the failure of string grammars at the chromatin level. Synthetic-biology platforms serve as tests of whether the layers compose, and genomic foundation models and the AlphaGenome Atlas, which predicts effects for all nine billion possible single-nucleotide variants, serve as oracles whose coverage and limits we map onto the framework. We state five falsifiable predictions and test the first, that sequence compressibility carries information about regulatory function beyond composition and conservation, on 38,556 single-nucleotide variants from a saturation-mutagenesis reporter assay of 21 regulatory elements. In a pooled model, local compressibility is associated with measured effect size (standardized β = −0.030, p = 0.0014). The association roughly halves under full control for base composition, loses significance when composition, motif and noise adjustments are combined under locus-level inference (wild cluster bootstrap p = 0.11), and averages zero within loci (random-effects β = −0.0003, p = 0.90). The prediction is therefore not supported at the variant level in these data, which bound the effect a genome-wide test should expect. The argument is not that the genome "is" a program, but that treating it as one supplies formal tools whose predictions can be checked.

selected_papers.abstract_full: The effectiveness of genomic prediction in forest trees is often constrained by genotype-by-environment (G×E) interactions, particularly when predicting performance in environments not represented in the training population. We evaluated the integration of genomic, enviromic (climatic and soil), and metabolomic (targeted monoterpene) information within multi-environment single-step genomic best linear unbiased prediction (ssGBLUP) reaction norm models to improve prediction in unobserved environments. Models incorporated environmental covariates (W) and genotype-specific responses using linear and nonlinear kernels, including Gaussian and Arc-Cosine formulations. The study examined 12 traits measured on 11,124 trees across four lodgepole pine progeny trials, with 1,490 trees genotyped with 25,099 SNPs. Predictive performance was assessed using leave-one-environment-out cross-validation. Additive genetic correlations among environments revealed substantial G×E for early-growth traits and drought-related decline, with correlations frequently below 0.65. Inclusion of environmental covariates reduced variance attributed to site effects, indicating that these descriptors captured environmental heterogeneity. Incorporating G×E and genotype-by-environmental covariate (G×W) interactions improved model performance, increasing explained phenotypic variance by up to 29.58% and reducing residual variance by up to 3.13% relative to baseline models. Across traits, G×E explained more phenotypic variation than G×W, contributing on average 2.31% and 0.60%, respectively. Predictive ability was high across models (0.688-0.701), with gains of up to 7.85% when nonlinear kernels were combined with metabolomic covariates, particularly for traits exhibiting stronger G×E. Monoterpene profiles yielded predictive performance comparable to climate and soil descriptors, highlighting the potential of integrating genomic, enviromic, and metabolomic information to improve prediction across environments and support climate-resilient forest tree breeding and deployment.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: There is a lack of effective molecular biomarkers for the early identification of the risk of cardiac arrest. Mitochondrial dysfunction is widely recognised as being involved in the pathophysiological process of cardiac arrest, but the upstream epigenetic regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. This study takes DNA methylation as its central focus. By systematically evaluating the genetic associations between methylation quantitative trait loci (mQTLs) in mitochondrial genes and the risk of cardiac arrest, and by tracking downstream changes in gene expression and protein abundance, the study aims to explore potential regulatory pathways linking epigenetic variations to molecular phenotypes and ultimately to disease. METHODS: The study utilised mitochondrial genes from MitoCarta 3.0, obtaining corresponding methylation quantitative trait loci (mQTL) from GoDMC, gene expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) from eQTLGen and GTEx, and protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) from UKB-PPP and deCODE. These were used as instrumental variables for Mendelian randomisation (MR), summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) and colocalisation analysis, to systematically screen for multi-omics genetic signals in mitochondrial genes associated with cardiac arrest (from FinnGen). Based on the analysis results, multi-omics evidence was categorised, and single-cell expression profiles and machine learning models were utilised to perform functional annotation and assess the discriminatory power of candidate genes. RESULTS: The analysis identified five mitochondrial genes with a directional genetic association with cardiac arrest: GATM, GRHPR, NDUFS6, PMAIP1 and AGXT. Among these, the cg10760299 locus of GATM was negatively associated with the risk of cardiac arrest (OR = 0.875, 95% CI 0.832-0.921, p < 0.001), whilst gene expression (OR = 1.396, 95% CI 1.194-1.633, p = 0.005) and protein abundance (OR = 1.513, 95% CI 1.228-1.863, p = 0.015) were positively associated with the risk of cardiac arrest. Single-cell expression profiles indicated that key genes exhibited expression differences between cardiomyocytes and fibroblasts, whilst integrated learning models suggested that these key genes possess potential for disease discrimination. CONCLUSION: Through multi-omics integration analysis, this study identified association signals between methylation sites such as GATM/cg10760299 and the risk of cardiac arrest, providing new candidate targets for research into epigenetic biomarkers of cardiac arrest.

selected_papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: Delivery >39 weeks' gestation is recommended for fetuses with congenital heart disease (FCHD). However, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), maternal diabetes and fetal growth restriction (FGR) are more common in these pregnancies and often necessitate early delivery. We evaluated indications for delivery at <39 weeks and examined maternal covariates, cardiac diagnoses and placental pathology. STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective observational study included maternal-fetal dyads with prenatally diagnosed, structurally isolated, genetically unremarkable FCHD delivered at a single center. Gestational age and delivery indication were obtained from medical record. Placental pathology was assessed using Amsterdam criteria. Regression models evaluated associations with gestational age and neonatal mortality. RESULTS: 46.3% (99/214) delivered <39 weeks; 65.6% (65/99) were due to maternal or fetal compromise, and 34.3% (33/99) to obstetric indications. HDP (20.1%) was strongly associated with <39-week delivery (32.3% vs 9.6%, p<0.001) and the greatest reduction in gestational age (-2.31 weeks, p<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified preeclampsia, type 2 diabetes, lower birthweight Z-score, and race as independent predictors of earlier delivery (p<0.05). Neonatal mortality was higher with maternal/fetal indications (15.7%) versus obstetric (5.4%) or elective FCHD delivery (5.6%) (p=0.02). CONCLUSION: Nearly half of FCHD infants delivered before 39 weeks, largely due to maternal and placental disease, underscoring the importance of placental health in this population.

selected_papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: To explore the clinical information and genetic characteristics of a child with Genitopatellar syndrome (GPS) and summarize relevant findings through a literature review. METHODS: A child with GPS diagnosed at the Department of Neonatology of Taizhou Hospital in Zhejiang Province in February 2024 was selected as study subject. Clinical data were collected, and trio Whole-exome sequencing (trio-WES) was carried out. Based on guidelines from the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG), the pathogenicity of candidate variant was assessed. Amino acid conservation was analyzed using MEGA, and three-dimensional structures of the wild-type and mutant proteins were predicted and compared using AlphaFold3 and PyMOL. A retrospective analysis was also conducted by searching the PubMed, Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) databases for case reports or studies of genetically confirmed GPS. This study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of the hospital (Ethics No.: L2024-10-06-01). RESULTS: The patient, a one-day-old male, had presented with genital abnormalities, clubfoot, polycystic kidneys, atrial septal defect, and agenesis of corpus callosum. Increased nuchal translucency and cervical lymphatic hygroma were detected during the first trimester of pregnancy. Trio-WES results revealed that he has harbored a de novo heterozygous c.3696del (p.Glu1233LysfsTer10) frameshift variant in exon 18 of the KAT6B gene (NM_012330.4). The variant was previously unreported, and its frequency in the general East Asian population has not been documented. Based on the ACMG guidelines, the variant was classified as likely pathogenic (evidence criteria including PS, PM, and PP). Protein homologous sequence alignment analysis suggested the variant site to be highly conserved across multiple species. Homology modeling and structural comparison further revealed varying degrees of change in the hydrogen bonding of amino acids adjacent to the variant site and in the two- and three-dimensional structures of the protein. Literature review has identified 19 patients, with the study cohort comprising 16 survivors (10 males, 6 females) and 3 non-survivors (1 male, 2 females). All patients exhibited varying degrees of genital anomalies, facial dysmorphism, corpus callosum dysgenesis, and flexion contractures of the hips and knees (19/19, 100.0%). Developmental delay/intellectual disability was observed in 17 patients (17/19, 89.5%), hydronephrosis/multiple renal cysts in 16 patients (16/19, 84.2%), patellar hypoplasia in 15 patients (15/19, 78.9%), congenital heart disease in 13 patients (13/19, 68.4%), and prenatal abnormalities were detected in 8 patients (8/19, 42.1%). Current management of the disease is primarily supportive and symptomatic, with the most effective measures including oxygen therapy, gastrostomy tube feeding support, and joint corrective surgeries. CONCLUSION: The c.3696del (p.Glu1233LysfsTer10) variant of the KAT6B gene probably underlay the pathogenesis of GPS in this child. Above finding has expanded the genotypic and phenotypic spectra of this syndrome. GPS may present with increased nuchal translucency accompanied by cystic hygroma during the first trimester. Additionally, the literature review in this study has systematically summarized the prenatal and postnatal phenotypic features, poor prognosis, and current clinical interventions for GPS, which may provide more robust evidence-based support for clinical diagnosis, treatment strategy selection, and prognostic evaluation.

selected_papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Chromosome 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) is a common multisystem genomic disorder with marked phenotypic variability and diagnostic delay. Data on diagnostic pathways and specialist involvement in Eastern Europe remain limited. We aimed to characterize diagnostic pathways and clinical triggers, assess specialist involvement and follow-up, and identify factors associated with diagnosis before or after 1 year of age in a Ukrainian cohort. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter observational study of patients with 22q11.2DS registered in the Ukrainian National Registry of Primary Immunodeficiencies. Clinical manifestations, diagnostic triggers, specialists involved in diagnosis and follow-up, immunological findings, and age at diagnosis were analyzed. RESULTS: The cohort included 126 patients, with a median age of 12 years (range, 0.1-39 years) and median age at diagnosis of 1.0 year (range, 0.1-18 years). Among 120 patients with available diagnostic timing, 63 (52.5%) were diagnosed within the first year, including the two antenatal cases. Congenital heart disease (CHD) was the most frequent major manifestation (74/89, 83.1%), followed by craniofacial dysmorphism (62/74, 83.8%), thymic hypoplasia (54/65, 83.1%), developmental delay (46/62, 74.2%), and recurrent infections (44/65, 67.7%). Among 83 patients with documented diagnostic triggers, CHD was the most frequent (61/83, 73.5%). Developmental delay was more frequent among patients diagnosed after 1 year than within the first year (22.9% vs. 4.4%, p = 0.0135). Immunodeficiency was a diagnostic trigger in 10/83 patients (12.0%), despite T-cell lymphopenia in 31/59 (52.5%). Immunologists and geneticists were most frequently involved in diagnosis. Cardiothoracic surgeons and cardiologists were more frequently involved among patients diagnosed within the first year than after 1 year (27.9% vs. 9.1%, p = 0.0411). Among 13 patients diagnosed after implementation of TREC/KREC newborn screening, two were identified following an abnormal screening result. CONCLUSIONS: In this Ukrainian cohort, 22q11.2DS diagnosis was predominantly phenotype-driven, with CHD representing the principal diagnostic trigger. Developmental delay was associated with diagnosis after 1 year, whereas immunological abnormalities relatively infrequently initiated diagnostic evaluation. Broader recognition of non-cardiac presentations, standardized referral criteria, coordinated multidisciplinary care, and continued development of newborn and prenatal screening may improve timely diagnosis of 22q11.2DS in Ukraine.

selected_papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: Adults with childhood-onset conditions are increasingly admitted to children's hospitals, yet many pediatric systems lack the infrastructure and expertise to manage adult-related medical needs. One approach to bridge this gap is the use of an adult medicine consult service. We aim to describe the demographics, clinical complexity, and consultation patterns of patients admitted to a freestanding children's hospital and evaluated by an adult medicine consult service, which is a current gap in the literature. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective descriptive cohort study was performed of admitted patients with a Hospital Medicine Adult Care (HMAC) service consult from July 2014 through June 2023. RESULTS: Annual adult admissions increased over the study period, from 7.4% to 10.2% of all admissions. HMAC consulted on 1666 admissions for 1008 unique patients (median age, 27 years [range, 14-71 years]). The most frequent reasons for consult were venous thromboembolism prophylaxis (33.7%), age older than 25 years (21.2%), transition of care (7.6%), and hypertension (7.6%). HMAC physicians addressed a mean of 5.5 diagnoses per encounter. Patients averaged 3.6 admissions (range, 1-22) and 4.9 comorbidities (range, 0-21) each. The most common comorbidities were technology dependence (47%), solid tumor malignancy (22.5%), genetic conditions (20.2%), epilepsy (19.7%), congenital heart disease (17.4%), and cerebral palsy (15.7%). selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), a major contributor to heart failure (HF), is characterized by ventricular dilation, impaired systolic and diastolic function, arrhythmias, and adverse cardiac remodeling. While genetic causes of DCM have been extensively investigated, non-genetic and acquired forms of DCM-like HF remain less well understood, particularly regarding regulation by non-coding RNAs. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are stable, covalently closed RNAs that regulate cellular processes through interactions with microRNAs, RNA-binding proteins, and translational machinery; however, their role in non-genetic DCM-like HF is largely unexplored. METHODS: We developed K9HeartCircDB ( https://www.k9heartcircdb.com/ ), a publicly accessible database of circRNAs identified in canine left ventricular (LV) tissues. The dataset includes samples from tachypacing-induced HF, a model of non-genetic DCM-like disease, and healthy controls. CircRNAs were annotated and integrated into a user-friendly platform that enables queries based on exon composition, predicted microRNA binding sites, protein-coding potential, siRNA targets, and primer design for validation. RESULTS: K9HeartCircDB provides a comprehensive catalog of circRNAs expressed in canine LV tissues under both HF and control conditions. The platform offers multiple analytical features, including circRNA annotation, predicted regulatory interactions, and experimental design support. Comparative exploration of circRNA profiles between tachypacing-induced HF and normal tissues enables identification of candidate molecules associated with non-genetic DCM-like pathology. CONCLUSIONS: K9HeartCircDB represents an integrated and accessible resource for studying circRNA biology in canine HF. By facilitating exploration of circRNA expression and function in a translationally relevant large-animal model, this database supports mechanistic investigations and advances research into non-genetic DCM-like disease.

The platform offers multiple analytical features, including circRNA annotation, predicted regulatory interactions, and experimental design support.
Comparative exploration of circRNA profiles between tachypacing-induced HF and normal tissues enables identification of candidate molecules associated with non-genetic DCM-like pathology.

selected_papers.abstract_full: ABSTRACT  Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and ischemic heart disease (IHD) are leading causes of heart failure, yet isoform-level changes in the failing heart remain poorly defined because reference annotations are derived largely from healthy tissues and short-read sequencing cannot reliably reconstruct full-length transcripts. We sequenced six human left ventricles (non-failing, DCM, and IHD; n = 2 each) with PacBio HiFi long reads and curated 48,232 isoforms across 11,760 genes, including 15,535 novel NIC and NNC isoforms. Independent evidence supported most novel structures: 81.7% of isoforms with novel splice junctions had short-read support for all novel junctions, and a cardiac CAGE atlas supported the 5′ ends of 93% of NIC and 86% of NNC isoforms. Novel isoform diversification was concentrated in sarcomere genes and persisted after accounting for gene complexity, expression, sequencing depth, and transcript length. We then augmented GENCODE v43 with 18,637 non-FSM long-read isoforms and re-quantified two independent short-read cohorts (MAGNet and GSE116250). For most genes carrying a transcript that changed more than 2-fold in DCM, the gene itself changed less than 2-fold, so these changes are not apparent at the gene level. Of 626 transcripts differentially expressed in both cohorts, 98% changed in the same direction, including all 100 long-read isoforms among them. The resource is available through CardioIsoMap, an interactive isoform-centric portal (  https://cardioisomap.streamlit.app/ ). This study provides a comprehensive isoform-resolved reference of the human heart in health and disease.

selected_papers.abstract_full: AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)]-lowering therapies are being investigated to reduce atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. However, their implications on women's reproductive health are unknown, and pre-clinical models offer limited insight towards understanding such effects. We evaluated potential causal effects of genetically proxied Lp(a) lowering on reproductive and offspring health outcomes. METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed common and rare variants in the LPA region using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), genetic risk scores (GRSs), and gene-based tests. Additionally, performing individual-level analyses using UK Biobank and All of Us cohorts, with genome sequencing linked to biomarkers and electronic health records, we investigated outcomes spanning maternal health during pregnancy, labour and delivery complications, pregnancy outcomes, and congenital malformations in 236 228 UK Biobank and 122 038 All of Us women and recorded female infertility in 102 549 All of Us women. In summary-level analyses, no significant adverse associations of genetically predicted low Lp(a) with reproductive and offspring health outcomes were detected. Nominal associations were present across MR, GRS, and gene-based analyses, but no adverse reproductive findings survived the multiple-testing corrections. Confidence intervals for all fertility and reproductive-count estimates included the null. Controls showed expected associations for higher Lp(a) with LDL cholesterol (P = 2 × 10-19) and triglycerides (P = 4 × 10-9). CONCLUSION: In summary, we found no robust or multiplicity-adjusted evidence of adverse reproductive or offspring health effects related to genetically proxied Lp(a) lowering. These findings provide genetic evidence relevant to assessing the reproductive and offspring health implications of targeting Lp(a).

selected_papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Taxanes are standard chemotherapeutic agents for breast cancer, yet their clinical utility is often limited by severe multi-organ adverse drug reactions (ADRs), which show marked inter-individual variability. METHODS: To investigate the genetic basis of this variability, we performed whole-exome sequencing (WES) in 203 breast cancer patients receiving taxane-based chemotherapy and assessed five ADR phenotypes-neutropenia, leukopenia, rash, peripheral neurotoxicity, and gastrointestinal toxicity. Common variants were tested via single-variant association tests, and rare variants via gene-based burden tests (SKAT-O). RESULTS: In common-variant analysis, PTGES rs2302821 showed a significant association with neutropenia (joint genotype test P = 5.57 × 10-6; adjusted P = 2.19 × 10-6), with the AC genotype conferring a protective effect (adjusted OR = 0.17, 95% CI: 0.08-0.35). For rash, rare-variant gene-based analysis nominated GSDMA as a candidate (P = 2.88 × 10-7). GSDMA exhibited skin-specific expression, and missense variants were exclusively observed in affected cases; however, these results remain exploratory given the limited number of rash cases (n = 12). A common-variant signal in IL36B was nominally significant in unadjusted analysis but attenuated after covariate adjustment, warranting further validation. DISCUSSION: Our findings identify PTGES rs2302821 as a potential genetic marker for taxane-induced neutropenia and nominate GSDMA as a preliminary candidate for rash susceptibility, providing a genomic perspective on inter-individual variability in taxane-related ADRs.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Genetic causes are identified in up to 15% of Parkinson's disease (PD) patients; the remaining idiopathic PD (iPD) patients are attributed to polygenic risk, environmental and lifestyle factors, and interactions thereof. We applied five advanced polygenic score (PGS) tools to data from 1762 iPD patients and 4227 healthy controls of European ancestry. 5-fold cross-validation revealed a significant boost in the discriminative power of modern Bayesian methods over simpler approaches, leading to the development of a novel iPD-PGS. This score demonstrated significantly improved performance compared to existing scores, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.680 (95% confidence interval (-CI):[0.665, 0.695]). External validation confirmed its robustness. Early-onset iPD patients exhibited higher PGS values than late-onset iPD patients and healthy controls, indicating increased polygenetic burden. Applying our novel iPD-PGS to carriers of heterozygous PRKN variants and GBA1 coding risk variants suggested that penetrance in these groups is partly explained by the same polygenic alterations as observed mitigating iPD. GBA1 showed a trend toward higher discriminative potential than PRKN (GBA1: AUC = 0.639, 95%-CI:[0.590, 0.687]; PRKN: AUC = 0.594, 95%-CI:[0.501, 0.687]), though confidence intervals overlapped. Our study highlights the potential of advanced PGSs in PD research, particularly in identifying high-risk individuals and modifying risk in rare-variant carriers.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Moyamoya angiopathy (MMA) is a rare steno-occlusive condition resulting in transient ischemic attacks and strokes in children and adults. Previous studies, mainly in adult patients, suggested RNF213 as the most prevalent susceptibility gene due to an Asian founder variant. Nevertheless, the genetic landscape in early-onset European MMA patients requires further elucidation. Exome-sequencing was performed in 104 pediatric MMA patients, including three with Down syndrome, and 520 healthy controls. Rare-variant enrichment testing was performed using the R-package SKAT on the whole cohort as well as in a 100% European subset, revealing a total of 28 enriched genes. Both tests showed the most common known MMA genes (RNF213 and NF1) among the top three enriched genes, underlining the validity of our approach. Seven of the concordantly enriched genes are novel MMA candidates (ATAD2, COL18A1, NAV1, ALOX12B, KRTAP4-7, KCNJ12, and KBTBD13). De novo variants were found in NF1, RNF213, COL18A1, ECI1, and YIPF1. In summary, our study confirms RNF213 and NF1 as major susceptibility genes and suggests seven novel early-onset MMA susceptibility genes. Of special interest is the novel candidate gene COL18A1, which is involved in angiogenesis and endothelial cell proliferation, due to its potential additional role as a modifier of MMA in trisomy 21.

selected_papers.abstract: Background:  Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a clinically and genetically heterogenous neurodegenerative disorder in which both monogenic and complex genetic mechanism contribute to disease susceptibility. Increasing evidence also indicates that non motor manifestations, including sleep disturbances, significantly influence disease burden. selected_papers.abstract_full: Background:  Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a clinically and genetically heterogenous neurodegenerative disorder in which both monogenic and complex genetic mechanism contribute to disease susceptibility. Increasing evidence also indicates that non motor manifestations, including sleep disturbances, significantly influence disease burden. This study aimed to characterize the genetic spectrum of ALS in a predominantly North Indian cohort while evaluating the prevalence of sleep related abnormalities. Methods: Seventy-three clinically diagnosed ALS patients were recruited from a tertiary care centre in North India. Disease severity was assessed using the ALSFRS-R. Sleep quality, daytime sleepiness, and REM sleep behaviour disorder symptoms were evaluated using the PSQI, ESS and RBDQ questionnaires, respectively. Genetic analysis included targeted sequencing of SOD1, TARDBP, and ANG, followed by repeat expansion analysis of C9orf72, ATXN1, ATXN2, ATXN3, and ATXN7. Whole exome sequencing was performed in selected cases to further investigate the genetic basis of ALS. Results: The cohort demonstrated a male predominance and an earlier age of onset compared to many Western populations. Poor sleep quality and excessive daytime sleepiness were frequently observed although no significant association was found between sleep parameters and disease severity. Genetic screening identified a pathogenic/likely pathogenic TARDBP variant classified by ClinVar while no known or novel pathogenic variants were detected in SOD1 or ANG. Repeat expansion studies revealed one patient harbouring pathogenic C9orf72 repeat expansions. For the ATXN1, one patient harboured pathogenic repeat expansions and two patients carried intermediate length repeats. Additionally, one patient harboured intermediate repeat expansions in ATXN2. Whole exome sequencing revealed novel and rare variants in ALS associated genes including ANXA11, SIGMAR1, SETX, ERBB4 and NEK1, highlighting substantial genetic heterogeneity. Conclusions: Our findings highlight the complex genetic heterogeneity of ALS, with pathogenic repeat expansions and rare variants identified across multiple disease associated genes. These results demonstrate the importance of comprehensive genetic testing to improve the detection of clinically relevant variants in ALS. In addition, the high prevalence of sleep related disturbances observed in the cohort emphasizes the need to incorporate non motor assessment into routine clinical evaluation of patients with ALS.

Poor sleep quality and excessive daytime sleepiness were frequently observed although no significant association was found between sleep parameters and disease severity.
Genetic screening identified a pathogenic/likely pathogenic TARDBP variant classified by ClinVar while no known or novel pathogenic variants were detected in SOD1 or ANG.

selected_papers.abstract: Rare alleles arise from mutations on an existing haplotype background, yet current gene-based rare variant association tests treat low-frequency coding variants as effects independent of the common regulatory variants that surround them. selected_papers.abstract_full: Rare alleles arise from mutations on an existing haplotype background, yet current gene-based rare variant association tests treat low-frequency coding variants as effects independent of the common regulatory variants that surround them. The penetrance of rare coding variants can be modulated by the cis-regulatory landscape, and failing to account for this context limits the statistical power of existing methods for complex traits. We present PrediXSKAT, a kernel-based rare variant association framework that incorporates the surrounding cis-regulatory landscape by estimating its impact on gene expression via PrediXcan. PrediXSKAT embeds predicted gene expression directly into the Sequence Kernel Association Test kernel through element-wise similarity weighting, concentrating rare variant signal among individuals who share concordant genetic and regulatory backgrounds. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that PrediXSKAT increases power over standard kernel-based testing under biologically realistic conditions where a proportion of tested variants carry small, mixed-direction effects. Type I error rates are controlled in the absence of association. Power gains persist across a range of sample sizes and causal variant architectures. Applied to whole-genome sequencing data from the Alzheimer’s Disease Sequencing Project, PrediXSKAT recapitulates established disease loci and amplifies signals at previously unreported candidate genes without indiscriminately inflating genome-wide results. PrediXSKAT provides a generalizable and extensible framework for the joint analysis of common regulatory and rare coding variants. The approach can be applied to any kernel-based set test and extended to jointly consider multiple genes within the same biological pathway, offering a principled strategy for improving rare variant discovery in large-scale sequencing studies of complex disease.
